तावदाकाशगा वाणी सहसा देवनिर्मिता ..
अटताराजमार्गेण विप्रेणानेन वै यतः .. 6.128.50 ..
5.127.m: just then, a voice moving in the sky suddenly was uttered by a god: / 'Because on the royal road while wandering (aṭatā) by this brahmin,

5.127.s:
utpāditastu putro'yamautsukyādbrāhmaṇena tu ..
aṭākhyo bhūpatistasmālloke khyāto bhaviṣyati .. 51 ..
5.127.d:
उत्पादितस्तु पुत्रोऽयमौत्सुक्याद्ब्राह्मणेन तु ..
अटाख्यो भूपतिस्तस्माल्लोके ख्यातो भविष्यति .. 51 ..
5.127.m: this son was generated out of eagerness by the brahmin, / therefore this king shall be renowned in the world by the name Aṭa.

5.127.s:
dīrghāyurbahuputraśca śatruṃpakṣakṣayāvahaḥ ..
etasmātkāraṇādviprā aṭākhyaḥ sa babhūva ha .. 52 ..
5.127.d:
दीर्घायुर्बहुपुत्रश्च शत्रुंपक्षक्षयावहः ..
एतस्मात्कारणाद्विप्रा अटाख्यः स बभूव ह .. 52 ..
5.127.m: He shall be long-lived, have many sons, and bring destruction to the faction of enemies.' / For this reason, O brahmins, he was named Aṭa.

5.127.s:
svavaṃśoddharacaṃdro'tra vāṃchitārthaprado'rthinām ..
tenaitatkṣetramāsādya sthāpitaṃ liṃgamuttamam ..
svanāmnā brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ sarvadeṣṭapradaṃ nṛṇām .. 53 ..
5.127.d:
स्ववंशोद्धरचंद्रोऽत्र वांछितार्थप्रदोऽर्थिनाम् ..
तेनैतत्क्षेत्रमासाद्य स्थापितं लिंगमुत्तमम् ..
स्वनाम्ना ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठाः सर्वदेष्टप्रदं नृणाम् .. 53 ..
5.127.m: Here, a moon delivering his lineage, granting desired objects to seekers, / having reached this sacred field, an excellent liṅga was established by him / in his own name, O best of brahmins, which grants all desires to mortals.

5.127.s:
yastanmāghacaturdaśyāṃ pūjayecchraddhayānvitaḥ ..
na tasya jāyate kiṃcidduḥkhaṃ saṃtānasaṃbhavam .. 54 ..
5.127.d:
यस्तन्माघचतुर्दश्यां पूजयेच्छ्रद्धयान्वितः ..
न तस्य जायते किंचिद्दुःखं संतानसंभवम् .. 54 ..
5.127.m: Whoever worships it with faith on the fourteenth day of Māgha, / no sorrow arising from offspring ever occurs to him.

5.127.s:
api varṣaśatānārī snātvā kuṇḍe sutaprade ..
aṭeśvaraṃ tataḥ paśyecchivabhaktiparāyaṇā .. 55 ..
5.127.d:
अपि वर्षशतानारी स्नात्वा कुण्डे सुतप्रदे ..
अटेश्वरं ततः पश्येच्छिवभक्तिपरायणा .. 55 ..
5.127.m: Even a woman hundred years old, having bathed in the son-granting pool / and then beholding Aṭeśvara, devoted to the worship of Śiva,

5.127.s: sadyaḥ putramavāpnoti vaṃśavṛddhikaraṃ param .. tatprasādānna saṃdehaḥ kārtikeya vaco yathā .. 56 ..
5.127.d: सद्यः पुत्रमवाप्नोति वंशवृद्धिकरं परम् .. तत्प्रसादान्न संदेहः कार्तिकेय वचो यथा .. 56 ..
5.127.m: quickly obtains a son who will supremely expand the lineage / through his grace; there is no doubt, just as spoken by Kārtikeya.

5.127.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye'ṭeśvarotpattimāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāmāṣṭāviṃśatyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 128 ..
5.127.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्येऽटेश्वरोत्पत्तिमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनामाष्टाविंशत्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 128 ..
5.127.m: Thus ends the one hundred twenty-eighth chapter, named 'Description of the Origin and Māhātmya of Aṭeśvara', in the māhātmya of the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth section in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.128.s:
.. sūta uvāca ..
tathānyo'pi ca tatrāsti yājñavalkyasamudravaḥ ..
āśramo loka vikhyāto mūrkhāṇāmapi siddhidaḥ .. 1 ..
5.128.d:
.. सूत उवाच ..
तथान्योऽपि च तत्रास्ति याज्ञवल्क्यसमुद्रवः ..
आश्रमो लोक विख्यातो मूर्खाणामपि सिद्धिदः .. 1 ..
5.128.m: Sūta said: / Likewise, there is also another hermitage there, originating from Yājñavalkya, / world-renowned, granting accomplishment even to fools,

5.128.s:
yatra taptvā tapastīvraṃ yājñavalkyena dhīmatā ..
saṃprāptā nikhilā vedā guruṇā'pahṛtāśca ye .. 2 ..
5.128.d:
यत्र तप्त्वा तपस्तीव्रं याज्ञवल्क्येन धीमता ..
संप्राप्ता निखिला वेदा गुरुणाऽपहृताश्च ये .. 2 ..
5.128.m: where, having performed severe austerity, the wise Yājñavalkya / obtained all the Vedas that had been taken away by his guru.

5.128.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
ko'sau gururabhūttasya yājñavalkyasya dhīmataḥ ..
pāṭhayitvā punaryena hṛtā vedā mahātmanā .. 3 ..
5.128.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
कोऽसौ गुरुरभूत्तस्य याज्ञवल्क्यस्य धीमतः ..
पाठयित्वा पुनर्येन हृता वेदा महात्मना .. 3 ..
5.128.m: The seers said: / Who was that guru of the wise Yājñavalkya, / by which great soul the Vedas, having been taught, were taken back again?

5.128.s:
kimarthaṃ ca samācakṣva sūtaputrātra vistarāt..
kautukaṃ paramaṃ jātaṃ sarveṣāṃ no dvijanmanām .. 4 ..
5.128.d:
किमर्थं च समाचक्ष्व सूतपुत्रात्र विस्तरात्..
कौतुकं परमं जातं सर्वेषां नो द्विजन्मनाम् .. 4 ..
5.128.m: And for what reason? Explain it in detail here, O son of Sūta; / supreme curiosity has arisen in all of us twice-born.

5.128.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
āsīdbrāhmaṇaśārdūlaḥ śākalya iti viśrutaḥ..
bhārgavānvayasaṃbhūto veda vedāṃgapāragaḥ .. 5 ..
5.128.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
आसीद्ब्राह्मणशार्दूलः शाकल्य इति विश्रुतः..
भार्गवान्वयसंभूतो वेद वेदांगपारगः .. 5 ..
5.128.m: Sūta said: / There was a tiger among brahmins, celebrated as Śākalya, / born in the lineage of Bhṛgu, fully versed in the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.

5.128.s:
bṛhatkalpe purā viprā vardhamāne purottame ..
bahuśiṣyasamāyukto vedādhyayanatatparaḥ .. 6 ..
5.128.d:
बृहत्कल्पे पुरा विप्रा वर्धमाने पुरोत्तमे ..
बहुशिष्यसमायुक्तो वेदाध्ययनतत्परः .. 6 ..
5.128.m: Formerly, in the Bṛhatkalpa, O brahmins, in the excellent city of Vardhamāna, / endowed with many pupils, he was devoted to the study of the Vedas.

5.128.s:
sa sadā prātarutthāya vidyādānaṃ prayacchati .
śiṣyebhyaścānurūpebhyaḥ prasādādvijasattamāḥ .. 7 ..
5.128.d:
स सदा प्रातरुत्थाय विद्यादानं प्रयच्छति .
शिष्येभ्यश्चानुरूपेभ्यः प्रसादाद्विजसत्तमाः .. 7 ..
5.128.m: Having risen in the morning, he always imparted knowledge / to worthy pupils out of favor, O best of the twice-born.

5.128.s:
cakāra sa tadā viprāḥ paurohityaṃ mahīpateḥ ..
sūryavaṃśaprasūtasya supriyasya mahātmanaḥ .. .. 8 ..
5.128.d:
चकार स तदा विप्राः पौरोहित्यं महीपतेः ..
सूर्यवंशप्रसूतस्य सुप्रियस्य महात्मनः .. .. 8 ..
5.128.m: At that time, O brahmins, he performed the priestly duties for the king / named Supriya, the great soul born in the solar dynasty.

5.128.s:
sa tasya dharmakṛtyāni sarvāṇyeva dinedine ..
kṛtvā svagṛhamabhyeti pūjitastena bhūbhujā .. 9 ..
5.128.d:
स तस्य धर्मकृत्यानि सर्वाण्येव दिनेदिने ..
कृत्वा स्वगृहमभ्येति पूजितस्तेन भूभुजा .. 9 ..
5.128.m: Every day, having performed all his religious duties, / he would return to his own house, honored by that king,

5.128.s:
ekaṃ śiṣyaṃ samāropya śāṃtyarthaṃ tasya bhūpateḥ ..
kathayitvā pramāṇaṃ ca vidhānaṃ homasaṃbhavam .. 6.129.10 ..
5.128.d:
एकं शिष्यं समारोप्य शांत्यर्थं तस्य भूपतेः ..
कथयित्वा प्रमाणं च विधानं होमसंभवम् .. 6.129.10 ..
5.128.m: having appointed a single disciple for that king's rites of pacification, / having explained the measure and the procedure pertaining to the oblation.

5.128.s:
śiṣyo'pi sakalaṃ kṛtvā tatkarma susamāhitaḥ ..
āśīrvādaṃ pradattvā ca bhūpatergṛhameti ca .. 11 ..
5.128.d:
शिष्योऽपि सकलं कृत्वा तत्कर्म सुसमाहितः ..
आशीर्वादं प्रदत्त्वा च भूपतेर्गृहमेति च .. 11 ..
5.128.m: The disciple also, having performed that entire rite with great concentration / and having bestowed a blessing upon the king, would return home.

5.128.s:
evaṃ prakurvatastasya śākalyasya mahātmanaḥ ..
paurohityaṃ gataḥ kālaḥ kiyanmātro dvijottamāḥ .. 12 .
5.128.d:
एवं प्रकुर्वतस्तस्य शाकल्यस्य महात्मनः ..
पौरोहित्यं गतः कालः कियन्मात्रो द्विजोत्तमाः .. 12 .
5.128.m: While the noble Śākalya was thus performing / the priestly office, O best of the twice-born, some time passed.

5.128.s:
tadā vaivāhike kāle śapto yaḥ śaṃbhunā svayam ..
suniṃdyāṃ vikṛtiṃ dṛṣṭvā tasya vedyāṃ gatasya ca .. 13 ..
5.128.d:
तदा वैवाहिके काले शप्तो यः शंभुना स्वयम् ..
सुनिंद्यां विकृतिं दृष्ट्वा तस्य वेद्यां गतस्य च .. 13 ..
5.128.m: Then, at the time of a wedding, [the king] who had been cursed by Śambhu himself, / seeing his very contemptible disfigurement as he went to the sacrificial altar,

5.128.s:
atha taṃ yojayāmāsa śāṃtyarthaṃ nṛpamaṃdire ..
yājñavalkyaṃ sa śākalyaḥ pratipadyāgataṃ tadā .. 14 ..
5.128.d:
अथ तं योजयामास शांत्यर्थं नृपमंदिरे ..
याज्ञवल्क्यं स शाकल्यः प्रतिपद्यागतं तदा .. 14 ..
5.128.m: then for rites of pacification in the king's palace, that Śākalya / directed Yājñavalkya, who had arrived on that occasion.

5.128.s:
so'pi tāruṇyagarveṇa veśyākarajavikṣataḥ ..
sarvāṃgeṣu sunirlajjaḥ prakaṭāṃgo jagāma vai .. 15 ..
5.128.d:
सोऽपि तारुण्यगर्वेण वेश्याकरजविक्षतः ..
सर्वांगेषु सुनिर्लज्जः प्रकटांगो जगाम वै .. 15 ..
5.128.m: He too, out of pride of youth, wounded by the fingernails of a courtesan / all over his limbs, shameless, went indeed with his body bare.

5.128.s:
tataśca śāṃtikaṃ kṛtvā japāṃte bhūpatiṃ ca tam ..
śāṃtodakapradānāya hasyamāno janairyayau .. 16 ..
5.128.d:
ततश्च शांतिकं कृत्वा जपांते भूपतिं च तम् ..
शांतोदकप्रदानाय हस्यमानो जनैर्ययौ .. 16 ..
5.128.m: Then, having performed the pacification rite, at the end of the recitation / he approached the king to give the sanctified water, being mocked by the people.

5.128.s:
pārthivo'pi ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛgrūpaṃ viṭaṃ dvijam ..
nāśīrjagrāha tenoktāṃ vākyametaduvāca ha .. 17 .
5.128.d:
पार्थिवोऽपि च तं दृष्ट्वा तादृग्रूपं विटं द्विजम् ..
नाशीर्जग्राह तेनोक्तां वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह .. 17 .
5.128.m: The king, too, seeing him, a twice-born of such form, a gallant, / did not accept the blessing spoken by him, and spoke this sentence:

5.128.s:
ucchiṣṭo'haṃ dvijaśreṣṭha śayyārūḍho vyavasthitaḥ .
atra śālodbhave staṃbhe tasmādetajjalaṃ kṣipa .. 18 ..
5.128.d:
उच्छिष्टोऽहं द्विजश्रेष्ठ शय्यारूढो व्यवस्थितः .
अत्र शालोद्भवे स्तंभे तस्मादेतज्जलं क्षिप .. 18 ..
5.128.m: 'I am impure, O best of the twice-born, remaining mounted on my bed; / therefore, throw this water here onto the pillar made of Śāla wood.'

5.128.s:
so'pi sāvajñamājñāya taṃ bhūpaṃ kupitānanaḥ ..
taṃ ca staṃbhaṃ samuddiśya dhyātvā tadbrahma śāśvatam .. 19 ..
5.128.d:
सोऽपि सावज्ञमाज्ञाय तं भूपं कुपिताननः ..
तं च स्तंभं समुद्दिश्य ध्यात्वा तद्ब्रह्म शाश्वतम् .. 19 ..
5.128.m: He too, realizing that the king was treating him with contempt, his face filled with wrath, / directed [the water] toward that pillar, having meditated upon the eternal Brahman.

5.128.s:
dyāṃ tvamālikhya ityeva proktvā maṃtraṃ ca yājuṣam.. (yāṃ tvamālikhya- pāṭhabhedaḥ)
prākṣipacchāṃtikaṃ toyaṃ tasya mūrdhani satvaram.. 6.129.20 ..
5.128.d:
द्यां त्वमालिख्य इत्येव प्रोक्त्वा मंत्रं च याजुषम्.. (यां त्वमालिख्य- पाठभेदः)
प्राक्षिपच्छांतिकं तोयं तस्य मूर्धनि सत्वरम्.. 6.129.20 ..
5.128.m: Saying 'dyāṃ tvam ālikhya' and reciting this mantra from the Yajurveda, / he quickly poured the pacifying water upon its top.

5.128.s:
tataḥ sa patite toye staṃbhaḥ pallavaśobhitaḥ ..
tatkṣaṇādeva saṃjajñe phala puṣpairvirājitaḥ .. 21 ..
5.128.d:
ततः स पतिते तोये स्तंभः पल्लवशोभितः ..
तत्क्षणादेव संजज्ञे फल पुष्पैर्विराजितः .. 21 ..
5.128.m: Then, as soon as that water fell, that pillar / immediately became adorned with shoots and shone with fruits and flowers.

5.128.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā pārthivaḥ so'tha vismayotphullalocanaḥ ..
paścāttāpaṃ vidhāyātha vākyametaduvāca ha .. 22 ..
5.128.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा पार्थिवः सोऽथ विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचनः ..
पश्चात्तापं विधायाथ वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह .. 22 ..
5.128.m: Seeing that, the king, his eyes wide with astonishment, / felt remorse and spoke these words:

5.128.s:
abhiṣekaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha mamāpi tvaṃ prayaccha bhoḥ ..
anenaiva tu mantreṇa śucitvaṃ me vyavasthitam .. 23 ..
5.128.d:
अभिषेकं द्विजश्रेष्ठ ममापि त्वं प्रयच्छ भोः ..
अनेनैव तु मन्त्रेण शुचित्वं मे व्यवस्थितम् .. 23 ..
5.128.m: "O best of brahmins, bestow an ablution upon me too! / By this very mantra my purity shall be established."

5.128.s:
.. yājñavalkya uvāca .. ..
mamābhiṣekadānasya tvamanarho'si pārthiva ..
tasmādyāsyāmyahaṃ sadyo yatrasthaḥ sa gururmama .. 24 ..
5.128.d:
.. याज्ञवल्क्य उवाच .. ..
ममाभिषेकदानस्य त्वमनर्होऽसि पार्थिव ..
तस्माद्यास्याम्यहं सद्यो यत्रस्थः स गुरुर्मम .. 24 ..
5.128.m: Yājñavalkya said: / "O king, you are unworthy of receiving an ablution from me. / Therefore, I shall at once go to where my guru resides."

5.128.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
tava dāsyāmi vastrāṇi vāhanāni vasūni ca ..
tasmādyacchābhiṣekaṃ me mantreṇā'nena sāṃpratam .. 25 ..
5.128.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
तव दास्यामि वस्त्राणि वाहनानि वसूनि च ..
तस्माद्यच्छाभिषेकं मे मन्त्रेणाऽनेन सांप्रतम् .. 25 ..
5.128.m: The king said: / "I shall give you garments, conveyances, and wealth. / Therefore, bestow the ablution upon me now with this mantra!"

5.128.s:
.. yājñavalkya uvāca .. ..
na homāṃtaṃ vinā mantraḥ sphurate pārthivottama ..
abhiṣekavidhau prokto yaḥ pūrvaṃ padmayoninā ..
tasmānnāhaṃ kariṣyāmi tava yadvai hṛdi sthitam.. 26 ..
5.128.d:
.. याज्ञवल्क्य उवाच .. ..
न होमांतं विना मन्त्रः स्फुरते पार्थिवोत्तम ..
अभिषेकविधौ प्रोक्तो यः पूर्वं पद्मयोनिना ..
तस्मान्नाहं करिष्यामि तव यद्वै हृदि स्थितम्.. 26 ..
5.128.m: Yājñavalkya said: / "A mantra does not take effect without concluding with an oblation, O best of kings, / as was declared anciently by the Lotus-born [Brahmā] in the rite of ablution. / Therefore, I shall not do what is in your heart."

5.128.s:
ityuktvā vacanaṃ bhūpaṃ yājñavalkyaḥ sa vai dvijaḥ ..
jagāma svagṛhaṃ tūrṇaṃ nispṛhatvaṃ samāśritaḥ .. 27
5.128.d:
इत्युक्त्वा वचनं भूपं याज्ञवल्क्यः स वै द्विजः ..
जगाम स्वगृहं तूर्णं निस्पृहत्वं समाश्रितः .. 27
5.128.m: Having spoken these words to the king, that brahmin Yājñavalkya, / relying on desirelessness, went quickly to his own home.

5.128.s:
apare'hni samāyātaṃ śākalyamatha bhūpatiḥ ..
provāca prāṃjalirbhūtvā vinayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ .. 28 ..
5.128.d:
अपरेऽह्नि समायातं शाकल्यमथ भूपतिः ..
प्रोवाच प्रांजलिर्भूत्वा विनयावनतः स्थितः .. 28 ..
5.128.m: On the next day, when Śākalya arrived, the king, / folding his hands and bowing in humility, spoke:

5.128.s:
yastvayā preṣitaḥ kalya śiṣyo brāhmaṇasattamaḥ ..
śāṃtyarthaṃ preṣaṇīyaśca bhūyo'pyevaṃ gṛhe mama .. 29 ..
5.128.d:
यस्त्वया प्रेषितः कल्य शिष्यो ब्राह्मणसत्तमः ..
शांत्यर्थं प्रेषणीयश्च भूयोऽप्येवं गृहे मम .. 29 ..
5.128.m: "That pupil, the best of brahmins, who was sent by you yesterday, / should be sent again to my house for the pacification rite."

5.128.s:
bāḍhamityeva sa proktvā tato gatvā nijālayam ..
yājñavalkyaṃ samāhūya tataḥ provāca sādaram .. 6.129.30 ..
5.128.d:
बाढमित्येव स प्रोक्त्वा ततो गत्वा निजालयम् ..
याज्ञवल्क्यं समाहूय ततः प्रोवाच सादरम् .. 6.129.30 ..
5.128.m: Saying 'So be it,' he went to his own abode, / summoned Yājñavalkya, and spoke to him with respect:

5.128.s:
adyāpi tvaṃ nareṃdrasya śāṃtyarthaṃ bhavane vraja ..
viśeṣātpārthiveṃdreṇa samāhūto'si putraka .. 31 .. ..
5.128.d:
अद्यापि त्वं नरेंद्रस्य शांत्यर्थं भवने व्रज ..
विशेषात्पार्थिवेंद्रेण समाहूतोऽसि पुत्रक .. 31 .. ..
5.128.m: "Go today as well to the king's palace for the pacification rite. / You have been specially invited by the king, my child."

5.128.s:
.. yājñavalkya uvāca .. ..
nāhaṃ tāta gamiṣyāmi śāṃtyarthaṃ tasya maṃdire ..
avalepena yuktasya śuddhyā virahitasya ca .. 32 ..
5.128.d:
.. याज्ञवल्क्य उवाच .. ..
नाहं तात गमिष्यामि शांत्यर्थं तस्य मंदिरे ..
अवलेपेन युक्तस्य शुद्ध्या विरहितस्य च .. 32 ..
5.128.m: Yājñavalkya said: / "Father, I will not go to his mansion for the pacification rite, / for he is filled with arrogance and devoid of purity.

5.128.s:
mayā tasyābhiṣekārthaṃ salilaṃ codyataṃ ca yat ..
salilaṃ tena tatkāṣṭhe samādiṣṭaṃ kubuddhinā .. 33 ..
5.128.d:
मया तस्याभिषेकार्थं सलिलं चोद्यतं च यत् ..
सलिलं तेन तत्काष्ठे समादिष्टं कुबुद्धिना .. 33 ..
5.128.m: The water which was prepared by me for his ablution / was directed by that evil-minded one toward that piece of wood.

5.128.s:
tato mayāpi tatraiva tatkṣaṇātsalilaṃ ca yat ..
tasminkāṣṭhe parikṣiptaṃ nītaṃ vṛddhiṃ ca tatkṣaṇāt .. 34 ..
5.128.d:
ततो मयापि तत्रैव तत्क्षणात्सलिलं च यत् ..
तस्मिन्काष्ठे परिक्षिप्तं नीतं वृद्धिं च तत्क्षणात् .. 34 ..
5.128.m: Then, the water that was immediately thrown by me / right there onto that wood caused it instantly to sprout and grow."

5.128.s:
.. śākalya uvāca .. ..
ata eva viśeṣeṇa samāhūto'si putraka ..
tasmāttatra drutaṃ gaccha nāvajñeyā mahībhujaḥ .. 35 ..
5.128.d:
.. शाकल्य उवाच .. ..
अत एव विशेषेण समाहूतोऽसि पुत्रक ..
तस्मात्तत्र द्रुतं गच्छ नावज्ञेया महीभुजः .. 35 ..
5.128.m: Śākalya said: / "For that very reason you have been specially invited, my child. / Therefore, go there quickly; kings must not be disregarded.

5.128.s:
apamānādbhavenmānaṃ pārthivānāmasaṃśayam ..
yaḥ karoti punastatra mānaṃ na sa bhavetpriyaḥ .. 36 ..
5.128.d:
अपमानाद्भवेन्मानं पार्थिवानामसंशयम् ..
यः करोति पुनस्तत्र मानं न स भवेत्प्रियः .. 36 ..
5.128.m: From disrespect, respect from kings may arise without doubt; / but one who displays pride there will not become dear.

5.128.s:
kopaprasāda vastūni vicinvaṃtīha ye sadā ..
ārohaṃti śanairbhṛtyā dhunvaṃtamapi pārthivam .. 37 ..
5.128.d:
कोपप्रसाद वस्तूनि विचिन्वंतीह ये सदा ..
आरोहंति शनैर्भृत्या धुन्वंतमपि पार्थिवम् .. 37 ..
5.128.m: Servants who constantly observe the causes of anger and favor / gradually win over a king, even when he shakes them off.

5.128.s:
samau mānāpamānau ca cittajñaḥ kālavittathā ..
sarvaṃsahaḥ kṣamī vijñaḥ sa bhavedrājavallabhaḥ .. 38 ..
5.128.d:
समौ मानापमानौ च चित्तज्ञः कालवित्तथा ..
सर्वंसहः क्षमी विज्ञः स भवेद्राजवल्लभः .. 38 ..
5.128.m: He to whom honor and dishonor are equal, who knows the king's mind and knows the right time, / who endures all, is forgiving, and wise—he becomes a king's favorite.

5.128.s:
apamānamanādṛtya tasmādgaccha nṛpālayam ..
mamājñāpi na laṃghyā ta eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ .. 39 ..
5.128.d:
अपमानमनादृत्य तस्माद्गच्छ नृपालयम् ..
ममाज्ञापि न लंघ्या त एष धर्मः सनातनः .. 39 ..
5.128.m: Disregarding disrespect, therefore, go to the king's abode. / Moreover, my command must not be transgressed by you; this is the eternal dharma."

5.128.s:
.. yājñavalkya uvāca .. ..
ājñābhaṃgo dhruvaṃ bhāvī paripāṭīvyatikramāt ..
karoṣi yadi śiṣyāṇāṃ ye tvayā tatra yojitāḥ .. 6.129.40 ..
5.128.d:
.. याज्ञवल्क्य उवाच .. ..
आज्ञाभंगो ध्रुवं भावी परिपाटीव्यतिक्रमात् ..
करोषि यदि शिष्याणां ये त्वया तत्र योजिताः .. 6.129.40 ..
5.128.m: Yājñavalkya said: / "A breach of your command will certainly happen if you transgress the order of turn / regarding the disciples who were assigned there by you.

5.128.s:
tasmādyadi balānmāṃ tvaṃ yojayiṣyasi taṃ prati ..
tvāṃ tyaktvā'nyatra yāsyāmi yataḥ proktaṃ maharṣibhiḥ .. 41 ..
5.128.d:
तस्माद्यदि बलान्मां त्वं योजयिष्यसि तं प्रति ..
त्वां त्यक्त्वाऽन्यत्र यास्यामि यतः प्रोक्तं महर्षिभिः .. 41 ..
5.128.m: Therefore, if you forcibly send me to him, / I will leave you and go elsewhere, for it has been declared by the great seers:

5.128.s:
gurorapyavaliptasya kāryākāryamajānataḥ ..
utpathe vartamānasya parityāgo vidhīyate .. 42 ..
5.128.d:
गुरोरप्यवलिप्तस्य कार्याकार्यमजानतः ..
उत्पथे वर्तमानस्य परित्यागो विधीयते .. 42 ..
5.128.m: 'Abandonment is prescribed even of a guru who is arrogant, / who does not know what ought and ought not to be done, and who walks on the wrong path.'"

5.128.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā śākalyaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ ..
tataḥ provāca taṃ bhūyo bhartsamāno muhurmuhuḥ .. 43 ..
5.128.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा शाकल्यः क्रोधमूर्छितः ..
ततः प्रोवाच तं भूयो भर्त्समानो मुहुर्मुहुः .. 43 ..
5.128.m: Sūta said: / Hearing those words of his, Śākalya, faint with anger, / then spoke to him again, rebuking him repeatedly:

5.128.s:
ekamapyakṣaraṃ yatra guruḥ śiṣye nivedayet ..
pṛthivyāṃ nāsti taddravyaṃ yaddattvā hyanṛṇī bhavet .. 44 ..
5.128.d:
एकमप्यक्षरं यत्र गुरुः शिष्ये निवेदयेत् ..
पृथिव्यां नास्ति तद्द्रव्यं यद्दत्त्वा ह्यनृणी भवेत् .. 44 ..
5.128.m: "Where a guru imparts even a single syllable to a pupil, / there exists no wealth on earth by giving which one could be freed from debt.

5.128.s:
tasmādgaccha drutaṃ dattvā madadhyayanamālayam ..
tyaktvā vidyāṃ mayā dattāṃ no cecchapsyāmyahaṃ tava .. 45 ..
5.128.d:
तस्माद्गच्छ द्रुतं दत्त्वा मदध्ययनमालयम् ..
त्यक्त्वा विद्यां मया दत्तां नो चेच्छप्स्याम्यहं तव .. 45 ..
5.128.m: Therefore, give back what was studied under me and quickly leave my house, / giving up the knowledge bestowed by me, or else I shall curse you!"

5.128.s:
evamuktvābhimaṃtryātha nādabiṃdusamudbhavaiḥ ..
maṃtrairātharvaṇaistoyaṃ pānārthaṃ cārpayattataḥ .. 46 ..
5.128.d:
एवमुक्त्वाभिमंत्र्याथ नादबिंदुसमुद्भवैः ..
मंत्रैराथर्वणैस्तोयं पानार्थं चार्पयत्ततः .. 46 ..
5.128.m: Having spoken thus, consecrating water with mantras of the Atharvaveda / arising from sound and the bindu, he then gave it [to him] to drink.

5.128.s:
so'pibattatkṣaṇāttoyaṃ tatpītvā vyākuleṃdriyaḥ ..
udgiradvāṃtidharmeṇa tattvavidyāvimiśritam .. 47 ..
5.128.d:
सोऽपिबत्तत्क्षणात्तोयं तत्पीत्वा व्याकुलेंद्रियः ..
उद्गिरद्वांतिधर्मेण तत्त्वविद्याविमिश्रितम् .. 47 ..
5.128.m: He drank the water at that moment; having drunk it, his senses agitated, / he vomited it out in the manner of an emetic, mixed with the knowledge of reality.

5.128.s:
tataḥ provāca taṃ bhūyaḥ śākalyaṃ kupitānanaḥ ..
ekamapyakṣaraṃ nāsti tāvakīyaṃ mamodare .. 48 ..
5.128.d:
ततः प्रोवाच तं भूयः शाकल्यं कुपिताननः ..
एकमप्यक्षरं नास्ति तावकीयं ममोदरे .. 48 ..
5.128.m: Then, with an angry face, he spoke again to Śākalya: / "Not even a single syllable belonging to you remains in my belly.

5.128.s:
tasmācchiṣyo'smi te nāhaṃ na ca me tvaṃ guruḥ sthitaḥ ..
sāṃprataṃ svecchayā'nyatra prayāsyāmi karoṣi kim .. 49 ..
5.128.d:
तस्माच्छिष्योऽस्मि ते नाहं न च मे त्वं गुरुः स्थितः ..
सांप्रतं स्वेच्छयाऽन्यत्र प्रयास्यामि करोषि किम् .. 49 ..
5.128.m: Therefore, I am not your disciple, nor do you remain my guru. / Now I will go elsewhere of my own accord; what will you do?"

5.128.s:
evamuktvā'tha nirgatya tasmātsthānācciraṃtanāt ..
papraccha mānavānbhūyaḥ siddhikṣetrāṇi cāsakṛt .. 6.129.50 ..
5.128.d:
एवमुक्त्वाऽथ निर्गत्य तस्मात्स्थानाच्चिरंतनात् ..
पप्रच्छ मानवान्भूयः सिद्धिक्षेत्राणि चासकृत् .. 6.129.50 ..
5.128.m: Having spoken thus and departed from that ancient place, / he repeatedly asked people about sacred fields yielding spiritual attainment.

5.128.s:
tatastasya samādiṣṭaṃ kṣetrametanmanīṣibhiḥ ..
siddhidaṃ sarvajaṃtūnāṃ na vṛthā syātkathaṃcana .. 51 ..
5.128.d:
ततस्तस्य समादिष्टं क्षेत्रमेतन्मनीषिभिः ..
सिद्धिदं सर्वजंतूनां न वृथा स्यात्कथंचन .. 51 ..
5.128.m: Then this sacred field was indicated to him by the wise / as one giving spiritual attainment to all living beings, and never failing in any way:

5.128.s:
āstāṃ tāvattapastaptvā vrataṃ niyamameva vā ..
hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre siddhiḥ saṃvasato'pi ca .. 52 ..
5.128.d:
आस्तां तावत्तपस्तप्त्वा व्रतं नियममेव वा ..
हाटकेश्वरजे क्षेत्रे सिद्धिः संवसतोऽपि च .. 52 ..
5.128.m: "Let alone performing austerity, a vow, or a restriction, / there is spiritual attainment even merely by dwelling in the sacred field born of Hāṭakeśvara.

5.128.s:
yenayena ca bhāvena tatra kṣetre vasejjanaḥ ..
tasyānurūpiṇī siddhiḥ śubhā syādyadi vā'śubhā .. 53 ..
5.128.d:
येनयेन च भावेन तत्र क्षेत्रे वसेज्जनः ..
तस्यानुरूपिणी सिद्धिः शुभा स्याद्यदि वाऽशुभा .. 53 ..
5.128.m: With whatever disposition a person lives in that sacred field, / attainment corresponding to it, whether auspicious or inauspicious, will arise."

5.128.s:
tacchrutvā ca drutaṃ prāpya kṣetrametaddvijottamāḥ ..
bhānumārādhayāmāsa sthāpayitvā tataḥ param .. 54 ..
5.128.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा च द्रुतं प्राप्य क्षेत्रमेतद्द्विजोत्तमाः ..
भानुमाराधयामास स्थापयित्वा ततः परम् .. 54 ..
5.128.m: Hearing that and quickly reaching this sacred field, O best of brahmins, / he established [an image] and thereafter worshipped the Sun,

5.128.s:
niyato niyatāhāro brahmacaryaparāyaṇaḥ ..
gāyatraṃ nyāsamāsādya nirvikalpena cetasā .. 55 ..
5.128.d:
नियतो नियताहारो ब्रह्मचर्यपरायणः ..
गायत्रं न्यासमासाद्य निर्विकल्पेन चेतसा .. 55 ..
5.128.m: self-restrained, with controlled food, devoted to celibacy, / having performed the nyāsa of the Gāyatrī, with an unwavering mind.

5.128.s:
tataśca bhagavāṃstuṣṭo varṣāṃte tamuvāca saḥ ..
darśane tasya saṃsthitvā tejaḥ saṃyamya dāruṇam .. 56 ..
5.128.d:
ततश्च भगवांस्तुष्टो वर्षांते तमुवाच सः ..
दर्शने तस्य संस्थित्वा तेजः संयम्य दारुणम् .. 56 ..
5.128.m: Then, pleased at the end of a year, the Lord spoke to him, / standing visible to him after subduing his fierce fiery radiance:

5.128.s:
yājñavalkya varaṃ brūhi yatte manasi rocate ..
sarvameva pradāsyāmi nādeyaṃ vidyate tvayi .. 57 ..
5.128.d:
याज्ञवल्क्य वरं ब्रूहि यत्ते मनसि रोचते ..
सर्वमेव प्रदास्यामि नादेयं विद्यते त्वयि .. 57 ..
5.128.m: "O Yājñavalkya, choose a boon that pleases your mind. / I shall grant everything; there is nothing that should not be given to you."

5.128.s:
.. yājñavalkya uvāca .. ..
yadi tuṣṭaḥ suraśreṣṭha vedādhyayanasaṃbhave ..
gururbhava mamādyaiva mamaitadvāṃchitaṃ hṛdi . 58 ..
5.128.d:
.. याज्ञवल्क्य उवाच .. ..
यदि तुष्टः सुरश्रेष्ठ वेदाध्ययनसंभवे ..
गुरुर्भव ममाद्यैव ममैतद्वांछितं हृदि . 58 ..
5.128.m: Yājñavalkya said: / "If you are pleased, O best of gods, / become my guru this very day in the study of the Vedas; this is my heart's desire."

5.128.s:
.. bhāskara uvāca .. ..
ahaṃ tava kṛpāviṣṭastejaḥ saṃhṛtya tatparam ..
tataścātra samāyātastena no dahyase dvija .. 59 ..
5.128.d:
.. भास्कर उवाच .. ..
अहं तव कृपाविष्टस्तेजः संहृत्य तत्परम् ..
ततश्चात्र समायातस्तेन नो दह्यसे द्विज .. 59 ..
5.128.m: Bhāskara said: / "Filled with compassion for you, I have withdrawn that supreme fiery radiance / and come here, so that you are not burned by it, O brahmin.

5.128.s:
tasmādatraiva kuṃḍe ca maṃtrānsārasvatāñchubhān ..
vedoktānkṣepayiṣyāmi svayameva dvijottama .. .. 6.129.60 ..
5.128.d:
तस्मादत्रैव कुंडे च मंत्रान्सारस्वताञ्छुभान् ..
वेदोक्तान्क्षेपयिष्यामि स्वयमेव द्विजोत्तम .. .. 6.129.60 ..
5.128.m: "Therefore, right here in this pool, O best of brahmins, / I myself shall cast the auspicious mantras belonging to Sarasvatī that are proclaimed in the Veda.

5.128.s:
tatra snātvā śucirbhūtvā yatkiṃcidvedasaṃbhavam ..
paṭhiṣyasi sakṛttatte kaṃṭhasthaṃ saṃbhaviṣyati .. 61 ..
5.128.d:
तत्र स्नात्वा शुचिर्भूत्वा यत्किंचिद्वेदसंभवम् ..
पठिष्यसि सकृत्तत्ते कंठस्थं संभविष्यति .. 61 ..
5.128.m: Having bathed there and become pure, whatever part born of the Veda / you recite but once, that will be retained in your throat.

5.128.s:
tattvārthaṃ prakaṭaṃ kṛtsnaṃ viditaṃ te bhaviṣyati ..
matprasādānna saṃdehaḥ satyametanmayoditam .. 62 ..
5.128.d:
तत्त्वार्थं प्रकटं कृत्स्नं विदितं ते भविष्यति ..
मत्प्रसादान्न संदेहः सत्यमेतन्मयोदितम् .. 62 ..
5.128.m: The entire manifest meaning of reality will be known to you / by my grace—there is no doubt; this truth has been spoken by me.

5.128.s:
adyādi mānavaḥ prātaḥ snātvā tvatra hrade ca yaḥ ..
sāvitreṇa ca sūktena māṃ dṛṣṭvā prapaṭhiṣyati ..
tasmai tatsyādasaṃdigdhaṃ yattavoktaṃ mayā dvija .. 63 ..
5.128.d:
अद्यादि मानवः प्रातः स्नात्वा त्वत्र ह्रदे च यः ..
सावित्रेण च सूक्तेन मां दृष्ट्वा प्रपठिष्यति ..
तस्मै तत्स्यादसंदिग्धं यत्तवोक्तं मया द्विज .. 63 ..
5.128.m: From this day forward, whatever human bathes in the morning in this pool, / and beholding me recites the hymn to Savitṛ, / to him that shall undoubtedly happen which has been told by me to you, O brahmin."

5.128.s:
.. yājñavalkya uvāca .. ..
evaṃ bhavatu deveśa yattvayoktaṃ vaco'khilam ..
paraṃ mama vaco'nyacca tacchṛṇuṣva bravīmi te .. 64 ..
5.128.d:
.. याज्ञवल्क्य उवाच .. ..
एवं भवतु देवेश यत्त्वयोक्तं वचोऽखिलम् ..
परं मम वचोऽन्यच्च तच्छृणुष्व ब्रवीमि ते .. 64 ..
5.128.m: Yājñavalkya said: / "Let all that was spoken by you be so, O Lord of gods; / but hear another word of mine—I speak to you.

5.128.s:
nāhaṃ manuṣyadharmāṇamupādhyāyaṃ kathaṃcana ..
kariṣyāmi jagannātha kṛpāṃ kuru mamopari .. 65 ..
5.128.d:
नाहं मनुष्यधर्माणमुपाध्यायं कथंचन ..
करिष्यामि जगन्नाथ कृपां कुरु ममोपरि .. 65 ..
5.128.m: Under no circumstances shall I take a teacher / who possesses human qualities, O Lord of the universe; have mercy on me!"

5.128.s:
tatastasyā dadau sūryo laghimā nāma śobhanām..
vidyāṃ hi tatprabhāvāya sutuṣṭenāṃtarātmanā .. 66 ..
5.128.d:
ततस्तस्या ददौ सूर्यो लघिमा नाम शोभनाम्..
विद्यां हि तत्प्रभावाय सुतुष्टेनांतरात्मना .. 66 ..
5.128.m: Then, with an exceedingly pleased inner spirit, the sun gave him / the auspicious lore named Laghimā for the sake of that power.

5.128.s:
tatastaṃ prāha karṇāṃte mamāśvānāṃ praviśya vai ..
abhyāsaṃ kuru vidyānāṃ vedādhyayanamācara .. 67 ..
5.128.d:
ततस्तं प्राह कर्णांते ममाश्वानां प्रविश्य वै ..
अभ्यासं कुरु विद्यानां वेदाध्ययनमाचर .. 67 ..
5.128.m: Then he said to him: "Entering near the ear of my horses, / practice the sciences and perform the study of the Veda.

5.128.s:
manmukhādbrāhmaṇaśreṣṭha yadyetattava vāṃchitam ..
na te syādyena doṣo'yaṃ mama raśmisamudbhavaḥ .. 68 ..
5.128.d:
मन्मुखाद्ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठ यद्येतत्तव वांछितम् ..
न ते स्याद्येन दोषोऽयं मम रश्मिसमुद्भवः .. 68 ..
5.128.m: [Learn] from my mouth, O best of brahmins, if this is your desire, / so that no fault arising from my rays will fall upon you."

5.128.s:
evamuktaḥ sa tenātha vājikarṇaṃ samāśritaḥ ..
laghurbhūtvā'paṭhadvedānbhāskarasya mukhāttataḥ .. 69 ..
5.128.d:
एवमुक्तः स तेनाथ वाजिकर्णं समाश्रितः ..
लघुर्भूत्वाऽपठद्वेदान्भास्करस्य मुखात्ततः .. 69 ..
5.128.m: Thus addressed by him, taking refuge in the horse's ear / and having become light [in body], he then recited the Vedas from the mouth of the Sun.

5.128.s:
evaṃ siddhiṃ samāpanno yājñavalkyo dvijottamāḥ ..
kṛtvopaniṣadaṃ cāru vedārthaiḥ sakalairyutam .. 6.129.70 ..
5.128.d:
एवं सिद्धिं समापन्नो याज्ञवल्क्यो द्विजोत्तमाः ..
कृत्वोपनिषदं चारु वेदार्थैः सकलैर्युतम् .. 6.129.70 ..
5.128.m: Having achieved perfection in this way, O best of brahmins, / Yājñavalkya composed a beautiful Upaniṣad endowed with all the meanings of the Veda.

5.128.s:
janakāya nareṃdrāya vyākhyāya ca tataḥ param ..
kātyāyanaṃ sutaṃ prāpya vedasūtrasya kārakam .. 71 ..
5.128.d:
जनकाय नरेंद्राय व्याख्याय च ततः परम् ..
कात्यायनं सुतं प्राप्य वेदसूत्रस्य कारकम् .. 71 ..
5.128.m: And after explaining it to King Janaka, / he obtained a son, Kātyāyana, the author of the Vedika aphorisms.

5.128.s:
tyaktvā kalevaraṃ tatra brahmadvāri vinirmite ..
tattejo brahmaṇo gātre yojayāmāsa śaktitaḥ .. 72 ..
5.128.d:
त्यक्त्वा कलेवरं तत्र ब्रह्मद्वारि विनिर्मिते ..
तत्तेजो ब्रह्मणो गात्रे योजयामास शक्तितः .. 72 ..
5.128.m: Discarding his physical frame there at the fashioned gate of Brahmā, / he joined that splendour into the body of Brahman according to his power.

5.128.s:
tasya tīrthe naraḥ snātvā dṛṣṭvā taṃ ca divākaram ..
nādabiṃduṃ paṭhitvā ca tadagre muktimāpnuyāt .. 73 ..
5.128.d:
तस्य तीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा दृष्ट्वा तं च दिवाकरम् ..
नादबिंदुं पठित्वा च तदग्रे मुक्तिमाप्नुयात् .. 73 ..
5.128.m: A person who bathes at his sacred ford, sees the Sun, / and recites the Nādabindu before it, attains liberation.

5.128.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye yājñavalkyāśramamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāmaikonatriṃśaduttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 129 .. .. cha ..
5.128.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये याज्ञवल्क्याश्रममाहात्म्यवर्णनंनामैकोनत्रिंशदुत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 129 .. .. छ ..
5.128.m: Thus ends the hundred and twenty-ninth chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of the Hermitage of Yājñavalkya,' in the 'Glory of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara' in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. 129.

5.129.s:
..ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
yājñavalkyasutaḥ sūta yastvayā parikīrtitaḥ ..
katamā tasya mātābhūtsarvaṃ no brūhi vistarāt .. 1 ..
5.129.d:
..ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
याज्ञवल्क्यसुतः सूत यस्त्वया परिकीर्तितः ..
कतमा तस्य माताभूत्सर्वं नो ब्रूहि विस्तरात् .. 1 ..
5.129.m: The seers said: / "O Sūta, the son of Yājñavalkya who was mentioned by you— / which [wife] was his mother? Tell us everything in detail!"

5.129.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tasya bhāryādvayaṃ śreṣṭhamāsītsarvaguṇānvitam..
ekā guṇavatī tasya maitreyīti prakīrtitā .. 2 ..
5.129.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तस्य भार्याद्वयं श्रेष्ठमासीत्सर्वगुणान्वितम्..
एका गुणवती तस्य मैत्रेयीति प्रकीर्तिता .. 2 ..
5.129.m: Sūta said: / "He had two excellent wives, endowed with all virtues. / One virtuous [wife] of his was renowned as Maitreyī.

5.129.s:
jyeṣṭhā cānyātha kalyāṇī khyātā kātyāyanīti ca ..
yasyāḥ kātyāyanaḥ putro vedārthānāṃ prajalpakaḥ .. 3 ..
5.129.d:
ज्येष्ठा चान्याथ कल्याणी ख्याता कात्यायनीति च ..
यस्याः कात्यायनः पुत्रो वेदार्थानां प्रजल्पकः .. 3 ..
5.129.m: And the other, the elder and auspicious one, was known as Kātyāyanī, / whose son was Kātyāyana, the expounder of the meanings of the Veda.

5.129.s:
tābhyāṃ kuṇḍadvayaṃ tatra saṃtiṣṭhati suśobhanam ..
yatra snātā narā yāṃti lokāṃstāṃśca mahodayān ..4 ..
5.129.d:
ताभ्यां कुण्डद्वयं तत्र संतिष्ठति सुशोभनम् ..
यत्र स्नाता नरा यांति लोकांस्तांश्च महोदयान् ..4 ..
5.129.m: Between the two of them there are two very beautiful pools, / bathing in which men go to worlds of great splendour.

5.129.s:
kātyāyanyāśca tīrthasya śāṃḍilyāstīrthamuttamam..
pativratātvayuktāyāstathānyattatra saṃsthitam .. 5 ..
5.129.d:
कात्यायन्याश्च तीर्थस्य शांडिल्यास्तीर्थमुत्तमम्..
पतिव्रतात्वयुक्तायास्तथान्यत्तत्र संस्थितम् .. 5 ..
5.129.m: Next to Kātyāyanī's sacred ford, there is another excellent sacred ford located there, / belonging to Śāṇḍilī, who was devoted to her husband.

5.129.s:
yatra kātyāyanī prāptā śāṃḍilyā pratibodhitā ..
vairāgyaṃ paramaṃ prāptā sapatnīduḥkhaduḥkhitā .. 6 ..
5.129.d:
यत्र कात्यायनी प्राप्ता शांडिल्या प्रतिबोधिता ..
वैराग्यं परमं प्राप्ता सपत्नीदुःखदुःखिता .. 6 ..
5.129.m: Where Kātyāyanī arrived, instructed by Śāṇḍilī, / and reached supreme detachment, grieved by the sorrow of a co-wife.

5.129.s:
tatra yā kurute snānaṃ tṛtīyāyāṃ samāhitā ..
nārī mārgasite pakṣe sā saubhāgyavatī bhavet ..
atha daurbhāgyasaṃpannā kāṇā vṛddhā'tha vāmanā ..
abhīṣṭā jāyate sā ca tatprabhāvāddvijottamāḥ .. 8 ..
5.129.d:
तत्र या कुरुते स्नानं तृतीयायां समाहिता ..
नारी मार्गसिते पक्षे सा सौभाग्यवती भवेत् ..
अथ दौर्भाग्यसंपन्ना काणा वृद्धाऽथ वामना ..
अभीष्टा जायते सा च तत्प्रभावाद्द्विजोत्तमाः .. 8 ..
5.129.m: Whatever woman, composed in mind, bathes there / on the third day of the bright fortnight of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, becomes fortunate in marriage. / Even if she is afflicted with misfortune, one-eyed, old, or a dwarf, / she becomes beloved through its power, O best of brahmins."

5.129.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
kīdṛksapatnijaṃ duḥkhaṃ kātyāyanyā upasthitam ..
upadeśaḥ kathaṃ labdhaḥ śāṃḍilyāḥ sūta kīdṛśaḥ .. 9 ..
5.129.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
कीदृक्सपत्निजं दुःखं कात्यायन्या उपस्थितम् ..
उपदेशः कथं लब्धः शांडिल्याः सूत कीदृशः .. 9 ..
5.129.m: The seers said: / "What kind of sorrow born of a co-wife befell Kātyāyanī? / How was instruction received from Śāṇḍilī, O Sūta, and of what kind was it?

5.129.s:
kātyāyanyā samācakṣva kautukaṃ no vyavasthitam ..
sāmānyo bhavitā naiṣa upadeśastayeritaḥ .. 6.130.10 ..
5.129.d:
कात्यायन्या समाचक्ष्व कौतुकं नो व्यवस्थितम् ..
सामान्यो भविता नैष उपदेशस्तयेरितः .. 6.130.10 ..
5.129.m: Explain to us the curious circumstance concerning Kātyāyanī. / This instruction uttered by her must not have been an ordinary one!"

5.129.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
maitreyyā saha saṃsaktaṃ yājñavalkyaṃ vilokya sā ..
kātyāyanī suduḥkhārtā saṃjātā cerṣyayā tataḥ .. 11 ..
5.129.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
मैत्रेय्या सह संसक्तं याज्ञवल्क्यं विलोक्य सा ..
कात्यायनी सुदुःखार्ता संजाता चेर्ष्यया ततः .. 11 ..
5.129.m: Sūta said: / "Beholding Yājñavalkya deeply attached to Maitreyī, / that Kātyāyanī became intensely tormented by grief and jealousy.

5.129.s:
sā na snāti na bhuṃkte ca na hāsyaṃ kurute kvacit ..
kevalaṃ bāṣpapūrṇākṣī niḥśvāsāḍhyā babhūva ha .. 12 ..
5.129.d:
सा न स्नाति न भुंक्ते च न हास्यं कुरुते क्वचित् ..
केवलं बाष्पपूर्णाक्षी निःश्वासाढ्या बभूव ह .. 12 ..
5.129.m: She did not bathe, she did not eat, nor did she ever laugh; / her eyes were only filled with tears, and she was heave with sighs.

5.129.s:
tataḥ kadācidevātha phalārthaṃ nirgatā bahiḥ ..
apaśyacchāṃḍilīnāma patipārśve vyavasthitām.. 13 ..
5.129.d:
ततः कदाचिदेवाथ फलार्थं निर्गता बहिः ..
अपश्यच्छांडिलीनाम पतिपार्श्वे व्यवस्थिताम्.. 13 ..
5.129.m: Then once, having gone outside to gather fruits, / she saw the woman named Śāṇḍilī standing beside her husband,

5.129.s:
kṛtāṃjalipuṭāṃ sādhvī vinayāvanatā sthitām ..
so'pi tasyā mukhāsaktaḥ sānurāgaḥ prasannadṛk .. 14 ..
5.129.d:
कृतांजलिपुटां साध्वी विनयावनता स्थिताम् ..
सोऽपि तस्या मुखासक्तः सानुरागः प्रसन्नदृक् .. 14 ..
5.129.m: standing with folded hands, virtuous and bent low with humility. / He too was gazing attentively at her face, full of affection, with a pleased look,

5.129.s:
guṇadoṣodbhavāṃ vārtāmāpṛcchyākathayattathā ..
sā ca tau daṃpatī dṛṣṭvā saṃhṛṣṭāvitaretaram .. 15 ..
5.129.d:
गुणदोषोद्भवां वार्तामापृच्छ्याकथयत्तथा ..
सा च तौ दंपती दृष्ट्वा संहृष्टावितरेतरम् .. 15 ..
5.129.m: and inquired about and spoke of news regarding virtues and shortcomings. / And seeing those two spouses delighted with one another,

5.129.s:
citte sve ciṃtayāmāsa sudhanyeyaṃ tapasvinī ..
yasyāḥ patirmukhāsakto guṇadoṣaprajalpakaḥ ..
sānurāgaśca susnigdho nānyāṃ nārīṃ bibhartti ca .. 16 ..
5.129.d:
चित्ते स्वे चिंतयामास सुधन्येयं तपस्विनी ..
यस्याः पतिर्मुखासक्तो गुणदोषप्रजल्पकः ..
सानुरागश्च सुस्निग्धो नान्यां नारीं बिभर्त्ति च .. 16 ..
5.129.m: she thought in her mind: 'Truly blessed is this ascetic woman, / whose husband gazes intently at her face, converses on virtues and faults, / is affectionate and very tender, and maintains no other woman!'

5.129.s:
evaṃ saṃcitya sā sādhvī bhūyobhūyo dvijottamāḥ ..
jagāma svāśramaṃ paścānniṃdyamānā svakaṃ vapuḥ .. 17 ..
5.129.d:
एवं संचित्य सा साध्वी भूयोभूयो द्विजोत्तमाः ..
जगाम स्वाश्रमं पश्चान्निंद्यमाना स्वकं वपुः .. 17 ..
5.129.m: Reflecting thus again and again, O best of brahmins, / that virtuous woman went back to her own hermitage, reproaching her own body.

5.129.s:
tataḥ kadācidekāṃte sthitāṃ tāṃ śāṃḍilīṃ dvijāḥ ..
bahirgate bhartari ca tasyāḥ kāryeṇa kenacit .. 18 ..
5.129.d:
ततः कदाचिदेकांते स्थितां तां शांडिलीं द्विजाः ..
बहिर्गते भर्तरि च तस्याः कार्येण केनचित् .. 18 ..
5.129.m: Then once, when Śāṇḍilī was remaining in private, O brahmins, / and her husband had gone outside on some business,

5.129.s:
kātyāyanī samāgamya tataḥ papraccha sādaram ..
vada kalyāṇi me kaṃcidupadeśaṃ mahodayam .. 19 ..
5.129.d:
कात्यायनी समागम्य ततः पप्रच्छ सादरम् ..
वद कल्याणि मे कंचिदुपदेशं महोदयम् .. 19 ..
5.129.m: Kātyāyanī approached and then respectfully inquired of her: / 'Tell me, O auspicious one, some instruction of great consequence,

5.129.s:
mukhaprekṣaḥ sadā bharttā yena strīṇāṃ prajāyate ..
nāpamānaṃ karotyeva duruktavacanaiḥ kvacit .. .. 6.130.20 ..
5.129.d:
मुखप्रेक्षः सदा भर्त्ता येन स्त्रीणां प्रजायते ..
नापमानं करोत्येव दुरुक्तवचनैः क्वचित् .. .. 6.130.20 ..
5.129.m: by which a husband ever looks intently at his wife's face / and never dishonours her with harsh-spoken words,

5.129.s:
nānyāṃ saṃgacchate nārīṃ cittenāpi kathaṃcana ..
ahaṃ bhartuḥ kṛtairduḥkhairatīva paripīḍitā ..
sapatnījairviśeṣeṇa tasmānme tvaṃ prakīrtaya .. .. 21 ..
5.129.d:
नान्यां संगच्छते नारीं चित्तेनापि कथंचन ..
अहं भर्तुः कृतैर्दुःखैरतीव परिपीडिता ..
सपत्नीजैर्विशेषेण तस्मान्मे त्वं प्रकीर्तय .. .. 21 ..
5.129.m: nor ever approaches another woman, even in his thoughts! / I am exceedingly afflicted by sorrows caused by my husband, / especially by those born of a co-wife; therefore, explain this to me:

5.129.s:
yathā te vaśago bharttā saṃjātaḥ kāmadaḥ sadā ..
manasāpi na saṃdadhyānnārīmeṣa kathaṃcana .. 22 ..
5.129.d:
यथा ते वशगो भर्त्ता संजातः कामदः सदा ..
मनसापि न संदध्यान्नारीमेष कथंचन .. 22 ..
5.129.m: how your husband has come under your control, ever granting your wishes, / so that he would never direct his mind toward any other woman!'"

5.129.s:
.. śāṃḍilyuvāca .. ..
śṛṇu sādhvi pravakṣyāmi tavāhaṃ guhyamuttamam ..
yathā mamābhavadvaśyo mukhaprekṣastathā patiḥ .. 23 ..
5.129.d:
.. शांडिल्युवाच .. ..
शृणु साध्वि प्रवक्ष्यामि तवाहं गुह्यमुत्तमम् ..
यथा ममाभवद्वश्यो मुखप्रेक्षस्तथा पतिः .. 23 ..
5.129.m: Śāṇḍilī said: / "Listen, O virtuous woman, I shall tell you the supreme secret / of how my husband came under my control and looks intently at my face.

5.129.s:
mama tātaḥ kurukṣetre śāṃḍilyo munisattamaḥ ..
vānaprasthāśrame'tiṣṭhatpūrve vayasi saṃsthitaḥ .. 24 ..
5.129.d:
मम तातः कुरुक्षेत्रे शांडिल्यो मुनिसत्तमः ..
वानप्रस्थाश्रमेऽतिष्ठत्पूर्वे वयसि संस्थितः .. 24 ..
5.129.m: My father was the excellent sage Śāṇḍilya in Kurukṣetra; / in his early age, he stayed in the hermit's life in the forest.

5.129.s:
tatraikāhaṃ samutpannā kanyā tasya mahātmanaḥ ..
vṛddhiṃ gatā krameṇātha tasminneva tapovane .. 25 ..
5.129.d:
तत्रैकाहं समुत्पन्ना कन्या तस्य महात्मनः ..
वृद्धिं गता क्रमेणाथ तस्मिन्नेव तपोवने .. 25 ..
5.129.m: There I was born, the only daughter of that great-souled one, / and grew up gradually in that very penance grove."

5.129.s:
karomi tatra śuśrūṣāṃ homakāle yathocitām ..
nīvārādīni dhānyāni nityaṃ caivānayāmyaham .. 26 ..
5.129.d:
करोमि तत्र शुश्रूषां होमकाले यथोचिताम् ..
नीवारादीनि धान्यानि नित्यं चैवानयाम्यहम् .. 26 ..
5.129.m: I performed service there at the time of the fire offering as was proper, / and I always brought wild grains and other provisions.

5.129.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya nārado munisattamaḥ ..
āśrame mama tātasya suśrāṃtaḥ samupāgataḥ .. 27 ..
5.129.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य नारदो मुनिसत्तमः ..
आश्रमे मम तातस्य सुश्रांतः समुपागतः .. 27 ..
5.129.m: Then, after some time, Nārada, the best of sages, / arrived at my father’s hermitage, utterly exhausted.

5.129.s:
tātādeśāttatastatra mayā sa viśramaḥ kṛtaḥ ..
pādaśaucādibhiḥ kṛtyaiḥ snānādyaiśca tathāparaiḥ .. 28 ..
5.129.d:
तातादेशात्ततस्तत्र मया स विश्रमः कृतः ..
पादशौचादिभिः कृत्यैः स्नानाद्यैश्च तथापरैः .. 28 ..
5.129.m: Then, by my father’s command, rest was provided to him there by me / through services such as washing his feet, bathing, and other such rites.

5.129.s:
tato bhuktāvasāne'tha niviṣṭaḥ mukhasaṃsthita..
mama mātrā paripṛṣṭo vinayādvaravarṇini .. 29 ..
5.129.d:
ततो भुक्तावसानेऽथ निविष्टः मुखसंस्थित..
मम मात्रा परिपृष्टो विनयाद्वरवर्णिनि .. 29 ..
5.129.m: Then, when he had finished eating, seated at ease and comfortably rested, / he was asked with deference by my mother, O fair-complexioned lady:

5.129.s:
ekeyaṃ kanyakāsmākaṃ jāte vayasi saṃsthite ..
saṃjātā muniśārdūla prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī .. 6.130.30 ..
5.129.d:
एकेयं कन्यकास्माकं जाते वयसि संस्थिते ..
संजाता मुनिशार्दूल प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी .. 6.130.30 ..
5.129.m: “This is our only daughter, born when our youth was already advanced, / dearer [to us] even than our own life-breaths, O tiger among sages!

5.129.s:
tadasyāḥ kīrtaya kṣipraṃ sukhopāyaṃ sukhodayam ..
vrataṃ vā niyamaṃ vā tvaṃ homaṃ vā mantrameva vā .. 31 ..
5.129.d:
तदस्याः कीर्तय क्षिप्रं सुखोपायं सुखोदयम् ..
व्रतं वा नियमं वा त्वं होमं वा मन्त्रमेव वा .. 31 ..
5.129.m: Therefore, swiftly declare for her an easy means that brings forth happiness: / a vow, an observance, a fire offering, or even a mantra,

5.129.s:
yena cīrṇena bharttā syātsusaumyaḥ sadguṇānvitaḥ ..
priyaṃvado mukhaprekṣaḥ paranārīparāṅmukhaḥ .. 32 ..
5.129.d:
येन चीर्णेन भर्त्ता स्यात्सुसौम्यः सद्गुणान्वितः ..
प्रियंवदो मुखप्रेक्षः परनारीपराङ्मुखः .. 32 ..
5.129.m: by performing which she may obtain a very gentle husband endowed with good qualities, / sweet-speaking, attentive to her countenance, and turning away from other women.”

5.129.s:
tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā sa munistadanaṃtaram ..
ciraṃ dhyātvā vacaḥ prāha prasannavadanastataḥ .. 33 ..
5.129.d:
तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा स मुनिस्तदनंतरम् ..
चिरं ध्यात्वा वचः प्राह प्रसन्नवदनस्ततः .. 33 ..
5.129.m: Having heard those words of hers, that sage immediately / meditated for a long time, and then spoke with a serene countenance:

5.129.s:
hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre pañcapiṃḍā vyavasthitā ..
gaurī gauryā svayaṃ tatra sthāpitā parameśvarī .. 34 ..
5.129.d:
हाटकेश्वरजे क्षेत्रे पञ्चपिंडा व्यवस्थिता ..
गौरी गौर्या स्वयं तत्र स्थापिता परमेश्वरी .. 34 ..
5.129.m: “In the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara, Parameśvarī Gaurī / resides as Pañcapiṇḍā, having been installed there by Gaurī herself.

5.129.s:
tāmeṣā vatsaraṃ yāvacchraddhayā parayā yutā ..
sadā pūjayatu prītyā tṛtīyāyāṃ viśeṣataḥ .. 35 ..
5.129.d:
तामेषा वत्सरं यावच्छ्रद्धया परया युता ..
सदा पूजयतु प्रीत्या तृतीयायां विशेषतः .. 35 ..
5.129.m: Let her always worship her with supreme faith and devotion for a year, / especially on the third lunar day.

5.129.s:
tato varṣāṃtamāsādya saṃprāpsyati yathocitam ..
bharttāraṃ nātra saṃdeho yādṛgrūpaṃ yathocitam .. 36
5.129.d:
ततो वर्षांतमासाद्य संप्राप्स्यति यथोचितम् ..
भर्त्तारं नात्र संदेहो यादृग्रूपं यथोचितम् .. 36
5.129.m: Then, at the end of the year, she will obtain a husband / of suitable form and worthy [of her]; of this there is no doubt.

5.129.s:
tatra pūrvaṃ gatā gaurī parityajya maheśvaram ..
gaṃgerṣyayā mahābhāge jñātvā kṣetraṃ susiddhidam .. 37 ..
5.129.d:
तत्र पूर्वं गता गौरी परित्यज्य महेश्वरम् ..
गंगेर्ष्यया महाभागे ज्ञात्वा क्षेत्रं सुसिद्धिदम् .. 37 ..
5.129.m: In former times Gaurī went there, having abandoned Maheśvara / out of jealousy toward the Gaṅgā, O noble lady, knowing it to be a sacred field that grants great success.

5.129.s:
tataḥ sā ciṃtayāmāsa kāṃ devīṃ pūjayāmyaham ..
saubhāgyārthaṃ yato'nyā māṃ pūjayaṃti surastriyaḥ .. 38 ..
5.129.d:
ततः सा चिंतयामास कां देवीं पूजयाम्यहम् ..
सौभाग्यार्थं यतोऽन्या मां पूजयंति सुरस्त्रियः .. 38 ..
5.129.m: Then she reflected: ‘Which goddess shall I worship / for the sake of marital fortune, since other divine women worship me?

5.129.s:
tasmādahaṃ prabhaktyāḍhyā svayamātmānameva ca ..
ātmanaiva kṛtotsāhā pūjayiṣyāmi siddhaye .. .. 39 ..
5.129.d:
तस्मादहं प्रभक्त्याढ्या स्वयमात्मानमेव च ..
आत्मनैव कृतोत्साहा पूजयिष्यामि सिद्धये .. .. 39 ..
5.129.m: Therefore, filled with great devotion, inspired with enthusiasm through my own self, / I will worship my very own self for the sake of accomplishment.’

5.129.s:
tataḥ prāṇāgnihotrotthairmaṃtrairātharvaṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ ..
mṛtpiṃḍānpaṃca saṃyojya hyekasthāne samāhitā .. 6.130.40 ..
5.129.d:
ततः प्राणाग्निहोत्रोत्थैर्मंत्रैराथर्वणैः शुभैः ..
मृत्पिंडान्पंच संयोज्य ह्येकस्थाने समाहिता .. 6.130.40 ..
5.129.m: Then, with auspicious mantras from the Atharvaveda arising from the internal fire offering, / having brought together five lumps of clay in one place with a collected mind,

5.129.s:
pṛthvīmapaśca tejaśca vāyumākāśameva ca .
teṣu saṃyojayāmāsa mṛtpiṃḍeṣu nidhāya sā .. 41 ..
5.129.d:
पृथ्वीमपश्च तेजश्च वायुमाकाशमेव च .
तेषु संयोजयामास मृत्पिंडेषु निधाय सा .. 41 ..
5.129.m: earth, water, fire, wind, and ether— / she placed these and united them in those lumps of clay.

5.129.s:
mahadbhūtāni caitāni pañca devī yatavratā ..
tataḥ saṃpūjayāmāsa puṣpadhūpānulepanaiḥ .. 42 ..
5.129.d:
महद्भूतानि चैतानि पञ्च देवी यतव्रता ..
ततः संपूजयामास पुष्पधूपानुलेपनैः .. 42 ..
5.129.m: Then the goddess, steadfast in her vow, worshipped these / five great elements with flowers, incenses, and ointments.

5.129.s:
atha tāṃ tatra vijñāya tapaḥsthāṃ girajāṃ bhavaḥ ..
tanmaṃtrākṛṣṭacittaśca satvaraṃ samupāgataḥ .. 43 ..
5.129.d:
अथ तां तत्र विज्ञाय तपःस्थां गिरजां भवः ..
तन्मंत्राकृष्टचित्तश्च सत्वरं समुपागतः .. 43 ..
5.129.m: Now, knowing that Girijā was stationed there in austerity, Bhava, / his mind drawn by those mantras, quickly arrived.

5.129.s:
provāca ca prahṛṣṭātmā kasmāttvamiha cāgatā ..
māṃ muktvā doṣanirmuktaṃ mukhaprekṣaṃ sadā ratam .. 44 ..
5.129.d:
प्रोवाच च प्रहृष्टात्मा कस्मात्त्वमिह चागता ..
मां मुक्त्वा दोषनिर्मुक्तं मुखप्रेक्षं सदा रतम् .. 44 ..
5.129.m: And delighted in mind, he spoke: ‘Why have you come here, / leaving me, who am free from fault, attentive to your countenance, and ever affectionate?

5.129.s:
tasmādāgaccha kailāsaṃ vṛṣārūḍhā mayā saha ..
athavā kāraṇaṃ brūhi yadi doṣo'sti me kvacit .. .. 45 ..
5.129.d:
तस्मादागच्छ कैलासं वृषारूढा मया सह ..
अथवा कारणं ब्रूहि यदि दोषोऽस्ति मे क्वचित् .. .. 45 ..
5.129.m: Therefore, mount the bull and come with me to Kailāsa, / or else tell me the reason if there is any fault in me.’

5.129.s:
.. devyuvāca .. ..
tvaṃ mūrdhnā jāhnavīṃ dhatse mūrtāṃ padajalātmikām ..
tasmānnāhaṃ gamiṣyāmi maṃdiraṃ te kathaṃcana .. 46 ..
5.129.d:
.. देव्युवाच .. ..
त्वं मूर्ध्ना जाह्नवीं धत्से मूर्तां पदजलात्मिकाम् ..
तस्मान्नाहं गमिष्यामि मंदिरं ते कथंचन .. 46 ..
5.129.m: The goddess said: / ‘You bear the Jāhnavī on your head, embodied as water from [Viṣṇu’s] foot; / therefore, I will by no means go to your abode

5.129.s:
yāvanna tyajasi vyaktaṃ mama sāpatnyatāṃ gatām ..
tathā nityaṃ praṇāmaṃ tvaṃ karoṣi vṛṣabhadhvaja .. 47 ..
5.129.d:
यावन्न त्यजसि व्यक्तं मम सापत्न्यतां गताम् ..
तथा नित्यं प्रणामं त्वं करोषि वृषभध्वज .. 47 ..
5.129.m: so long as you do not visibly abandon her who has become my co-wife. / Moreover, you continually bow down, O Bull-bannered Lord,

5.129.s:
pratyakṣamapi me nityaṃ saṃdhyāyāśca na lajjase ..
tasmādetatparityajya karma lajjākaraṃ param .. 48 ..
5.129.d:
प्रत्यक्षमपि मे नित्यं संध्यायाश्च न लज्जसे ..
तस्मादेतत्परित्यज्य कर्म लज्जाकरं परम् .. 48 ..
5.129.m: even before my very eyes every day to Sandhyā, and you feel no shame. / Therefore, give up this exceedingly shameful conduct!

5.129.s:
ākārayasi māṃ deva tatsyādyadi mataṃ mama ..
anyathāhaṃ na yāsyāmi tava harmye kathaṃcana ..
etacchrutvā yadiṣṭaṃ te kuruṣva vṛṣabhadhvaja .. 49 ..
5.129.d:
आकारयसि मां देव तत्स्याद्यदि मतं मम ..
अन्यथाहं न यास्यामि तव हर्म्ये कथंचन ..
एतच्छ्रुत्वा यदिष्टं ते कुरुष्व वृषभध्वज .. 49 ..
5.129.m: If you summon me, O Lord, let it be according to my wish; / otherwise, I will by no means go to your palace. / Having heard this, do as you please, O Bull-bannered Lord!’

5.129.s:
.. deva uvāca . ..
nāhaṃ saukhyena tāṃ gaṃgāṃ dhārayāmi sureśvari .. 6.130.50 ..
5.129.m: The Lord said: / ‘I do not bear the Gaṅgā for the sake of pleasure, O ruler of the gods!

5.129.s:
bhagīrathena bhūpena prārthito jñāti kāraṇāt ..
divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu tapastaptvā sudāruṇam .. 51 ..
5.129.d:
भगीरथेन भूपेन प्रार्थितो ज्ञाति कारणात् ..
दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रं तु तपस्तप्त्वा सुदारुणम् .. 51 ..
5.129.m: I was entreatied by King Bhagīratha on behalf of his kinsmen, / after he performed severe austerity for a divine thousand years, [saying:]

5.129.s:
yena no yāti pātālaṃ gaṃgā svargaparicyutā ..
tasmāttvaṃ deva madvākyātsvamūrdhnā vaha jāhnavīm ..52..
5.129.d:
येन नो याति पातालं गंगा स्वर्गपरिच्युता ..
तस्मात्त्वं देव मद्वाक्यात्स्वमूर्ध्ना वह जाह्नवीम् ..52..
5.129.m: “So that the Gaṅgā, fallen from heaven, does not go down to Pātāla, / therefore, O Lord, at my request, bear the Jāhnavī on your head!”

5.129.s:
mayā tasya pratijñātaṃ dhārayiṣyāmyasaṃśayam ..
ākāśājjāhnavīvegaṃ pataṃtaṃ dharaṇītale .. 53 ..
5.129.d:
मया तस्य प्रतिज्ञातं धारयिष्याम्यसंशयम् ..
आकाशाज्जाह्नवीवेगं पतंतं धरणीतले .. 53 ..
5.129.m: I promised him, “Without doubt I shall hold / the speed of the Jāhnavī falling from the sky upon the surface of the earth.”

5.129.s:
no cedvrajeta pātālaṃ yadatra viṣayesthi?m..
tato'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi tadihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu ..54..
5.129.d:
नो चेद्व्रजेत पातालं यदत्र विषयेस्थि?म्..
ततोऽहं संप्रवक्ष्यामि तदिहैकमनाः शृणु ..54..
5.129.m: Lest what exists in this realm should go to Pātāla. / Therefore, I shall explain it; listen here with a single-pointed mind:

5.129.s:
eṣā gaṃgā varārohe mama mūrdhno vinirgatā ..
himavaṃtaṃ nagaṃ bhittvā dvidhā jātā tataḥ param..55..
5.129.d:
एषा गंगा वरारोहे मम मूर्ध्नो विनिर्गता ..
हिमवंतं नगं भित्त्वा द्विधा जाता ततः परम्..55..
5.129.m: This Gaṅgā, O lady of fair hips, issuing from my head, / cleaved Mount Himavat, and after that split into two.

5.129.s:
tataḥ siṃdhvabhidhānā sā paścimaṃ sāgaraṃ gatā..
śatāni nava saṃgṛhya nadīnāṃ parameśvari ..56..
5.129.d:
ततः सिंध्वभिधाना सा पश्चिमं सागरं गता..
शतानि नव संगृह्य नदीनां परमेश्वरि ..56..
5.129.m: Then, under the name Sindhu, it went to the western ocean, / gathering nine hundred rivers, O Parameśvarī;

5.129.s:
tathā gaṃgābhidhānā ca saiva prāksāgaraṃ gatā ..
tāvatīśca samādāya nadīḥ parvatanandini ..57..
5.129.d:
तथा गंगाभिधाना च सैव प्राक्सागरं गता ..
तावतीश्च समादाय नदीः पर्वतनन्दिनि ..57..
5.129.m: likewise, that same river, under the name Gaṅgā, went to the eastern ocean, / taking along an equal number of rivers, O daughter of the mountain.

5.129.s:
evamaṣṭādaśaitāni nadīnāṃ parvatātmaje ..
śatāni sāgare yāṃti tena nityaṃ sa tiṣṭhati ..58..
5.129.d:
एवमष्टादशैतानि नदीनां पर्वतात्मजे ..
शतानि सागरे यांति तेन नित्यं स तिष्ठति ..58..
5.129.m: Thus, these eighteen hundred rivers, O daughter of the mountain, / flow into the ocean; because of this it always endures,

5.129.s:
satataṃ śoṣyamāṇo'pi vāḍavena divāniśam ..
samudrasalilaṃ meghāḥ samādāya tataḥ param ..59..
5.129.d:
सततं शोष्यमाणोऽपि वाडवेन दिवानिशम् ..
समुद्रसलिलं मेघाः समादाय ततः परम् ..59..
5.129.m: even though it is constantly being dried up day and night by the submarine fire. / Then, gathering the waters of the ocean, the clouds

5.129.s:
martyaloke pravarṣaṃti tataḥ sasyaṃ prajāyate..
sasyena jīvate lokaḥ prabhavanti makhāstathā ..
makhāṃśena surāḥ sarve tṛptiṃ yāṃti tataḥ param.. 6.130.60 ..
5.129.d:
मर्त्यलोके प्रवर्षंति ततः सस्यं प्रजायते..
सस्येन जीवते लोकः प्रभवन्ति मखास्तथा ..
मखांशेन सुराः सर्वे तृप्तिं यांति ततः परम्.. 6.130.60 ..
5.129.m: rain down upon the mortal world; from that, grain is produced; / by grain, the world lives, and likewise sacrifices come into being; / through their share of sacrifices, all the gods attain satisfaction thereafter.

5.129.s:
etasmātkāraṇānmūrdhni devi gaṃgāṃ dadhāmyaham ..
na snehātkāmato naiva jagadyena pravartate .. 61 ..
5.129.d:
एतस्मात्कारणान्मूर्ध्नि देवि गंगां दधाम्यहम् ..
न स्नेहात्कामतो नैव जगद्येन प्रवर्तते .. 61 ..
5.129.m: For this reason, O goddess, I bear the Gaṅgā on my head, / not out of attachment, nor out of desire, so that the world may function.

5.129.s:
athavā santyajāmyenāṃ yadi mūrdhnaḥ kathaṃcana ..
taddūraṃ vegato bhittvā pṛthvīṃ yāti rasātalam .. 62 ..
5.129.d:
अथवा सन्त्यजाम्येनां यदि मूर्ध्नः कथंचन ..
तद्दूरं वेगतो भित्त्वा पृथ्वीं याति रसातलम् .. 62 ..
5.129.m: Alternatively, if I somehow let her go from my head, / cleaving far through the earth with her force, she will go to Rasātala.

5.129.s:
tataḥ śoṣaṃ vrajedāśu samudraḥ saritāṃ patiḥ ..
aurveṇa pīyamāno'tra tato vṛṣṭirna jāyate ..
vṛṣṭyabhāvājjagannāśaḥ satyametanmayoditam .. 63 ..
5.129.d:
ततः शोषं व्रजेदाशु समुद्रः सरितां पतिः ..
और्वेण पीयमानोऽत्र ततो वृष्टिर्न जायते ..
वृष्ट्यभावाज्जगन्नाशः सत्यमेतन्मयोदितम् .. 63 ..
5.129.m: Then the ocean, the lord of rivers, would swiftly dry up, / being swallowed by the Aurva fire here; from that, rain would not occur, / and from the absence of rain would come the destruction of the world. This is the truth that I have spoken.

5.129.s:
evaṃ gaṃgākṛte proktaṃ mayā tava sureśvari ..
śṛṇu sandhyākṛte'nyacca yena tāṃ praṇamāmyaham.. 64 ..
5.129.d:
एवं गंगाकृते प्रोक्तं मया तव सुरेश्वरि ..
शृणु सन्ध्याकृतेऽन्यच्च येन तां प्रणमाम्यहम्.. 64 ..
5.129.m: This has been told to you by me concerning the Gaṅgā, O ruler of the gods; / listen now to something else concerning Sandhyā, why it is that I bow down to her.’

5.129.s: iti śrīskāndemahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśva rakṣetramāhātmye paṃcapiṇḍāgauryutpattivarṇanaṃnāma triṃśaduttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 130 .. .. cha ..
5.129.d: इति श्रीस्कान्देमहापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्व रक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये पंचपिण्डागौर्युत्पत्तिवर्णनंनाम त्रिंशदुत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 130 .. .. छ ..
5.129.m: Thus ends the one hundred and thirtieth chapter, entitled ‘Description of the Origin of Pañcapiṇḍāgaurī,’ in the Māhātmya of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] in the Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses composed by Śrī Skanda.

5.130.s:
.. deva uvāca .. ..
eṣā rātriḥ samādiṣṭā dānavānāṃ sureśvari ..
piśācānāṃ ca bhūtānāṃ rākṣasānāṃ viśeṣataḥ .. 1 ..
5.130.d:
.. देव उवाच .. ..
एषा रात्रिः समादिष्टा दानवानां सुरेश्वरि ..
पिशाचानां च भूतानां राक्षसानां विशेषतः .. 1 ..
5.130.m: The Lord said: / ‘This night has been assigned, O ruler of the gods, to the Dānavas, / and especially to Piśācas, Bhūtas, and Rākṣasas.

5.130.s:
yatkiṃcitkriyate karma tatra snānādikaṃ śubham..
tatsarvaṃ jāyate teṣāṃ purā dattaṃ svayaṃbhuvā .. 2 ..
5.130.d:
यत्किंचित्क्रियते कर्म तत्र स्नानादिकं शुभम्..
तत्सर्वं जायते तेषां पुरा दत्तं स्वयंभुवा .. 2 ..
5.130.m: Whatever auspicious rite is performed then, such as ritual ablution, / all of that belongs to them; this was granted long ago by the Self-manifest.’

5.130.s:
maryādā taiḥ samaṃ yena devānāṃ ca yadā kṛtā ..
arhāṇāṃ yajñabhāgasya kāśyapānāmathāgrajām.. 3 ..
5.130.d:
मर्यादा तैः समं येन देवानां च यदा कृता ..
अर्हाणां यज्ञभागस्य काश्यपानामथाग्रजाम्.. 3 ..
5.130.m: when a boundary was set by him alongside them and the gods, / who are worthy of their share of the sacrifice, for the elder-born offspring of Kaśyapa.

5.130.s:
tadarthaṃ daśasāhasrā dānavā yuddha durmadāḥ ..
kuṃtaprāsakarā bhānuṃ ruṃdhantyudgatakārmukāḥ ..4..
5.130.d:
तदर्थं दशसाहस्रा दानवा युद्ध दुर्मदाः ..
कुंतप्रासकरा भानुं रुंधन्त्युद्गतकार्मुकाः ..4..
5.130.m: For that purpose, ten thousand Dānavas, arrogant in battle, / holding spears and darts, blocking the sun with raised bows;

5.130.s:
tamuddiśya sahasrāṃśuṃ yajjalaṃ parikṣipyate.
sāvitreṇa ca mantreṇa teṣāṃ tajjāyate phalam ..5..
5.130.d:
तमुद्दिश्य सहस्रांशुं यज्जलं परिक्षिप्यते.
सावित्रेण च मन्त्रेण तेषां तज्जायते फलम् ..5..
5.130.m: The water that is cast aiming at the thousand-rayed sun / with the Savitṛ mantra results in their [destruction].

5.130.s:
te hatāstena toyena vajratulyena tatkṣaṇāt ..
pramuṃcaṃti sahasrāṃśuṃ nityameva sureśvari .. 6 ..
5.130.d:
ते हतास्तेन तोयेन वज्रतुल्येन तत्क्षणात् ..
प्रमुंचंति सहस्रांशुं नित्यमेव सुरेश्वरि .. 6 ..
5.130.m: Slain instantly by that water, which is like a thunderbolt, / they release the thousand-rayed sun, O ruler of the gods, constantly.

5.130.s:
etasmātkāraṇāttoyamastrarūpaṃ kṣipāmyaham ..
saṃdhyā kālaṃ samuddiśya bhānuṃ saṃdhyāṃ na pārvati .. 7 ..
5.130.d:
एतस्मात्कारणात्तोयमस्त्ररूपं क्षिपाम्यहम् ..
संध्या कालं समुद्दिश्य भानुं संध्यां न पार्वति .. 7 ..
5.130.m: For this reason I cast water that has the form of a missile, / addressing the twilight hour and the sun, not [worshiping] twilight [as a woman], O Pārvatī.

5.130.s:
yadyadācarati śreṣṭhastattaduttarataḥ sthitaḥ ..
udayārthaṃ raviṃ yāntaṃ nirundhanti ca dāruṇāḥ .. 8 ..
5.130.d:
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदुत्तरतः स्थितः ..
उदयार्थं रविं यान्तं निरुन्धन्ति च दारुणाः .. 8 ..
5.130.m: Whatever the best person practices, those standing behind follow that. / When the sun advances toward sunrise, the cruel [demons] obstruct him.

5.130.s:
te'pi saṃdhyājalairdevi nihatā brāhmaṇottamaiḥ ..
mayā ca taṃ vimuñcaṃti mūrcchitā nipatanti ca .. 9 ..
5.130.d:
तेऽपि संध्याजलैर्देवि निहता ब्राह्मणोत्तमैः ..
मया च तं विमुञ्चंति मूर्च्छिता निपतन्ति च .. 9 ..
5.130.m: They too, O goddess, slain by the twilight waters by the best of brahmins / and by me, release him, fainting and falling down.

5.130.s:
etasmātkāraṇāddevi sandhyayorubhayorapi ..
ahaṃ cānye ca viprā ye te namaṃti divākaram.. 6.131.10 ..
5.130.d:
एतस्मात्कारणाद्देवि सन्ध्ययोरुभयोरपि ..
अहं चान्ये च विप्रा ये ते नमंति दिवाकरम्.. 6.131.10 ..
5.130.m: For this reason, O goddess, at both twilights, / I and whatever other brahmins there are bow down to the daymaker.

5.130.s:
tasmāttvaṃ gṛhamāgaccha tyaktverṣyāṃ parvatātmaje ..
praśasyāṃ tvāṃ parityaktvā nānyāsti hṛdaye mama .. 11 ..
5.130.d:
तस्मात्त्वं गृहमागच्छ त्यक्त्वेर्ष्यां पर्वतात्मजे ..
प्रशस्यां त्वां परित्यक्त्वा नान्यास्ति हृदये मम .. 11 ..
5.130.m: Therefore, abandon jealousy and return home, O daughter of the mountain; / abandoning you, who are praiseworthy, there is no other woman in my heart."

5.130.s:
.. devyuvāca .. ..
niṣkāmo vā sakāmo vā saṃdhyāṃ strīsaṃjñitāmimām ..
yattvaṃ namasi deveśa tanme duḥkhaṃ prajāyate .. 12 ..
5.130.d:
.. देव्युवाच .. ..
निष्कामो वा सकामो वा संध्यां स्त्रीसंज्ञितामिमाम् ..
यत्त्वं नमसि देवेश तन्मे दुःखं प्रजायते .. 12 ..
5.130.m: The goddess said: / "Whether without desire or with desire, that you bow to this twilight, / who is named as a woman, O lord of gods, causes grief to me.

5.130.s:
tasmādgaṅgāparityāgaṃ sandhyāyāśca viśeṣataḥ ..
yāvanna kuruṣe deva tāvattuṣṭirna me bhavet .. 13 ..
5.130.d:
तस्माद्गङ्गापरित्यागं सन्ध्यायाश्च विशेषतः ..
यावन्न कुरुषे देव तावत्तुष्टिर्न मे भवेत् .. 13 ..
5.130.m: Therefore, until you abandon the Gaṅgā and especially the twilight, / O god, there will be no satisfaction for me."

5.130.s:
evamuktvā'tha sā devī viśeṣavratamāsthitā..
avamanya mahādevaṃ prārthayānamapi svayam.. 14 ..
5.130.d:
एवमुक्त्वाऽथ सा देवी विशेषव्रतमास्थिता..
अवमन्य महादेवं प्रार्थयानमपि स्वयम्.. 14 ..
5.130.m: Having spoken thus, the goddess then undertook a special vow, / showing disregard even for Mahādeva, though he himself was pleading.

5.130.s:
tataḥ sa cintayāmāsa kimetatkāraṇaṃ sthitam..
viraktā'pi mamotkaṇṭhāṃ yenaiṣā prakaroti na .. 19 ..
na ca sāmnā vrajettuṣṭiṃ kathaṃcidapi pārvatī ..
mṛṣerṣyāṃdhāriṇī devī naitatsvalpaṃ hi kāraṇam .. 16 ..
tato mantraprabhāvaṃ taṃ vijñāya parameśvaraḥ ..
dhyānaṃ dhṛtvā susūkṣmeṇa jñānenātha svayaṃ tataḥ .. 17 ..
tameva mantraṃ mantreṇa nyāsena ca viśeṣataḥ ..
samyagārādhayāmāsa saṃpūjyātmānamātmanā .. 18 ..
yathā devyātmabhūtāni pṛthakkṛtvā ca paṃca ca ..
pūjitāni tathā devaḥ sarveṣāmaṃtare gataḥ .. 19 ..
tānyeva pūjayāmāsa pṛthakkṛtvā samādhitaḥ ..
niyojya ca punarbāhye tataḥ pūjāṃ samācarat ..6.131.2...
5.130.d:
ततः स चिन्तयामास किमेतत्कारणं स्थितम्..
विरक्ताऽपि ममोत्कण्ठां येनैषा प्रकरोति न .. 19 ..
न च साम्ना व्रजेत्तुष्टिं कथंचिदपि पार्वती ..
मृषेर्ष्यांधारिणी देवी नैतत्स्वल्पं हि कारणम् .. 16 ..
ततो मन्त्रप्रभावं तं विज्ञाय परमेश्वरः ..
ध्यानं धृत्वा सुसूक्ष्मेण ज्ञानेनाथ स्वयं ततः .. 17 ..
तमेव मन्त्रं मन्त्रेण न्यासेन च विशेषतः ..
सम्यगाराधयामास संपूज्यात्मानमात्मना .. 18 ..
यथा देव्यात्मभूतानि पृथक्कृत्वा च पंच च ..
पूजितानि तथा देवः सर्वेषामंतरे गतः .. 19 ..
तान्येव पूजयामास पृथक्कृत्वा समाधितः ..
नियोज्य च पुनर्बाह्ये ततः पूजां समाचरत् ..6.131.2...
5.130.m:
Then he reflected, "What is this state of affairs? / Even though estranged, why does she not show longing for me?
And Pārvatī can by no means be appeased by conciliation; / the goddess is consumed by false jealousy—surely this is no small cause."
Then, knowing that power of the mantra, the supreme lord, / having taken up meditation through very subtle knowledge, then himself
worshiped that very mantra through the mantra and especially through nyāsa, / fully worshiping the Self by the Self.
Just as the goddess worshiped her own five forms, having separated them, / so the god entered into the midst of all of them,
and worshiped them, having separated them through absorption; / and having projected them outward again, he then performed the worship.

5.130.s:
tasmānnāsti paraḥ kaścitpūjyapūjyaḥ sa eva ca ..
aiśvaryātsarvadevānāmīśānastena nirmitaḥ .. 21 ..
5.130.d:
तस्मान्नास्ति परः कश्चित्पूज्यपूज्यः स एव च ..
ऐश्वर्यात्सर्वदेवानामीशानस्तेन निर्मितः .. 21 ..
5.130.m: Therefore there is no other higher being; he alone is the worshiper and the worshiped. / Because of his lordship over all gods, he manifested as Īśāna.

5.130.s:
evaṃ yāvatsa īśānaḥ samārādhayati prabhuḥ ..
tāvaddevī samāyātā mantrākṛṣṭā ca yatra saḥ .. 22 ..
5.130.d:
एवं यावत्स ईशानः समाराधयति प्रभुः ..
तावद्देवी समायाता मन्त्राकृष्टा च यत्र सः .. 22 ..
5.130.m: While the lord Īśāna was worshiping in this manner, / the goddess, drawn by the mantra, arrived where he was.

5.130.s:
tataḥ provāca taṃ devaṃ praṇipatyakṛtāṃjaliḥ ..
jñātaṃ mayā vibho sarvaṃ na māṃ tyaja tava priyām .. 23 ..
5.130.d:
ततः प्रोवाच तं देवं प्रणिपत्यकृतांजलिः ..
ज्ञातं मया विभो सर्वं न मां त्यज तव प्रियाम् .. 23 ..
5.130.m: Then, prostrating herself with folded hands, she spoke to the god: / "All is understood by me, O omnipresent one; do not abandon me, your beloved!

5.130.s:
tasmādāgaccha gacchāvo yatra tvaṃ vāñchasi prabho ..
kṣamyatāṃ deva me sarvaṃ na kṛtaṃ yadvacastava .. 24 ..
5.130.d:
तस्मादागच्छ गच्छावो यत्र त्वं वाञ्छसि प्रभो ..
क्षम्यतां देव मे सर्वं न कृतं यद्वचस्तव .. 24 ..
5.130.m: Therefore come, let us go wherever you wish, O lord; / forgive me everything, O god—that I did not obey your word."

5.130.s:
tatastuṣṭo mahādevastāmāliṅgya śucismitām ..
idamūce vihasyoccairmeghagambhīrayā girā .. 25 ..
5.130.d:
ततस्तुष्टो महादेवस्तामालिङ्ग्य शुचिस्मिताम् ..
इदमूचे विहस्योच्चैर्मेघगम्भीरया गिरा .. 25 ..
5.130.m: Then Mahādeva, delighted, embraced her of pure smiles / and spoke these words, laughing loudly, with a voice deep as a thundercloud:

5.130.s:
yaiṣā tvayā''tmabhūtotthā nirmitā paramā tanuḥ ..
etāṃ yā kāminī kācitpūjayiṣyati bhaktitaḥ ..
anenaiva vidhānena tasyā bhartā bhaviṣyati .. 26 ..
5.130.d:
यैषा त्वया'ऽत्मभूतोत्था निर्मिता परमा तनुः ..
एतां या कामिनी काचित्पूजयिष्यति भक्तितः ..
अनेनैव विधानेन तस्या भर्ता भविष्यति .. 26 ..
5.130.m: "This supreme body which has been created, arising from yourself— / whatever woman with desire worships this with devotion, / by this very procedure, will obtain a husband.

5.130.s:
tṛtīyāyāṃ viśeṣeṇa yāvatsaṃvatsaraṃ śubhe ..
sā labhiṣyati satkāntaṃ putradaṃ sarvakāmadam .. 27 ..
5.130.d:
तृतीयायां विशेषेण यावत्संवत्सरं शुभे ..
सा लभिष्यति सत्कान्तं पुत्रदं सर्वकामदम् .. 27 ..
5.130.m: Especially on the third lunar day for a year, O auspicious one, / she will obtain an excellent beloved who gives sons and grants all desires.

5.130.s:
tathaitāṃ māmakīṃ mūrtimīśānākhyāṃ ca ye narāḥ ..
teṣāṃ duṣṭāpi yā kāntā saumyā caiva bhaviṣyati .. 28 ..
5.130.d:
तथैतां मामकीं मूर्तिमीशानाख्यां च ये नराः ..
तेषां दुष्टापि या कान्ता सौम्या चैव भविष्यति .. 28 ..
5.130.m: Likewise, whichever men worship this form of mine named Īśāna, / their beloved, even if malicious, will become gentle.

5.130.s:
ye punaḥ kanyakāhetoḥ pūjayiṣyaṃti bhaktitaḥ ..
yāṃ kanyāṃ manasi sthāpya tāṃ labhiṣyantyasaṃśayam ..29..
5.130.d:
ये पुनः कन्यकाहेतोः पूजयिष्यंति भक्तितः ..
यां कन्यां मनसि स्थाप्य तां लभिष्यन्त्यसंशयम् ..29..
5.130.m: Moreover, those who worship with devotion for the sake of obtaining a maiden, / fixing that maiden in their minds, will without doubt obtain her.

5.130.s:
niṣkāmāścāpi ye martyā pūjayiṣyaṃti sarvadā ..
te yāsyaṃti parāṃ siddhiṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitām .. 6.131.30 ..
5.130.d:
निष्कामाश्चापि ये मर्त्या पूजयिष्यंति सर्वदा ..
ते यास्यंति परां सिद्धिं जरामरणवर्जिताम् .. 6.131.30 ..
5.130.m: And whatever mortals, devoid of desire, worship constantly, / they will attain supreme perfection, free from old age and death."

5.130.s:
evamuktvā mahādevo vṛṣamāropya tāṃ priyām ..
svayamāruhya paścācca kailāsaṃ parvataṃ gataḥ .. 31 ..
5.130.d:
एवमुक्त्वा महादेवो वृषमारोप्य तां प्रियाम् ..
स्वयमारुह्य पश्चाच्च कैलासं पर्वतं गतः .. 31 ..
5.130.m: Having spoken thus, Mahādeva placed his beloved upon the bull, / and having mounted it himself afterwards, went to Mount Kailāsa.

5.130.s:
.. nārada uvāca . ..
tasmāttava suteyaṃ yā tāmārādhayatu drutam ..
pañcapiṇḍamayā gaurīṃ yāvatsaṃvatsaraṃ śubhām .. 32 ..
5.130.d:
.. नारद उवाच . ..
तस्मात्तव सुतेयं या तामाराधयतु द्रुतम् ..
पञ्चपिण्डमया गौरीं यावत्संवत्सरं शुभाम् .. 32 ..
5.130.m: Nārada said: / "Therefore, let this daughter of yours quickly worship that / auspicious Gaurī consisting of five lumps, for the duration of a year,

5.130.s:
tṛtīyāyāṃ viśeṣeṇa tataḥ prāpsyati satpatim ..
mukhaprekṣamatiprītaṃ rūpādibhirguṇairyutam .. 33 ..
5.130.d:
तृतीयायां विशेषेण ततः प्राप्स्यति सत्पतिम् ..
मुखप्रेक्षमतिप्रीतं रूपादिभिर्गुणैर्युतम् .. 33 ..
5.130.m: especially on the third lunar day; then she will obtain an excellent husband, / eager to gaze upon her face, exceedingly loving, endowed with good qualities such as beauty."

5.130.s:
.. śāṃḍilyuvāca .. ..
evamuktvā muniśreṣṭho nāradaḥ prayayau tataḥ ..
tīrthayātrāṃ prati prītyā mama mātrā visarjitaḥ .. 34 ..
5.130.d:
.. शांडिल्युवाच .. ..
एवमुक्त्वा मुनिश्रेष्ठो नारदः प्रययौ ततः ..
तीर्थयात्रां प्रति प्रीत्या मम मात्रा विसर्जितः .. 34 ..
5.130.m: Śāṇḍilī said: / "Having spoken thus, Nārada, the best of sages, then departed / on a pilgrimage to sacred fords, affectionately seen off by my mother.

5.130.s:
mayāpi ca tadādeśātkaumāryepi ca saṃsthayā ..
pūjayā vatsaraṃ yāvatpūjitā patikāmyayā .. 35 ..
5.130.d:
मयापि च तदादेशात्कौमार्येपि च संस्थया ..
पूजया वत्सरं यावत्पूजिता पतिकाम्यया .. 35 ..
5.130.m: And by me also, according to his instruction, staying in maidenhood, / worship was performed for a year with the desire for a husband,

5.130.s:
tṛtīyāyāṃ viśeṣeṇa mārgamāsāditaḥ śubhe ..
naivedyairvividhairdānairgaṃdhamālyānulepanaiḥ .. 36 ..
5.130.d:
तृतीयायां विशेषेण मार्गमासादितः शुभे ..
नैवेद्यैर्विविधैर्दानैर्गंधमाल्यानुलेपनैः .. 36 ..
5.130.m: especially on the third lunar day, beginning in the month of Mārga, O auspicious one, / with various offerings, gifts, fragrant incenses, garlands, and ointments.

5.130.s:
tatprabhāvādayaṃ prāpto jaiminirnāma saddvijaḥ ..
kātyāyani yathā dṛṣṭastvayā kiṃ kīrtitaiḥ paraiḥ .. 37
5.130.d:
तत्प्रभावादयं प्राप्तो जैमिनिर्नाम सद्द्विजः ..
कात्यायनि यथा दृष्टस्त्वया किं कीर्तितैः परैः .. 37
5.130.m: Through its power this excellent brahmin named Jaimini was obtained, / whom you have seen, O Kātyāyanī; what need is there to speak of others?

5.130.s:
tasmāttvamapi kalyāṇi pūjayaināṃ samāhitā ..
saṃprāpsyasi susaubhāgyaṃ maitreyyā sadṛśaṃ śubhe .. 38 ..
5.130.d:
तस्मात्त्वमपि कल्याणि पूजयैनां समाहिता ..
संप्राप्स्यसि सुसौभाग्यं मैत्रेय्या सदृशं शुभे .. 38 ..
5.130.m: Therefore you too, O blessed one, worship her with a concentrated mind; / you will attain great marital fortune equal to Maitreyī, O auspicious one.

5.130.s:
tvayā na pūjitā ceyaṃ kaumārye vartamānayā ..
yāvatsaṃvatsaraṃ gaurī tṛtīyāyāṃ na cādhikam .. 39 ..
5.130.d:
त्वया न पूजिता चेयं कौमार्ये वर्तमानया ..
यावत्संवत्सरं गौरी तृतीयायां न चाधिकम् .. 39 ..
5.130.m: This Gaurī was not worshiped by you while living in maidenhood / for a year on the third lunar day, nor beyond that.

5.130.s:
sāpatnyaṃ tena saṃjātaṃ saubhāgyepi nirargale ..
yathoktavidhinā devī satyametanmayoditam .. 6.131.40 ..
5.130.d:
सापत्न्यं तेन संजातं सौभाग्येपि निरर्गले ..
यथोक्तविधिना देवी सत्यमेतन्मयोदितम् .. 6.131.40 ..
5.130.m: Because of that, cowife rivalry has arisen, even though your marital fortune is unobstructed. / [Worship] the goddess according to the prescribed rite; this truth has been spoken by me."

5.130.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
śrutvā kātyāyanī sarvaṃ śāṃḍilyā yatprakīrtitam ..
tataḥ praṇamya tāṃ pṛṣṭvā svameva bhavanaṃ yayau .. 41 ..
5.130.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
श्रुत्वा कात्यायनी सर्वं शांडिल्या यत्प्रकीर्तितम् ..
ततः प्रणम्य तां पृष्ट्वा स्वमेव भवनं ययौ .. 41 ..
5.130.m: Sūta said: / Having heard all that was proclaimed by Śāṇḍilī, / Kātyāyanī then bowed to her, took her leave, and went to her own house.

5.130.s:
mārgaśīrṣe'tha saṃprāpte tṛtīyādivase site ..
tāṃ devīṃ pūjayāmāsa varṣaṃ yāvakṛtakṣaṇā .. 42 ..
5.130.d:
मार्गशीर्षेऽथ संप्राप्ते तृतीयादिवसे सिते ..
तां देवीं पूजयामास वर्षं यावकृतक्षणा .. 42 ..
5.130.m: Then, when Mārgaśīrṣa arrived, on the third day of the bright fortnight, / she worshiped that goddess for a year, having found her opportunity.

5.130.s:
gauriṇīrbhojayāmāsa mṛṣṭānnairbhojanai rasaiḥ ..
tailakṣāraparityaktairgandhaiḥ kuṃkumapūrvakaiḥ .. 43 ..
5.130.d:
गौरिणीर्भोजयामास मृष्टान्नैर्भोजनै रसैः ..
तैलक्षारपरित्यक्तैर्गन्धैः कुंकुमपूर्वकैः .. 43 ..
5.130.m: She fed married women with delicious foods and savors, / free from oil and salt, and honored them with perfumes beginning with saffron.

5.130.s:
tatastu vatsare pūrṇe yājñavalkyastadantikam ..
gatvā provāca kiṃ kaṣṭaṃ tvaṃ karoṣi śucismite .. 44 ..
5.130.d:
ततस्तु वत्सरे पूर्णे याज्ञवल्क्यस्तदन्तिकम् ..
गत्वा प्रोवाच किं कष्टं त्वं करोषि शुचिस्मिते .. 44 ..
5.130.m: Then, when the year was completed, Yājñavalkya approached her / and said: "What hardship are you undergoing, O you of pure smile,

5.130.s:
mayā kāṃtena raktena kāmadena sadaiva tu ..
tasmādāgaccha gacchāva svameva bhavanaṃ śubhe .. 45 ..
5.130.d:
मया कांतेन रक्तेन कामदेन सदैव तु ..
तस्मादागच्छ गच्छाव स्वमेव भवनं शुभे .. 45 ..
5.130.m: when I am your beloved, impassioned, and always fulfilling your desires? / Therefore come, let us go to our own abode, O auspicious one!"

5.130.s:
evamuktvā tu tāṃ hṛṣṭāṃ gṛhītvā dakṣiṇe kare ..
jagāma bhavanaṃ paścātpulakāṃkitagātrajām .. 46..
5.130.d:
एवमुक्त्वा तु तां हृष्टां गृहीत्वा दक्षिणे करे ..
जगाम भवनं पश्चात्पुलकांकितगात्रजाम् .. 46..
5.130.m: Having spoken thus, he took her, who was joyful and whose limbs were bristling with hair-thrills, / by the right hand and then went to his home.

5.130.s:
tataḥ paraṃ tayā sārdhaṃ vartate harṣitānanaḥ ..
maitreyyā sahito yadvadaviśeṣeṇa sarvadā .. 47 ..
5.130.d:
ततः परं तया सार्धं वर्तते हर्षिताननः ..
मैत्रेय्या सहितो यद्वदविशेषेण सर्वदा .. 47 ..
5.130.m: Thereafter, with a delighted countenance, he lived with her, / just as [he lived] with Maitreyī, always without differentiation.

5.130.s:
tataḥ saṃjanayāmāsa tasyāṃ putraṃ guṇānvitam ..
kātyāyanābhidhānaṃ ca yajña vidyāvicakṣaṇam.. 48 ..
5.130.d:
ततः संजनयामास तस्यां पुत्रं गुणान्वितम् ..
कात्यायनाभिधानं च यज्ञ विद्याविचक्षणम्.. 48 ..
5.130.m: Then upon her he begot a son endowed with virtues, / named Kātyāyana, who was discerning in the knowledge of sacrifice.

5.130.s:
putro vararuciryasya babhūva guṇasāgaraḥ..
sarvajñaḥ sarvakṛtyeṣu vedavedāṃgapāragaḥ ..49..
5.130.d:
पुत्रो वररुचिर्यस्य बभूव गुणसागरः..
सर्वज्ञः सर्वकृत्येषु वेदवेदांगपारगः ..49..
5.130.m: His son was Vararuci, an ocean of virtues, / omniscient in all rites and proficient in the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.

5.130.s:
sthāpito'tra śubhe kṣetre yena vidyārthināṃ kṛte ..
samārādhya viśeṣeṇa caturthyāṃ śuklavāsare .. 6.131.50 ..
5.130.d:
स्थापितोऽत्र शुभे क्षेत्रे येन विद्यार्थिनां कृते ..
समाराध्य विशेषेण चतुर्थ्यां शुक्लवासरे .. 6.131.50 ..
5.130.m: By him, for the sake of seekers of learning, was installed here in this auspicious sacred field, / having worshipped [him] especially on a Friday fourth lunar day,

5.130.s:
mahāgaṇapatirbhaktyā sarvavidyāpradāyakaḥ ..
yastasya purato viprāḥ śāṃtipāṭhavidhānataḥ .. .. 51 ..
5.130.d:
महागणपतिर्भक्त्या सर्वविद्याप्रदायकः ..
यस्तस्य पुरतो विप्राः शांतिपाठविधानतः .. .. 51 ..
5.130.m: the great Gaṇapati, with devotion, the grantor of all learning. / O brahmins, whoever before him, according to the rite of reciting the śānti hymns,

5.130.s:
gṛhṇāti puṣpamālāṃ yaḥ paṭhecchaktyā dvijottamāḥ ..
vedāṃtakṛtsa vipraḥ syātsadā janmanijanmani .. 52 ..
5.130.d:
गृह्णाति पुष्पमालां यः पठेच्छक्त्या द्विजोत्तमाः ..
वेदांतकृत्स विप्रः स्यात्सदा जन्मनिजन्मनि .. 52 ..
5.130.m: takes up a garland of flowers and recites according to his capacity, O best of the twice-born, / that brahmin will always be an author of Vedānta in birth after birth.

5.130.s:
aśaktyā cātha pāṭhasya yo gṛhṇāti dhanena ca ..
sa viśeṣādbhavedvipro vedavedāṃgapāragaḥ .. 53..
5.130.d:
अशक्त्या चाथ पाठस्य यो गृह्णाति धनेन च ..
स विशेषाद्भवेद्विप्रो वेदवेदांगपारगः .. 53..
5.130.m: And if through incapacity for recitation he takes it with money, / that brahmin will especially become proficient in the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.

5.130.s:
viduṣāṃ sa gṛhe janma yājñikānāṃ sadā labhet..
na kadācittu mūrkhārṇāṃ ninditānāṃ kathañcana .. 54 ..
5.130.d:
विदुषां स गृहे जन्म याज्ञिकानां सदा लभेत्..
न कदाचित्तु मूर्खार्णां निन्दितानां कथञ्चन .. 54 ..
5.130.m: He will always obtain birth in the home of learned men who perform sacrifices, / never in any way among fools or censured men.

5.130.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmya īśānotpattipaṃcapiṃḍikāgaurīmāhātmya vararucisthāpitagaṇapatimāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmaikatriṃśaduttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 131 ..
5.130.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्य ईशानोत्पत्तिपंचपिंडिकागौरीमाहात्म्य वररुचिस्थापितगणपतिमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामैकत्रिंशदुत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 131 ..
5.130.m: Thus ends the hundred and thirty-first chapter, named 'Description of the Māhātmya of the Gaṇapati Installed by Vararuci' in the Māhātmya of the Origin of Īśāna and the Five Piṇḍikā-Gaurīs, in the Māhātmya of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the sixth section, the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.131.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ . ..
tvayā sūtaja tatrasthaṃ yājñavalkyasya kīrtitam ..
tīrthaṃ vararuceścaiva vaināyakyaṃ pravidyate .. 1 ..
5.131.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः . ..
त्वया सूतज तत्रस्थं याज्ञवल्क्यस्य कीर्तितम् ..
तीर्थं वररुचेश्चैव वैनायक्यं प्रविद्यते .. 1 ..
5.131.m: The seers said: / O son of Sūta, you have related the sacred ford situated there belonging to Yājñavalkya, / and there exists that of Vararuci dedicated to Vināyaka.

5.131.s:
kātyāyanasya na proktaṃ kiñcittatra mahāmate ..
kiṃ vā tena kṛtaṃ naiva kiṃ vā te vismṛtiṃ gatam .. 2 ..
5.131.d:
कात्यायनस्य न प्रोक्तं किञ्चित्तत्र महामते ..
किं वा तेन कृतं नैव किं वा ते विस्मृतिं गतम् .. 2 ..
5.131.m: Nothing of Kātyāyana has been told there, O high-minded one. / Was nothing indeed done by him, or has it slipped your memory?

5.131.s:
tasmādācakṣva naḥ śīghraṃ yadi kiṃcinmahātmanā ..
kṣetretra nirmitaṃ tīrthaṃ sarvasiddhipradāyakam . 3 ..
5.131.d:
तस्मादाचक्ष्व नः शीघ्रं यदि किंचिन्महात्मना ..
क्षेत्रेत्र निर्मितं तीर्थं सर्वसिद्धिप्रदायकम् . 3 ..
5.131.m: Therefore, declare to us quickly if any sacred ford granting all perfections / was made in this sacred field by that great-souled one.

5.131.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tena vāstupadaṃnāma tatra tīrthavinirmitam ..
kātyāyanena vipreṇa sarvakāmapradaṃ nṛṇām .. 4 ..
5.131.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तेन वास्तुपदंनाम तत्र तीर्थविनिर्मितम् ..
कात्यायनेन विप्रेण सर्वकामप्रदं नृणाम् .. 4 ..
5.131.m: Sūta said: / A sacred ford named Vāstupada was constructed there / by that brahmin Kātyāyana, granting all desires to men,

5.131.s:
catvāriṃśattribhiryuktā devatā yatra paṃca ca ..
pūjyaṃte pūjitāścāpi siddhiṃ yacchaṃti tatkṣaṇāt .. 5 ..
5.131.d:
चत्वारिंशत्त्रिभिर्युक्ता देवता यत्र पंच च ..
पूज्यंते पूजिताश्चापि सिद्धिं यच्छंति तत्क्षणात् .. 5 ..
5.131.m: where forty-five deities / are worshipped, and being worshipped, they bestow perfection that very moment.

5.131.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
kasmāttā devatāḥ sūta pūjyaṃte tatra saṃsthitāḥ ..
nāmataśca vibhāgena kīrtayasva pṛthakpṛthak .. 6 ..
5.131.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
कस्मात्ता देवताः सूत पूज्यंते तत्र संस्थिताः ..
नामतश्च विभागेन कीर्तयस्व पृथक्पृथक् .. 6 ..
5.131.m: The seers said: / Why, O Sūta, are those deities situated there worshipped? / Tell us according to their names and divisions, one by one.

5.131.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
pūrvaṃ kiṃcinmahadbhūtaṃ nirgataṃ dharaṇītalāt ..
apūrvaṃ raudramatyugraṃ kṛṣṇa daṃtaṃ bhayānakam .. 7 ..
5.131.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
पूर्वं किंचिन्महद्भूतं निर्गतं धरणीतलात् ..
अपूर्वं रौद्रमत्युग्रं कृष्ण दंतं भयानकम् .. 7 ..
5.131.m: Sūta said: / Formerly a certain great being emerged from the surface of the earth, / extraordinary, terrible, exceedingly fierce, black-toothed, and terrifying,

5.131.s:
śaṃkukarṇaṃ kṛśāsyaṃ ca ūrdhvakeśaṃ bhayānakam ..
devānāṃ nāśanārthāya mānuṣāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ .. ..
ākṛṣṭaṃ dānaveṃdreṇa maṃtraiḥ śukrapradarśitaiḥ ..
avadhyaṃ sarvaśastrāṇāmastrāṇāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ .. 9 ..
5.131.d:
शंकुकर्णं कृशास्यं च ऊर्ध्वकेशं भयानकम् ..
देवानां नाशनार्थाय मानुषाणां विशेषतः .. ..
आकृष्टं दानवेंद्रेण मंत्रैः शुक्रप्रदर्शितैः ..
अवध्यं सर्वशस्त्राणामस्त्राणां च विशेषतः .. 9 ..
5.131.m: with peg-like ears, an emaciated face, hair standing upright, terrifying, / for the destruction of the gods and especially of men, / drawn forth by the lord of Dānavas through mantras demonstrated by Śukra, / immune to being killed by any weapons, and especially missiles.

5.131.s:
atha devāḥ samālokya tattādṛksubhayāvaham ..
jaghnuḥ śastraiḥ śitaiścitraiḥ kopena mahatānvitāḥ .. 6.132.10 ..
5.131.d:
अथ देवाः समालोक्य तत्तादृक्सुभयावहम् ..
जघ्नुः शस्त्रैः शितैश्चित्रैः कोपेन महतान्विताः .. 6.132.10 ..
5.131.m: Then the gods, seeing that [creature] that was of such a kind and so terrifying, / struck it with various sharp weapons, filled with great wrath.

5.131.s:
naiva śekustadaṃgeṣu prahartuṃ yatnamāsthitāḥ ..
bhakṣyaṃte kevalaṃ tena śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ .. 11 ..
5.131.d:
नैव शेकुस्तदंगेषु प्रहर्तुं यत्नमास्थिताः ..
भक्ष्यंते केवलं तेन शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः .. 11 ..
