5.131.m: They were not able to inflict injury upon its limbs despite their effort; / they were merely devoured by it in their hundreds and thousands.

5.131.s:
atha te yatnamāsthāya sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ ..
brahmāṇamagrataḥ kṛtvā tadbhūtamabhidudruvuḥ .. 12 ..
5.131.d:
अथ ते यत्नमास्थाय सर्वे देवाः सवासवाः ..
ब्रह्माणमग्रतः कृत्वा तद्भूतमभिदुद्रुवुः .. 12 ..
5.131.m: Then, making an effort, all the gods along with Indra, / placing Brahmā in front, ran toward that being.

5.131.s:
tataḥ saṃgṛhya yatnena sarvagātreṣu sarvataḥ ..
tacca paṃcaguṇairdevaiḥ pātitaṃ dharaṇītale.. .. 13 ..
5.131.d:
ततः संगृह्य यत्नेन सर्वगात्रेषु सर्वतः ..
तच्च पंचगुणैर्देवैः पातितं धरणीतले.. .. 13 ..
5.131.m: Then, having seized it with effort on all limbs from all sides, / it was brought down to the surface of the earth by the gods, five times in number.

5.131.s:
upaviṣṭāstatastasya sarve bhūtvā samaṃtataḥ ..
prahārānsaṃprayacchaṃti na lagaṃti ca tasya te .. 14 ..
5.131.d:
उपविष्टास्ततस्तस्य सर्वे भूत्वा समंततः ..
प्रहारान्संप्रयच्छंति न लगंति च तस्य ते .. 14 ..
5.131.m: Thereupon, all of them having sat upon it from every side, / delivered blows, but they did not take effect on it.

5.131.s:
ātharvaṇena sūktena jātaṃ cāmṛtabiṃdunā ..
tadbhūtaṃ preṣitaṃ daityairmuṃḍena ca tadaṃtikam.. 15 ..
5.131.d:
आथर्वणेन सूक्तेन जातं चामृतबिंदुना ..
तद्भूतं प्रेषितं दैत्यैर्मुंडेन च तदंतिकम्.. 15 ..
5.131.m: Born through an Atharvan hymn and a drop of nectar, / that being had been dispatched by the Daityas and by Muṇḍa into their presence.

5.131.s:
evaṃ varṣasahasrāṃtaṃ tattathaiva vyavasthitam .
na muṃcaṃti bhayātte tu na haṃtuṃ śaknuvaṃti ca .. 16 ..
5.131.d:
एवं वर्षसहस्रांतं तत्तथैव व्यवस्थितम् .
न मुंचंति भयात्ते तु न हंतुं शक्नुवंति च .. 16 ..
5.131.m: In this way, for up to a thousand years, it remained just so; / out of fear they did not release it, nor were they able to kill it.

5.131.s:
tasyodare sthito brahmā śakrādyā amarāśca ye ..
caturdikṣu sthitāḥ kruddhā mahadyatnena saṃsthitāḥ ..
tataste dānavāḥ sarve maṃtraṃ cakruḥ parasparam .. 17 ..
5.131.d:
तस्योदरे स्थितो ब्रह्मा शक्राद्या अमराश्च ये ..
चतुर्दिक्षु स्थिताः क्रुद्धा महद्यत्नेन संस्थिताः ..
ततस्ते दानवाः सर्वे मंत्रं चक्रुः परस्परम् .. 17 ..
5.131.m: Brahmā stood on its belly, and the immortals beginning with Indra / stood in the four quarters, enraged, maintaining their positions with great effort. / Then all those Dānavas took counsel with one another:

5.131.s:
asya bhūtasya raudrasya śukrasṛṣṭasya tatkṣaṇāt ..
eka evātra nirdiṣṭa upāyo devasaṃkṣayaḥ . 18 ..
5.131.d:
अस्य भूतस्य रौद्रस्य शुक्रसृष्टस्य तत्क्षणात् ..
एक एवात्र निर्दिष्ट उपायो देवसंक्षयः . 18 ..
5.131.m: "For this fierce being created by Śukra, / the destruction of the gods has been pointed out as the only remedy here immediately."

5.131.s:
tataḥ śastrāṇi tīkṣṇāni dānavāste mahābalāḥ ..
muṃcaṃto vividhānnādānsamājagmuḥ sahasraśaḥ .. 19 ..
5.131.d:
ततः शस्त्राणि तीक्ष्णानि दानवास्ते महाबलाः ..
मुंचंतो विविधान्नादान्समाजग्मुः सहस्रशः .. 19 ..
5.131.m: Then those mighty Dānavas, releasing sharp weapons / and emitting various cries, arrived by the thousands.

5.131.s:
etasminnaṃtare viṣṇurāgatastatra tatkṣaṇāt ..
āha bhūtaṃ tadā viṣṇurvacasā hlādayanniva .. 6.132.20 ..
5.131.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे विष्णुरागतस्तत्र तत्क्षणात् ..
आह भूतं तदा विष्णुर्वचसा ह्लादयन्निव .. 6.132.20 ..
5.131.m: In the meantime Viṣṇu arrived there that very moment. / Then Viṣṇu spoke to the being, as if gladdening it with his speech:

5.131.s:
yo yasminsaṃsthito gātre devastava samudbhave ..
tatra pūjāṃ samādāya tasmāttvāṃ tarpayiṣyati ..21..
5.131.d:
यो यस्मिन्संस्थितो गात्रे देवस्तव समुद्भवे ..
तत्र पूजां समादाय तस्मात्त्वां तर्पयिष्यति ..21..
5.131.m: "Whichsoever god is situated upon whichsoever limb of yours, O being, / having received worship there, he will satisfy you with that.

5.131.s:
naivaṃvidhā tu loke'sminpūjā devasya saṃsthitā ..
kasyacidyādṛśī te'dya mayā saṃpratipāditā .. 22 ..
5.131.d:
नैवंविधा तु लोकेऽस्मिन्पूजा देवस्य संस्थिता ..
कस्यचिद्यादृशी तेऽद्य मया संप्रतिपादिता .. 22 ..
5.131.m: No worship of any god in this world has ever been established / of such a kind as has been granted to you today by me."

5.131.s:
tatastena pratijñātamavikalpena? cetasā..
evaṃ te'haṃ kariṣyāmi paraṃ me vacanaṃ śṛṇu .. 23 ..
5.131.d:
ततस्तेन प्रतिज्ञातमविकल्पेन? चेतसा..
एवं तेऽहं करिष्यामि परं मे वचनं शृणु .. 23 ..
5.131.m: Then it agreed with an unwavering mind: / "I shall do thus for you, but listen to my condition:

5.131.s:
yadi kaścinna me pūjāṃ kariṣyati kadācana ..
kathaṃcinmānavaḥ kaścitsa me bhakṣyo bhaviṣyati .. 24 ..
5.131.d:
यदि कश्चिन्न मे पूजां करिष्यति कदाचन ..
कथंचिन्मानवः कश्चित्स मे भक्ष्यो भविष्यति .. 24 ..
5.131.m: If anyone does not perform worship to me at any time, / any such human being shall become my food."

5.131.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
bāḍhamityeva ca prokte tato devena cakriṇā ..
tadbhūtaṃ niścalaṃ jātaṃ harṣeṇa mahatānvitam .. 25 ..
5.131.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
बाढमित्येव च प्रोक्ते ततो देवेन चक्रिणा ..
तद्भूतं निश्चलं जातं हर्षेण महतान्वितम् .. 25 ..
5.131.m: Sūta said: / When "So be it!" was indeed uttered by the discus-bearing deity, / that being became motionless, filled with great joy.

5.131.s:
tato devāḥ samutthāya tattyaktvā śastrapāṇayaḥ ..
jaghnuśca niśitaiḥ śastraiḥ palāyanasamutsukān ..
lajjāhīnāngatāmarṣāndīnavākyaprajalpakān .. 26 ..
5.131.d:
ततो देवाः समुत्थाय तत्त्यक्त्वा शस्त्रपाणयः ..
जघ्नुश्च निशितैः शस्त्रैः पलायनसमुत्सुकान् ..
लज्जाहीनान्गतामर्षान्दीनवाक्यप्रजल्पकान् .. 26 ..
5.131.m: Then the gods, having arisen and left it, with weapons in hand, / struck with sharp weapons those who were eager to flee, / devoid of shame, devoid of anger, uttering wretched words.

5.131.s:
tataḥ svasthaḥ sa bhūtvā tu harirdaityairnipātitaiḥ ..
provāca padmajaṃ nāma bhūtasyāsya kuruṣva bhoḥ .. 27 ..
5.131.d:
ततः स्वस्थः स भूत्वा तु हरिर्दैत्यैर्निपातितैः ..
प्रोवाच पद्मजं नाम भूतस्यास्य कुरुष्व भोः .. 27 ..
5.131.m: Then Hari, having become calm once the Daityas were brought down, / said to the lotus-born [Brahmā]: "Sir, give a name to this being."

5.131.s:
.. brahmovāca ... ..
anena tava vākyasya proktaṃ vākyaṃ hare yataḥ ..
vāstvetaditi yasmācca tasmādvāstu bhaviṣyati .. 28 ..
5.131.d:
.. ब्रह्मोवाच ... ..
अनेन तव वाक्यस्य प्रोक्तं वाक्यं हरे यतः ..
वास्त्वेतदिति यस्माच्च तस्माद्वास्तु भविष्यति .. 28 ..
5.131.m: Brahmā said: / "Since in response to your word, O Hari, his word was spoken, / and since [he said] 'this should be a settlement' (vāstu), therefore he will be Vāstu."

5.131.s:
evamuktvā hṛṣīkeśa āhūya viśvakarmaṇe ..
vidhānaṃ kathayāmāsa pūjārthaṃ vistarānvitam .. 29 ..
5.131.d:
एवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेश आहूय विश्वकर्मणे ..
विधानं कथयामास पूजार्थं विस्तरान्वितम् .. 29 ..
5.131.m: Having spoken thus, Hṛṣīkeśa summoned Viśvakarman / and declared in detail the rule for its worship.

5.131.s:
etasminnaṃtare prāha yājñavalkyasutaḥ sudhīḥ ..
viśvakarmāṇamāhūya prathamaṃ dvijasattamāḥ .. 6.132.30 ..
5.131.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे प्राह याज्ञवल्क्यसुतः सुधीः ..
विश्वकर्माणमाहूय प्रथमं द्विजसत्तमाः .. 6.132.30 ..
5.131.m: In the meantime, the wise son of Yājñavalkya, / having first summoned Viśvakarman, O best of the twice-born, said:

5.131.s:
hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre mamāśramapadaṃ kuru ..
anenaiva vidhānena proktena tu mahāmate .. 31 ..
5.131.d:
हाटकेश्वरजे क्षेत्रे ममाश्रमपदं कुरु ..
अनेनैव विधानेन प्रोक्तेन तु महामते .. 31 ..
5.131.m: "In the sacred field arising from Hāṭakeśvara, construct my hermitage / according to this very rule that was spoken, O high-minded one!"

5.131.s:
tatohaṃ sakalaṃ buddhvā vṛddhiṃ neṣyāmi bhūtale ..
bālāvabodhanārthāya tasmādāgaccha satvaram .. 32 ..
5.131.d:
ततोहं सकलं बुद्ध्वा वृद्धिं नेष्यामि भूतले ..
बालावबोधनार्थाय तस्मादागच्छ सत्वरम् .. 32 ..
5.131.m: "Then, understanding it completely, I shall propagate it on the earth / for the instruction of the ignorant; therefore, come quickly."

5.131.s:
tataḥ saṃpreṣayāmāsa taṃ brahmāpi tadaṃtikam ..
viśvakarmāṇamāhūya svasutasya hite sthitaḥ .. 33 ..
5.131.d:
ततः संप्रेषयामास तं ब्रह्मापि तदंतिकम् ..
विश्वकर्माणमाहूय स्वसुतस्य हिते स्थितः .. 33 ..
5.131.m: Then Brahmā also sent him into his presence, / having summoned Viśvakarman, intent on the welfare of his son.

5.131.s:
viśvakarmāpi tatraitya vāstupūjāṃ yathoditām ..
cakāra brahmaṇā proktāṃ yādṛśīṃ sakalāṃ tataḥ .. 34..
5.131.d:
विश्वकर्मापि तत्रैत्य वास्तुपूजां यथोदिताम् ..
चकार ब्रह्मणा प्रोक्तां यादृशीं सकलां ततः .. 34..
5.131.m: Viśvakarman too, having arrived there, performed the site-worship as prescribed, / all of it just as was spoken by Brahmā.

5.131.s:
kātyāyano'pi tāṃ sarvāṃ dṛṣṭvā cakre sahasraśaḥ ..
tadā viśvahitārthāya śālākarmādi pūrvikām .. . 35 ..
5.131.d:
कात्यायनोऽपि तां सर्वां दृष्ट्वा चक्रे सहस्रशः ..
तदा विश्वहितार्थाय शालाकर्मादि पूर्विकाम् .. . 35 ..
5.131.m: Kātyāyana also, having seen all of it, then performed it thousands of times / for the welfare of the world, beginning with the construction of halls and the like.

5.131.s:
evaṃ vāstupadaṃ jātaṃ tasminkṣetre dvijottamāḥ ..
asminkṣetre naraḥ pāpātspṛṣṭo mucyeta karmaṇā .. 36 ..
5.131.d:
एवं वास्तुपदं जातं तस्मिन्क्षेत्रे द्विजोत्तमाः ..
अस्मिन्क्षेत्रे नरः पापात्स्पृष्टो मुच्येत कर्मणा .. 36 ..
5.131.m: Thus the sacred site for building came to be in that sacred field, O best of brahmins. / In this sacred field, a man touched by sin is freed by this rite.

5.131.s:
tathā na prāpnuyāddoṣaṃ gṛhajātaṃ kathaṃcana ..
śilpotthaṃ kupadotthaṃ ca kuvāstujamathāpi ca .. 37 ..
5.131.d:
तथा न प्राप्नुयाद्दोषं गृहजातं कथंचन ..
शिल्पोत्थं कुपदोत्थं च कुवास्तुजमथापि च .. 37 ..
5.131.m: Likewise, he will never incur any fault arising from a house, / whether arising from craftsmanship, from an improper site, or from improper construction.

5.131.s:
vaiśākhasya tṛtīyāyāṃ śuklāyāṃ rohiṇīṣu ca ..
tatpadaṃ nihitaṃ tatra vāstostena mahātmanā .. 38 ..
5.131.d:
वैशाखस्य तृतीयायां शुक्लायां रोहिणीषु च ..
तत्पदं निहितं तत्र वास्तोस्तेन महात्मना .. 38 ..
5.131.m: On the third lunar day of the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha, under the asterism Rohiṇī, / that sacred site of building was established there by that great-souled one.

5.131.s:
tasminnapi ca yaḥ pūjāṃ tenaiva vidhinā naraḥ ..
tasya yaḥ kurute samyaksa bhūpatvamavāpnuyāt .. 39 ..
5.131.d:
तस्मिन्नपि च यः पूजां तेनैव विधिना नरः ..
तस्य यः कुरुते सम्यक्स भूपत्वमवाप्नुयात् .. 39 ..
5.131.m: And whatever man properly performs worship there according to that very rite, / he shall attain kingship.

5.131.s:
gṛhaṃ doṣānvitaṃ prāpya śilpādibhirupadrutam ..
tasyopasaṃgamaṃ prāpya samṛddhiṃ yāti taddine .. 6.132.40 ..
5.131.d:
गृहं दोषान्वितं प्राप्य शिल्पादिभिरुपद्रुतम् ..
तस्योपसंगमं प्राप्य समृद्धिं याति तद्दिने .. 6.132.40 ..
5.131.m: Having acquired a house beset with faults and troubled by defects of craftsmanship and the like, / he attains prosperity on that very day upon approaching it.

5.131.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgara khaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye vāstupadotpattimāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma dvātriṃśaduttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 132 ..
5.131.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागर खण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये वास्तुपदोत्पत्तिमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम द्वात्रिंशदुत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 132 ..
5.131.m: Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-second chapter, entitled 'Description of the Glory of the Origin of the Sacred Site for Building', in the Glory of Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section], in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.132.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tathā'nyāpi ca tatrāsti devatā dvijasattamāḥ ..
ajāgṛheti vikhyātā sarvarogakṣayāvahā .. 1 ..
5.132.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तथाऽन्यापि च तत्रास्ति देवता द्विजसत्तमाः ..
अजागृहेति विख्याता सर्वरोगक्षयावहा .. 1 ..
5.132.m: Sūta said: / Likewise, there is also another deity there, O best of brahmins, / renowned as Ajāgṛhā, who brings about the destruction of all diseases.

5.132.s:
ajāpālo yadā rājā sarvalokahite rataḥ ..
ajārūpāḥ prayāṃti sma vyādhayaḥ sakalā dvijāḥ ..
tadā rātrau samānīya tasminsthāne dadhāti saḥ .. 2 ..
5.132.d:
अजापालो यदा राजा सर्वलोकहिते रतः ..
अजारूपाः प्रयांति स्म व्याधयः सकला द्विजाः ..
तदा रात्रौ समानीय तस्मिन्स्थाने दधाति सः .. 2 ..
5.132.m: When Ajāpāla was king, devoted to the welfare of all people, / all diseases, O brahmins, went about in the form of she-goats; / then, having brought them together at night, he kept them in that place.

5.132.s:
tatastadāśrayātsthānamajāgṛhamiti smṛtam ..
sarvairjanairdharā pṛṣṭhedarśanādvyādhināśanam .. 3 ..
5.132.d:
ततस्तदाश्रयात्स्थानमजागृहमिति स्मृतम् ..
सर्वैर्जनैर्धरा पृष्ठेदर्शनाद्व्याधिनाशनम् .. 3 ..
5.132.m: Therefore, because of that shelter, the place was remembered as Ajāgṛha / by all people on the surface of the earth, destroying disease merely by darśana.

5.132.s:
tatraiśvaryamabhūtpūrvaṃ yattadbrāhmaṇasattamāḥ ..
ahaṃ vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi śrotavyaṃ susamāhitaiḥ .. 4 ..
5.132.d:
तत्रैश्वर्यमभूत्पूर्वं यत्तद्ब्राह्मणसत्तमाः ..
अहं वः कीर्तयिष्यामि श्रोतव्यं सुसमाहितैः .. 4 ..
5.132.m: The sovereign power that existed there of old, O best of brahmins, / that I shall recount to you; it should be listened to with concentrated minds.

5.132.s:
tatrāgato dvijaḥ kaścitkṣetre tāpasarūpadhṛk ..
tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena rātrau prāptaḥ śramānvitaḥ .. 5 ..
5.132.d:
तत्रागतो द्विजः कश्चित्क्षेत्रे तापसरूपधृक् ..
तीर्थयात्राप्रसंगेन रात्रौ प्राप्तः श्रमान्वितः .. 5 ..
5.132.m: A certain brahmin, bearing the appearance of an ascetic, arrived in that sacred field; / having arrived at night while on a pilgrimage to sacred fords, he was overcome with fatigue.

5.132.s:
ajāvṛṃdamathālokya niviṣṭaṃ susukhānvitam ..
romaṃtha karmasaṃyuktaṃ viśvastamakutobhayam.. 6 ..
5.132.d:
अजावृंदमथालोक्य निविष्टं सुसुखान्वितम् ..
रोमंथ कर्मसंयुक्तं विश्वस्तमकुतोभयम्.. 6 ..
5.132.m: Then, seeing a flock of she-goats settled very comfortably, / engaged in chewing the cud, confident, and free from any fear,

5.132.s:
sa jñātvā mānuṣeṇātra bhavitavyamasaṃśayam ..
na śūnyāḥ paśavo rātrau sthāsyaṃti vijane vane .. 7 ..
5.132.d:
स ज्ञात्वा मानुषेणात्र भवितव्यमसंशयम् ..
न शून्याः पशवो रात्रौ स्थास्यंति विजने वने .. 7 ..
5.132.m: he, knowing that 'a human being must surely be here— / unattended animals will not remain at night in a deserted forest'—

5.132.s:
tataḥ phūtkṛtya phūkṛtya divaṃ yāvanna saṃdadhe ..
kaścidvācaṃ prasuptaśca tāvattatraiva ciṃtayan .. 8 ..
5.132.d:
ततः फूत्कृत्य फूकृत्य दिवं यावन्न संदधे ..
कश्चिद्वाचं प्रसुप्तश्च तावत्तत्रैव चिंतयन् .. 8 ..
5.132.m: then called out aloud, and as long as no one answered with a word, / he fell asleep right there, thinking:

5.132.s:
avaśyaṃ mānuṣeṇātra paśūnāṃ rakṣaṇāya ca ..
āgaṃtavyaṃ kuto'pyāśu tasmāttiṣṭhāmi nirbhayaḥ .. 9 ..
5.132.d:
अवश्यं मानुषेणात्र पशूनां रक्षणाय च ..
आगंतव्यं कुतोऽप्याशु तस्मात्तिष्ठामि निर्भयः .. 9 ..
5.132.m: "Surely a human being must come here soon from somewhere / to protect the animals; therefore, I shall remain without fear."

5.132.s:
evaṃ tasya prasuptasya gatā sā rajanī tataḥ ..
tatastvaritavattasya suśrāṃtasya dvijottamāḥ .. 6.133.10 ..
5.132.d:
एवं तस्य प्रसुप्तस्य गता सा रजनी ततः ..
ततस्त्वरितवत्तस्य सुश्रांतस्य द्विजोत्तमाः .. 6.133.10 ..
5.132.m: While he was thus fast asleep, that night passed away, / and then it seemed quick to him, being thoroughly exhausted, O best of brahmins.

5.132.s:
atha yāvatprabhāte sa prapaśyati nijāṃ tanum ..
tāvatkuṣṭhādibhī rogaiḥ samaṃtātparivāritām .. 11 ..
5.132.d:
अथ यावत्प्रभाते स प्रपश्यति निजां तनुम् ..
तावत्कुष्ठादिभी रोगैः समंतात्परिवारिताम् .. 11 ..
5.132.m: Now, as soon as he looked at his own body at dawn, / it was completely encompassed on all sides by diseases such as leprosy.

5.132.s:
aśaktaścalituṃ sthānādapi caikaṃ padaṃ kvacit ..
tejo hīno'pi raudreṇa cintayāmāsa vai tataḥ .. 12 ..
5.132.d:
अशक्तश्चलितुं स्थानादपि चैकं पदं क्वचित् ..
तेजो हीनोऽपि रौद्रेण चिन्तयामास वै ततः .. 12 ..
5.132.m: Unable to move even a single step from that place, / bereft of vigor by the fierce [affliction], he then reflected:

5.132.s:
kimidaṃ kāraṇaṃ yena mamaiṣā saṃsthitā tanuḥ ..
akasmādeva rogo'yaṃ calituṃ naiva ca kṣamaḥ ..13..
5.132.d:
किमिदं कारणं येन ममैषा संस्थिता तनुः ..
अकस्मादेव रोगोऽयं चलितुं नैव च क्षमः ..13..
5.132.m: "What is this reason on account of which my body has become like this? / This disease [has appeared] all of a sudden, and I am not able to move at all."

5.132.s:
evaṃ cintayamānasya tasya viprasya tatkṣaṇāt..
dvādaśārkapratīkāśaḥ puruṣaḥ samupāgataḥ .. 14 ..
5.132.d:
एवं चिन्तयमानस्य तस्य विप्रस्य तत्क्षणात्..
द्वादशार्कप्रतीकाशः पुरुषः समुपागतः .. 14 ..
5.132.m: While that brahmin was reflecting thus, at that very moment / a man resembling twelve suns approached.

5.132.s:
taṃ yūthaṃ kālayāmāsa tataḥ saṃjñābhirāhvayan ..
pṛthaktvena samādāya yaṣṭiṃ savyena pāṇinā .. 15 ..
5.132.d:
तं यूथं कालयामास ततः संज्ञाभिराह्वयन् ..
पृथक्त्वेन समादाय यष्टिं सव्येन पाणिना .. 15 ..
5.132.m: He then drove that flock, calling them by their names individually, / holding a staff in his left hand.

5.132.s:
athāpaśyatsa taṃ vipraṃ vyādhibhiḥ sarvato vṛtam..
aśaktaṃ calituṃ kvāpi tataḥ provāca sādaram..16..
5.132.d:
अथापश्यत्स तं विप्रं व्याधिभिः सर्वतो वृतम्..
अशक्तं चलितुं क्वापि ततः प्रोवाच सादरम्..16..
5.132.m: Then he saw that brahmin surrounded on all sides by diseases, / unable to move anywhere; then he respectfully spoke:

5.132.s:
kastvamevaṃvidhaḥ prāptaḥ sthāne cātra dvijottama ..
nāsti rājye mama vyādhiḥ kasyacitkutracitsphuṭam .. 17..
5.132.d:
कस्त्वमेवंविधः प्राप्तः स्थाने चात्र द्विजोत्तम ..
नास्ति राज्ये मम व्याधिः कस्यचित्कुत्रचित्स्फुटम् .. 17..
5.132.m: "Who are you that have arrived in such a state at this place, O best of brahmins? / In my kingdom, there is clearly no disease for anyone anywhere.

5.132.s:
ajonāma narendro'haṃ yadi te śrotramāgataḥ..
vyādhīṃśca cchāgarūpeṇa rakṣāmi janakāraṇāt ..18..
5.132.d:
अजोनाम नरेन्द्रोऽहं यदि ते श्रोत्रमागतः..
व्याधींश्च च्छागरूपेण रक्षामि जनकारणात् ..18..
5.132.m: I am the king named Aja, if this has reached your ears; / and I keep diseases in the form of goats for the sake of the people.

5.132.s:
tasmādbrūhi śarīrastho yaste vyādhirvyavasthitaḥ ..
yenā'haṃ nigrahaṃ tasya karomi dvijasattama .19..
5.132.d:
तस्माद्ब्रूहि शरीरस्थो यस्ते व्याधिर्व्यवस्थितः ..
येनाऽहं निग्रहं तस्य करोमि द्विजसत्तम .19..
5.132.m: Therefore, declare the disease that has settled in your body, / so that I may subdue it, O best of brahmins."

5.132.s:
.. brāhmaṇa uvāca .. ..
tīrthayātrāparo'haṃ ca bhramāmi kṣitimaṃḍale..
krameṇā'tra samāyātaḥ kṣetre'sminhāṭakeśvare .. 6.133.20 ..
5.132.d:
.. ब्राह्मण उवाच .. ..
तीर्थयात्रापरोऽहं च भ्रमामि क्षितिमंडले..
क्रमेणाऽत्र समायातः क्षेत्रेऽस्मिन्हाटकेश्वरे .. 6.133.20 ..
5.132.m: The brahmin said: / "Devoted to pilgrimages to sacred fords, I wander upon the earth; / in due course, I have arrived here in this sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara.

5.132.s:
niśāvaktre nṛpaśreṣṭha vāsaḥ saṃciṃtito mayā ..
dṛṣṭvā'mūṃśca paśūnbhūpa mānuṣaṃ bhāvyameva hi .. 21 ..
5.132.d:
निशावक्त्रे नृपश्रेष्ठ वासः संचिंतितो मया ..
दृष्ट्वाऽमूंश्च पशून्भूप मानुषं भाव्यमेव हि .. 21 ..
5.132.m: At the beginning of night, O best of kings, dwelling was sought by me; / and having seen these animals, O king, a human presence seemed certain.

5.132.s: tataścātra prasupto'haṃ paśūnāmaṃtike nṛpa ..22..
5.132.d: ततश्चात्र प्रसुप्तोऽहं पशूनामंतिके नृप ..22..
5.132.m: And then I fell asleep here near the animals, O king.

5.132.s:
atha yāvatprabhāte'haṃ prapaśyāmi nijāṃ tanum..
tāvatkuṣṭhādirogaiśca samaṃtātparivāritām .. 23 ..
5.132.d:
अथ यावत्प्रभातेऽहं प्रपश्यामि निजां तनुम्..
तावत्कुष्ठादिरोगैश्च समंतात्परिवारिताम् .. 23 ..
5.132.m: Now, as soon as I looked at my own body at dawn, / it was completely surrounded on all sides by diseases such as leprosy.

5.132.s:
nānyatkiṃcinnṛpaśreṣṭha kāraṇaṃ vedmi tattvataḥ ..
kimetena nṛpaśreṣṭha bhūyobhūyaḥ prajalpatā ..
bahutvātkuru tasmānme yathā syānnīrujā tanuḥ.. 24 ..
5.132.d:
नान्यत्किंचिन्नृपश्रेष्ठ कारणं वेद्मि तत्त्वतः ..
किमेतेन नृपश्रेष्ठ भूयोभूयः प्रजल्पता ..
बहुत्वात्कुरु तस्मान्मे यथा स्यान्नीरुजा तनुः.. 24 ..
5.132.m: I know of no other cause in truth, O best of kings. / What is the use of prattling on and on, O best of kings, / with so many words? Therefore, make my body free from disease!"

5.132.s:
tataste vyādhayaḥ proktā ajāpālena bhūbhujā ..
kenājñā khaṃḍitā me'dya ko vadhyaḥ sāṃprataṃ mama .. 25 ..
5.132.d:
ततस्ते व्याधयः प्रोक्ता अजापालेन भूभुजा ..
केनाज्ञा खंडिता मेऽद्य को वध्यः सांप्रतं मम .. 25 ..
5.132.m: Then those diseases were addressed by King Ajāpāla: / "By whom has my command been broken today? Who deserves to be put to death by me now?"

5.132.s:
.. vyādhaya ūcuḥ .. ..
mā kopaṃ kuru bhūpāla kṛtye'smiṃstvaṃ kathaṃcana ..
yasmādeṣa dvijo viṣṭaḥ sāṃprataṃ vyādhibhistribhiḥ ..26...
5.132.d:
.. व्याधय ऊचुः .. ..
मा कोपं कुरु भूपाल कृत्येऽस्मिंस्त्वं कथंचन ..
यस्मादेष द्विजो विष्टः सांप्रतं व्याधिभिस्त्रिभिः ..26...
5.132.m: The diseases said: / "Do not become angry at all in this matter, O king, / for this brahmin has now been entered by three diseases:

5.132.s:
rājayakṣmā ca kuṣṭhaṃ ca pāmā ca dvijasattama ..
ete saṃsargajā doṣāstrayo'dyāpi prakīrtitāḥ .. 27 ..
5.132.d:
राजयक्ष्मा च कुष्ठं च पामा च द्विजसत्तम ..
एते संसर्गजा दोषास्त्रयोऽद्यापि प्रकीर्तिताः .. 27 ..
5.132.m: consumption, leprosy, and scabies, O best of brahmins. / These three faults are declared even today to arise from contact.

5.132.s:
eteṣāṃ prathamau yau dvau nivṛttirahitau smṛtau ..
auṣadhaiścaiva maṃtraiśca śeṣā nāśaṃ vrajaṃti ca ..28..
5.132.d:
एतेषां प्रथमौ यौ द्वौ निवृत्तिरहितौ स्मृतौ ..
औषधैश्चैव मंत्रैश्च शेषा नाशं व्रजंति च ..28..
5.132.m: Of these, the first two are traditionally considered incurable; / but the remaining ones go to destruction through medicines and mantras.

5.132.s:
ābhyāṃ ca brahmaśāposti yena nāsti nivartanam ..
tasmādatra nṛpaśreṣṭha kuru yatte kṣamaṃ bhavet ..29...
5.132.d:
आभ्यां च ब्रह्मशापोस्ति येन नास्ति निवर्तनम् ..
तस्मादत्र नृपश्रेष्ठ कुरु यत्ते क्षमं भवेत् ..29...
5.132.m: And in these two there is a brahmin's curse, because of which there is no removal; / therefore, O best of kings, do what may be suitable here.

5.132.s:
etena brāhmaṇenaite spṛṣṭā rājaṃstrayopi ca..
tasmāttāvattanuṃ cāsyāviśatāṃ tāvasaṃśayam..6.133.30..
aparaṃ śṛṇu bhūpāla vacanaṃ no mukhāccyutam..
hitāya sarvajaṃtūnāṃ tava śreyovivṛddhaye..3...
5.132.d:
एतेन ब्राह्मणेनैते स्पृष्टा राजंस्त्रयोपि च..
तस्मात्तावत्तनुं चास्याविशतां तावसंशयम्..6.133.30..
अपरं शृणु भूपाल वचनं नो मुखाच्च्युतम्..
हिताय सर्वजंतूनां तव श्रेयोविवृद्धये..3...
5.132.m:
All three of these were touched by this brahmin, O king; / therefore, those two have undoubtedly entered his body.
Hear another word, O king, fallen from our mouths / for the benefit of all creatures and for the increase of your welfare:

5.132.s:
yatra sthānaṃ ciraṃ tatra medinyāṃ vihitaṃ nṛpa.
purīṣaṃ ca samāviddhā tenaiṣā medinī drutam..32..
5.132.d:
यत्र स्थानं चिरं तत्र मेदिन्यां विहितं नृप.
पुरीषं च समाविद्धा तेनैषा मेदिनी द्रुतम्..32..
5.132.m: Where a place has been maintained on the earth for a long time, O king, / this earth quickly becomes filled with excrement."

5.132.s:
kālāṃtarepi ye martyā bhūmyāmasyāṃ samāgatāḥ.
bhūmeḥ sparśaṃ kariṣyaṃti te bhaviṣyaṃti cedṛśāḥ..33..
5.132.d:
कालांतरेपि ये मर्त्या भूम्यामस्यां समागताः.
भूमेः स्पर्शं करिष्यंति ते भविष्यंति चेदृशाः..33..
5.132.m:
"In the course of time, whichever mortals arrive on this ground
and touch the ground, will likewise become such."

5.132.s:
vayaṃ śeṣā mahārāja vyādhayo ye vyavasthitāḥ.
tvayā muktvā bhaviṣyāmo mantrauṣadhavaśānugāḥ ..34..
5.132.d:
वयं शेषा महाराज व्याधयो ये व्यवस्थिताः.
त्वया मुक्त्वा भविष्यामो मन्त्रौषधवशानुगाः ..34..
5.132.m:
"The rest of us diseases who remain, O great king,
released by you, will become subject to mantras and medicinal herbs."

5.132.s: naitau punastu durgrāhyau brahmaśāpa samudbhavau ..35..
5.132.d: नैतौ पुनस्तु दुर्ग्राह्यौ ब्रह्मशाप समुद्भवौ ..35..
5.132.m: "These two, however, arising from a brahmin's curse, are difficult to curb."

5.132.s:
tacchrutvā pārthivaḥ so'pi tasminsthāne vyavasthitaḥ ..
taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ punaḥ prāha na bhetavyaṃ tvayā dvija .. 36 ..
5.132.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा पार्थिवः सोऽपि तस्मिन्स्थाने व्यवस्थितः ..
तं ब्राह्मणं पुनः प्राह न भेतव्यं त्वया द्विज .. 36 ..
5.132.m:
Having heard that, the king, remaining in that place,
spoke again to that brahmin: "Do not fear, O twice-born.

5.132.s:
ahaṃ tvāṃ rakṣayiṣyāmi vyādherasmātsudāruṇāt ..
atra tasmātpratīkṣasva kañcitkālaṃ mamājñayā .. 37 ...
5.132.d:
अहं त्वां रक्षयिष्यामि व्याधेरस्मात्सुदारुणात् ..
अत्र तस्मात्प्रतीक्षस्व कञ्चित्कालं ममाज्ञया .. 37 ...
5.132.m:
I will protect you from this terrible disease;
therefore, wait here for some time by my command."

5.132.s:
evamuktvā tataścakre tadarthaṃ sumahattapaḥ ..
ārādhayanprabhaktyā ca samyaktāṃ kṣetradevatām ..38..
5.132.d:
एवमुक्त्वा ततश्चक्रे तदर्थं सुमहत्तपः ..
आराधयन्प्रभक्त्या च सम्यक्तां क्षेत्रदेवताम् ..38..
5.132.m:
Having spoken thus, he then performed great austerity for that purpose,
worshipping that deity of the sacred field with deep devotion and in the proper manner,

5.132.s:
muṃḍenātharvaśīrṣeṇa divārātramataṃdritaḥ..
kṣetrapālotthasūktena vāstusūktena ca dvijāḥ..39..
siddhārthai raktapuṣpaiśca guggulena sudhūpitaiḥ..
homaṃ kurvannṛpaḥ paścānnīlarudrānviśeṣataḥ..6.133.4...
5.132.d:
मुंडेनाथर्वशीर्षेण दिवारात्रमतंद्रितः..
क्षेत्रपालोत्थसूक्तेन वास्तुसूक्तेन च द्विजाः..39..
सिद्धार्थै रक्तपुष्पैश्च गुग्गुलेन सुधूपितैः..
होमं कुर्वन्नृपः पश्चान्नीलरुद्रान्विशेषतः..6.133.4...
5.132.m:
day and night without slackening, O brahmins, with the Muṇḍa-[Upaniṣad], the Atharvaśīrṣa,
with the hymn to the Guardian of the Field, and with the hymn to the Vāstu,
offering oblation with white mustard seeds, red flowers, and well-fumigated bdellium gum,
the king then especially [reciting] the Nīlarudras.

5.132.s:
atha naktāvasānena tasya homasya cotthitā..
bhittvā dharātalaṃ devī mantrākṛṣṭā vinirgatā..41..
5.132.d:
अथ नक्तावसानेन तस्य होमस्य चोत्थिता..
भित्त्वा धरातलं देवी मन्त्राकृष्टा विनिर्गता..41..
5.132.m:
Then, at the end of the night, arising from that oblation,
the goddess burst through the surface of the earth and emerged, drawn by the mantras.

5.132.s: devatā tasya kṣetrasya tataḥ provāca taṃ nṛpam..42..
5.132.d: देवता तस्य क्षेत्रस्य ततः प्रोवाच तं नृपम्..42..
5.132.m: Then the deity of that sacred field spoke to that king:

5.132.s:
ekāhaṃ tava bhūpāla homasyāsya prabhāvataḥ ..
vinirgatā dharāpṛṣṭhātkṣetrasyāsyādhipā smṛtā .. 43 ..
5.132.d:
एकाहं तव भूपाल होमस्यास्य प्रभावतः ..
विनिर्गता धरापृष्ठात्क्षेत्रस्यास्याधिपा स्मृता .. 43 ..
5.132.m:
"I alone, O protector of the earth, through the power of this oblation of yours,
have emerged from the surface of the earth; I am known as the sovereign of this sacred field.

5.132.s:
tasmādvada mahābhāga yatte kṛtyaṃ karomyaham ..
parāṃ tuṣṭimanuprāptā tasmādbrūhi yadīpsitam .. 44 ..
5.132.d:
तस्माद्वद महाभाग यत्ते कृत्यं करोम्यहम् ..
परां तुष्टिमनुप्राप्ता तस्माद्ब्रूहि यदीप्सितम् .. 44 ..
5.132.m:
Therefore, declare, O fortunate one, what duty I may perform for you.
I have attained supreme satisfaction; therefore, speak what is desired."

5.132.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
atra sthāne sadā stheyaṃ tvayā devi viśeṣataḥ ..
vyādhisaṃsargajo doṣo bhūmerasyā yathā vrajet .. .. 45 ..
5.132.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
अत्र स्थाने सदा स्थेयं त्वया देवि विशेषतः ..
व्याधिसंसर्गजो दोषो भूमेरस्या यथा व्रजेत् .. .. 45 ..
5.132.m:
The king said:
"O goddess, you should especially dwell in this place forever,
so that the fault born of contact with diseases may depart from this earth.

5.132.s:
adyaprabhṛti deveśi tathā nītirvidhīyatām ..
no cedasyāḥ prasaṃgena prabhaviṣyaṃti mānavāḥ .. 46 ..
5.132.d:
अद्यप्रभृति देवेशि तथा नीतिर्विधीयताम् ..
नो चेदस्याः प्रसंगेन प्रभविष्यंति मानवाः .. 46 ..
5.132.m:
From this day forward, O ruler of gods, let such a rule be established;
otherwise, by contact with it, human beings will become

5.132.s:
vyādhigrastā yathā vipro yo'yaṃ saṃdṛśyate puraḥ ..
mayātra vyādhayaḥ kālaṃ ciraṃ saṃsthāpitā yataḥ ..
bhaviṣyati ca me doṣo no ceddevi na saṃśayaḥ .. 47 ..
5.132.d:
व्याधिग्रस्ता यथा विप्रो योऽयं संदृश्यते पुरः ..
मयात्र व्याधयः कालं चिरं संस्थापिता यतः ..
भविष्यति च मे दोषो नो चेद्देवि न संशयः .. 47 ..
5.132.m:
afflicted by disease, like this brahmin who is seen before us.
Since diseases were kept here by me for a long time,
fault will come upon me otherwise, O goddess, without a doubt.

5.132.s:
tathāyaṃ brāhmaṇo rogāttvatprasādātsureśvari ..
mukto bhavatu medinyāmatra stheyaṃ sadā tvayā ..48..
5.132.d:
तथायं ब्राह्मणो रोगात्त्वत्प्रसादात्सुरेश्वरि ..
मुक्तो भवतु मेदिन्यामत्र स्थेयं सदा त्वया ..48..
5.132.m:
Likewise, may this brahmin be freed from disease by your grace, O ruler of gods;
and you should dwell perpetually here on this earth."

5.132.s:
.. kṣetradevatovāca .. ..
etatsthānaṃ mayā sarvaṃ vyādhidoṣavivarjitam ..
vihitaṃ sarvadaivātra sthāsye'hamiha sarvadā ..49..
5.132.d:
.. क्षेत्रदेवतोवाच .. ..
एतत्स्थानं मया सर्वं व्याधिदोषविवर्जितम् ..
विहितं सर्वदैवात्र स्थास्येऽहमिह सर्वदा ..49..

5.132.s:
sāṃprataṃ yo'tra me sthāne vyādhigrastaḥ sameṣyati ..
pūjayiṣyati māṃ bhaktyā nīrogaḥ sa bhaviṣyati .. 6.133.50 ..
5.132.d:
सांप्रतं योऽत्र मे स्थाने व्याधिग्रस्तः समेष्यति ..
पूजयिष्यति मां भक्त्या नीरोगः स भविष्यति .. 6.133.50 ..
5.132.m:
Now, whoever, afflicted with disease, approaches my place here
and worships me with devotion, will become free from disease.

5.132.s:
tasmādadya dvijeṃdro'yaṃ māṃ pūjayatu sādaram ..
bhaktyā paramayā yuktaḥ śucirbhūtvā samāhitaḥ.. 51 ..
5.132.d:
तस्मादद्य द्विजेंद्रोऽयं मां पूजयतु सादरम् ..
भक्त्या परमया युक्तः शुचिर्भूत्वा समाहितः.. 51 ..
5.132.m:
Therefore, let this best of brahmins worship me respectfully today,
endowed with supreme devotion, having become pure and concentrated in mind.

5.132.s:
atra kṣetre parā'nyāsti vikhyātā caṃdrakūpikā. ..
tasyāṃ snātu yathānyāyaṃ nityameva mahīpate .. 52 ..
5.132.d:
अत्र क्षेत्रे पराऽन्यास्ति विख्याता चंद्रकूपिका. ..
तस्यां स्नातु यथान्यायं नित्यमेव महीपते .. 52 ..
5.132.m:
In this sacred field there is another celebrated well, the Candrakūpikā;
let him bathe in it according to rule every day, O lord of the earth,

5.132.s:
dakṣaśāpapraśaptena yā caṃdreṇa purā kṛtā ..
svasnānārthaṃ kṣayavyādhipragrastena mahātmanā . 53 ..
5.132.d:
दक्षशापप्रशप्तेन या चंद्रेण पुरा कृता ..
स्वस्नानार्थं क्षयव्याधिप्रग्रस्तेन महात्मना . 53 ..
5.132.m:
which was formerly made by the Moon, when cursed by Dakṣa's curse,
for his own ritual ablution, when that great soul was afflicted with consumption.

5.132.s:
tathā khaṇḍaśilānāma devatā cātra tiṣṭhati ..
saubhāgyakūpikāsnānaṃ kṛtvā tāṃ ca prapaśyatu ..54..
5.132.d:
तथा खण्डशिलानाम देवता चात्र तिष्ठति ..
सौभाग्यकूपिकास्नानं कृत्वा तां च प्रपश्यतु ..54..
5.132.m:
Likewise, a deity named Khaṇḍaśilā dwells here;
having taken a ritual ablution in the Saubhāgyakūpikā, let him behold her,

5.132.s:
yā kṛtā kāmadevena kuṣṭhagrastena vai purā .
snapanārthaṃ ca kuṣṭhasya vināśāya ca sādaram .. 55..
5.132.d:
या कृता कामदेवेन कुष्ठग्रस्तेन वै पुरा .
स्नपनार्थं च कुष्ठस्य विनाशाय च सादरम् .. 55..
5.132.m:
which was formerly made by Kāmadeva when afflicted with leprosy,
for ceremonial bath and for the destruction of leprosy, with reverence.

5.132.s:
tathā cāpsarasāṃ kuṇḍamatrāsti nṛpasattama ..
tatra snātvā raverahni tataḥ pāmā praśāmyati .. 96 ..
.. sūta uvāca ..
tataḥ sa brāhmaṇaḥ prāpya supuṇyāṃ candrakūpikām ..
snānaṃ kṛtvā ca tāṃ devīṃ pūjayāmāsa bhaktitaḥ ..
yāvanmāsaṃ tato muktaḥ satvaraṃ rājayakṣmaṇā .. 57
tataḥ saubhāgyakūpīṃ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā kāmavinirmitām ..
tathā snānaṃ vidhāyātha paśyankhaṃḍaśilāṃ ca tām .. 58 ..
tadvanmāsena nirmuktaḥ kuṣṭhena dvijasattamāḥ ..
tasyā devyāḥ prabhāvena kūpikāyāṃ viśeṣataḥ . 59 ..
tataścāpsarasāṃ kuṃḍe snātvaikaṃ ravivāsaram ..
pāmayā saṃparityakto buddhyeva viṣayātmakaḥ .. 6.133.60 ..
tataḥ sa brāhmaṇo jāto dvādaśārkasamaprabhaḥ ..
toṣeṇa mahatā yukto dattāśīstasya bhūpateḥ .. 61 ..
prayayau vāṃchitaṃ deśamanujñātaśca bhūbhujā ..
devatāyāṃ praṇāmaṃ ca tābhyāṃ kṛtvā punaḥpunaḥ .. 62 ..
5.132.d:
तथा चाप्सरसां कुण्डमत्रास्ति नृपसत्तम ..
तत्र स्नात्वा रवेरह्नि ततः पामा प्रशाम्यति .. 96 ..
.. सूत उवाच ..
ततः स ब्राह्मणः प्राप्य सुपुण्यां चन्द्रकूपिकाम् ..
स्नानं कृत्वा च तां देवीं पूजयामास भक्तितः ..
यावन्मासं ततो मुक्तः सत्वरं राजयक्ष्मणा .. 57
ततः सौभाग्यकूपीं तां दृष्ट्वा कामविनिर्मिताम् ..
तथा स्नानं विधायाथ पश्यन्खंडशिलां च ताम् .. 58 ..
तद्वन्मासेन निर्मुक्तः कुष्ठेन द्विजसत्तमाः ..
तस्या देव्याः प्रभावेन कूपिकायां विशेषतः . 59 ..
ततश्चाप्सरसां कुंडे स्नात्वैकं रविवासरम् ..
पामया संपरित्यक्तो बुद्ध्येव विषयात्मकः .. 6.133.60 ..
ततः स ब्राह्मणो जातो द्वादशार्कसमप्रभः ..
तोषेण महता युक्तो दत्ताशीस्तस्य भूपतेः .. 61 ..
प्रययौ वांछितं देशमनुज्ञातश्च भूभुजा ..
देवतायां प्रणामं च ताभ्यां कृत्वा पुनःपुनः .. 62 ..
5.132.m:
And likewise, there is a pool of the apsarases here, O best of kings;
having bathed there on the day of the Sun (Sunday), one's scabies is alleviated."
Sūta said:
Then that brahmin, having reached the very holy Candrakūpikā
and having taken a ritual ablution, worshipped that goddess with devotion;
within a month he was quickly freed from consumption.
Then, having seen that Saubhāgyakūpī fashioned by Kāma,
and having likewise performed a ritual ablution, and beholding that Khaṇḍaśilā,
in like manner within a month he was freed from leprosy, O best of brahmins,
by the power of that goddess, especially at the well.
Then, having bathed in the pool of the apsarases on a single Sunday,
he was abandoned by scabies, as an intellect attached to sense-objects [is abandoned by attachments].
Then that brahmin became radiant as the twelve suns;
filled with great joy, he bestowed a blessing upon that king,
and, permitted by the king, went to his desired region,
having repeatedly offered bow to both deities.

5.132.s:
sopi rājā sadoṣāṃstānajārūpānvilokya ca ..
svasyaiva brāhmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ tathā saṃpraharṣitaḥ .. 63 ..
svayaṃ ca prayayau tatra yatrastho hāṭakeśvaraḥ ..
tenaiva ca śarīreṇa nijakāṃtāsamanvitaḥ ..64 ..
ajāgṛhe sthitā yasmātsā devī kṣetradevatā ..
ajāgṛhā tataḥ khyātā sarvatraiva dvijottamāḥ .. 65 ..
adyāpi yakṣmaṇā grasto yastāṃ pūjayate naraḥ ..
tainaiva vidhinā samyaksa nīrogo drutaṃ bhavet.. 66 ..
5.132.d:
सोपि राजा सदोषांस्तानजारूपान्विलोक्य च ..
स्वस्यैव ब्राह्मणं दृष्ट्वा तं तथा संप्रहर्षितः .. 63 ..
स्वयं च प्रययौ तत्र यत्रस्थो हाटकेश्वरः ..
तेनैव च शरीरेण निजकांतासमन्वितः ..64 ..
अजागृहे स्थिता यस्मात्सा देवी क्षेत्रदेवता ..
अजागृहा ततः ख्याता सर्वत्रैव द्विजोत्तमाः .. 65 ..
अद्यापि यक्ष्मणा ग्रस्तो यस्तां पूजयते नरः ..
तैनैव विधिना सम्यक्स नीरोगो द्रुतं भवेत्.. 66 ..
5.132.m:
That king also, having seen those [diseases] with their faults in the form of goats,
and having seen his own brahmin thus [cured], was greatly delighted.
And he himself went to that place where Hāṭakeśvara resides,
in that very body, accompanied by his beloved wife.
Because that goddess, the deity of the sacred field, stayed in the house of goats (Ajāgṛha),
she is known everywhere as Ajāgṛhā, O best of brahmins.
Even today, a man afflicted with consumption who worships her
properly according to that very rite quickly becomes free from disease.

5.132.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye'jāgṛhotpattimāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma trayastriṃśaduttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 133 ..
5.132.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्येऽजागृहोत्पत्तिमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम त्रयस्त्रिंशदुत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः .. 133 ..
5.132.m: Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-third chapter, entitled "Description of the Origin and Greatness of Ajāgṛhā" in the Greatness of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the auspicious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

5.133.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
yadā dakṣeṇa kruddhena purā śapto himadyutiḥ ..
tatsarvaṃ bhavatā proktaṃ somanāthakathānakam.. 1 ..
5.133.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
यदा दक्षेण क्रुद्धेन पुरा शप्तो हिमद्युतिः ..
तत्सर्वं भवता प्रोक्तं सोमनाथकथानकम्.. 1 ..
5.133.m:
The seers said:
"When the Moon (the cold-rayed one) was formerly cursed by angry Dakṣa,
all of that story of Somanātha was recounted by you.

5.133.s:
sāṃprataṃ vada kāmasya yathā kuṣṭho'bhavatpurā ..
yena doṣeṇa śāpaśca kena tasya niyojitaḥ .. 2 .
5.133.d:
सांप्रतं वद कामस्य यथा कुष्ठोऽभवत्पुरा ..
येन दोषेण शापश्च केन तस्य नियोजितः .. 2 .
5.133.m:
Now tell how leprosy formerly came upon Kāma,
through what fault, and by whom the curse was placed upon him.

5.133.s:
śilākhaṃḍā ca yā devī tathā saubhāgyakūpikā ..
yathā tatra samutpannā tathā'smākaṃ prakīrtaya .. 3 ..
5.133.d:
शिलाखंडा च या देवी तथा सौभाग्यकूपिका ..
यथा तत्र समुत्पन्ना तथाऽस्माकं प्रकीर्तय .. 3 ..
5.133.m:
And how the goddess Śilākhaṇḍā and the Saubhāgyakūpikā
came to be there—proclaim that to us."

5.133.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
purāsīdbrāhmaṇo nāma hārīta iti viśrutaḥ ..
sa tapastatra saṃtepe vānaprasthāśrame vasan .. 4 ..
5.133.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
पुरासीद्ब्राह्मणो नाम हारीत इति विश्रुतः ..
स तपस्तत्र संतेपे वानप्रस्थाश्रमे वसन् .. 4 ..

5.133.s:
tasya bhāryā'bhavatsādhvī rūpaudāryasamanvitā ..
trailokyasundarī sākṣāllakṣmīriva madhudviṣaḥ .. 5 ..
5.133.d:
तस्य भार्याऽभवत्साध्वी रूपौदार्यसमन्विता ..
त्रैलोक्यसुन्दरी साक्षाल्लक्ष्मीरिव मधुद्विषः .. 5 ..
5.133.m:
His virtuous wife was endowed with beauty and nobility,
a beauty of the three worlds, like Lakṣmī the consort of Madhudviṣ (Viṣṇu) in visible form,

5.133.s:
khyātā pūṇakalānāma sarvaiḥ samuditāguṇaiḥ ..
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā padmajo'pyāśu kāmasya vaśago'bhavat .. 6 ..
5.133.d:
ख्याता पूणकलानाम सर्वैः समुदितागुणैः ..
तां दृष्ट्वा पद्मजोऽप्याशु कामस्य वशगोऽभवत् .. 6 ..
5.133.m:
known by the name of Puṇyakalā, endowed with all virtues.
Seeing her, even the lotus-born [Brahmā] quickly came under the power of desire (Kāma).

5.133.s:
kadācidapi sa prāptastasminkṣetre manobhavaḥ ..
saha ratyā tathā prītyā kāmeśvaradidṛkṣayā .. 7 ..
5.133.d:
कदाचिदपि स प्राप्तस्तस्मिन्क्षेत्रे मनोभवः ..
सह रत्या तथा प्रीत्या कामेश्वरदिदृक्षया .. 7 ..
5.133.m:
Once that mind-born [Kāma] arrived in that sacred field
along with Rati and Prīti, wishing to see Kāmeśvara.

5.133.s:
etasminnaṃtare sāpi snānārthaṃ tatra cāgatā ..
kṛtvā vastraparityāgaṃ viveśa jalāśayam .. 8 ..
5.133.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे सापि स्नानार्थं तत्र चागता ..
कृत्वा वस्त्रपरित्यागं विवेश जलाशयम् .. 8 ..
5.133.m: In the meantime, she too came there to bathe; / having cast off her clothes, she entered the pool of water.

5.133.s:
atha tāṃ kāmadevopi samālokya śubhānanām..
ātmīyairapi nirviddho hṛdaye puṣpasāyakaiḥ .. 9 ..
5.133.d:
अथ तां कामदेवोपि समालोक्य शुभाननाम्..
आत्मीयैरपि निर्विद्धो हृदये पुष्पसायकैः .. 9 ..
5.133.m: Then, upon seeing that fair-faced lady, even the god of love / was pierced in his own heart by his floral arrows.

5.133.s:
tato ratiṃ parityaktvā prītiṃ ca śarapīḍitaḥ..
vijanaṃ kaṃcidāsādya prasuptaḥ sa taroradhaḥ .. 6.134.10 ..
5.133.d:
ततो रतिं परित्यक्त्वा प्रीतिं च शरपीडितः..
विजनं कंचिदासाद्य प्रसुप्तः स तरोरधः .. 6.134.10 ..
5.133.m: Then, tormented by his arrows, abandoning Rati / and Prīti, he approached a solitary place and fell asleep beneath a tree.

5.133.s:
gātraiḥ pulakitaiḥ sarvairniḥśvāsānniḥśvasanmuhuḥ ..
agnivarṇānsudīrghāṃśca bāṣpa pūrṇavilocanaḥ .. 11 ..
5.133.d:
गात्रैः पुलकितैः सर्वैर्निःश्वासान्निःश्वसन्मुहुः ..
अग्निवर्णान्सुदीर्घांश्च बाष्प पूर्णविलोचनः .. 11 ..
5.133.m: With all his limbs bristling, repeatedly drawing deep sighs / of a fiery hue, his eyes full of tears,

5.133.s:
tiṣṭhansa darśane tasyā ekadṛṣṭyā vyalokayat..
yogīva susamādhistho dhyāyaṃstadbrahma saṃsthitam .. 12 ..
5.133.d:
तिष्ठन्स दर्शने तस्या एकदृष्ट्या व्यलोकयत्..
योगीव सुसमाधिस्थो ध्यायंस्तद्ब्रह्म संस्थितम् .. 12 ..
5.133.m: Standing in her sight, he gazed with an unwavering gaze, / like a yogi seated in deep absorption meditating upon that immanent Brahman.

5.133.s:
sāpi kāmaṃ samālokya sānurāgaṃ puraḥ sthitam ..
jṛṃbhābhaṃgakṛtāsyaṃ ca vepamānaśarīrakam .. 13 ..
5.133.d:
सापि कामं समालोक्य सानुरागं पुरः स्थितम् ..
जृंभाभंगकृतास्यं च वेपमानशरीरकम् .. 13 ..
5.133.m: She too, seeing Kāma standing before her filled with longing, / his mouth gaping in yawns and his body trembling,

5.133.s:
sāpi tadbāṇanirbhinnā sābhilāṣā babhūva ha ..
kāmaṃ prati viśeṣeṇa tasya rūpeṇa mohitā .. 14 ..
5.133.d:
सापि तद्बाणनिर्भिन्ना साभिलाषा बभूव ह ..
कामं प्रति विशेषेण तस्य रूपेण मोहिता .. 14 ..
5.133.m: She too, pierced by his arrows, was filled with desire; / infatuated especially with Kāma on account of his beauty,

5.133.s:
atha tasmājjalātkṛcchrādviniṣkramya śucismitā ..
tīropāṃtaṃ samāsādya sthitā taddṛṣṭigocare .. 15 ..
5.133.d:
अथ तस्माज्जलात्कृच्छ्राद्विनिष्क्रम्य शुचिस्मिता ..
तीरोपांतं समासाद्य स्थिता तद्दृष्टिगोचरे .. 15 ..
5.133.m: Then, having emerged with difficulty from that water, the fair-smiling woman, / having approached the edge of the bank, stood within the range of his vision.

5.133.s:
tataḥ kāmaḥ samutthāya śanaistadaṃtikaṃ yayau ..
kṛtāṃjalipuṭo bhūtvā tataḥ provāca sādaram .. 16 ..
5.133.d:
ततः कामः समुत्थाय शनैस्तदंतिकं ययौ ..
कृतांजलिपुटो भूत्वा ततः प्रोवाच सादरम् .. 16 ..
5.133.m: Then Kāma arose and went slowly to her presence; / having joined his hands in reverence, he spoke respectfully:

5.133.s:
kā tvamatra viśālākṣi prāptā snātuṃ jalāśaye ..
mama nāśāya cārvaṃgi tasmācchṛṇu vaco mama .. 17 ..
5.133.d:
का त्वमत्र विशालाक्षि प्राप्ता स्नातुं जलाशये ..
मम नाशाय चार्वंगि तस्माच्छृणु वचो मम .. 17 ..
5.133.m: "Who are you, large-eyed lady, who have come to bathe in this pool of water / for my destruction, fair-limbed one? Therefore, listen to my words.

5.133.s:
ahaṃ puṣpaśaro loke prasiddhaścāruhāsini ..
viḍaṃbanāṃ mayā nītā devā api nijaiḥ śaraiḥ .. 18 ..
5.133.d:
अहं पुष्पशरो लोके प्रसिद्धश्चारुहासिनि ..
विडंबनां मया नीता देवा अपि निजैः शरैः .. 18 ..
5.133.m: I am renowned in the world as the flower-arrowed god, sweet-smiling lady; / even the gods have been brought to humiliation by my own arrows.

5.133.s:
madbāṇenāhato rudraḥ svaśarīre nitaṃbinīm ..
arddhena dhārayāmāsa tyaktvā lajjāṃ sudūrataḥ .. 19 ..
5.133.d:
मद्बाणेनाहतो रुद्रः स्वशरीरे नितंबिनीम् ..
अर्द्धेन धारयामास त्यक्त्वा लज्जां सुदूरतः .. 19 ..
5.133.m: Struck by my arrow, Rudra held the broad-hipped woman / on one half of his body, casting shame far away.

5.133.s:
brahmā maccharanirbhinnaḥ svasutāṃ cakame tataḥ ..
janayāmāsa tānviprānvālakhilyāṃstathāvidhān .. 20 ..
5.133.d:
ब्रह्मा मच्छरनिर्भिन्नः स्वसुतां चकमे ततः ..
जनयामास तान्विप्रान्वालखिल्यांस्तथाविधान् .. 20 ..
5.133.m: Brahmā, pierced by my arrow, then lusted after his own daughter; / and he fathered those renowned brahmins, the Vālakhilyas.

5.133.s:
ahilyāṃ cakame śakro gautamasya priyāṃ satīm ..
madbāṇaiḥ pīḍito'tīva svargādetya dharātalam .. 21 ..
5.133.d:
अहिल्यां चकमे शक्रो गौतमस्य प्रियां सतीम् ..
मद्बाणैः पीडितोऽतीव स्वर्गादेत्य धरातलम् .. 21 ..
5.133.m: Śakra, exceedingly tormented by my arrows, came from heaven to the surface of the earth / and lusted after Ahilyā, the beloved and virtuous wife of Gautama.

5.133.s:
evaṃ devā api kṣuṇṇā maccharairye mahattarāḥ ..
kiṃ punarmānavāḥ subhrūḥ kṛmiprāyāḥ sucaṃcalāḥ .. 22 ..
5.133.d:
एवं देवा अपि क्षुण्णा मच्छरैर्ये महत्तराः ..
किं पुनर्मानवाः सुभ्रूः कृमिप्रायाः सुचंचलाः .. 22 ..
5.133.m: Thus even the gods, who are exalted, were shattered by my arrows; / what then of human beings, fair-browed one, who are akin to worms and utterly fickle?

5.133.s:
ākīṭāṃtaṃ jagatsarvamābrahmāṃtaṃ tathaiva ca ..
viḍaṃbanāṃ parāṃ prāptaṃ maccharaiścāruhāsini .. 23 ..
5.133.d:
आकीटांतं जगत्सर्वमाब्रह्मांतं तथैव च ..
विडंबनां परां प्राप्तं मच्छरैश्चारुहासिनि .. 23 ..
5.133.m: The entire world, from insects up to Brahmā, / has been brought to supreme humiliation by my arrows, sweet-smiling one.

5.133.s: ahaṃ punastvayā bhīru nīto'vasthāmimāṃ śubhe .. 24 ..
5.133.d: अहं पुनस्त्वया भीरु नीतोऽवस्थामिमां शुभे .. 24 ..
5.133.m: Yet, timid one, auspicious woman, I have been brought to this state by you.

5.133.s:
tasmāddehi mahābhāge mamādya ratadakṣiṇām ..
yāvanna yāṃti saṃtyajya mama prāṇāḥ kalevarāt .. .. 25 ..
5.133.d:
तस्माद्देहि महाभागे ममाद्य रतदक्षिणाम् ..
यावन्न यांति संत्यज्य मम प्राणाः कलेवरात् .. .. 25 ..
5.133.m: Therefore, fortunate lady, give me today the gift of amorous union, / before my life-breaths depart from my body!"

5.133.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
sāpi tadvacanaṃ śrutvā pativrataparāyaṇā ..
hanyamānā viśeṣeṇa tadbāṇairhṛdaye bhṛśam .. 26 ..
5.133.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
सापि तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा पतिव्रतपरायणा ..
हन्यमाना विशेषेण तद्बाणैर्हृदये भृशम् .. 26 ..
5.133.m: Sūta said: / Hearing his words, she, devoted to her husband, / was stricken vehemently in her heart, especially by his arrows.

5.133.s:
anabhijñā ca sā sādhvī kāmadharmasya kevalam ..
tāpasaiḥ saha saṃvṛddhā nānyaṃ jānāti kiṃcana .. 27 ..
5.133.d:
अनभिज्ञा च सा साध्वी कामधर्मस्य केवलम् ..
तापसैः सह संवृद्धा नान्यं जानाति किंचन .. 27 ..
5.133.m: And that virtuous woman was completely unacquainted with the nature of passion; / having grown up among ascetics, she knew nothing else.

5.133.s:
vaktuṃ tadviṣaye yacca procyate kāmapīḍitaiḥ ..
adhomukhā'likhadbhūmimaṃguṣṭhena sthitā ciram .. 28 ..
5.133.d:
वक्तुं तद्विषये यच्च प्रोच्यते कामपीडितैः ..
अधोमुखाऽलिखद्भूमिमंगुष्ठेन स्थिता चिरम् .. 28 ..
5.133.m: [Unable] to speak regarding that which is uttered by those tormented by passion, / she stood for a long time with her face turned downward, scratching the ground with her big toe.

5.133.s:
etasminnantare bhānuḥ prāptaścāstaṃ giriṃ prati ..
vihārasamaye prāpta āhitāgnirniveśane .. 29 ..
5.133.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे भानुः प्राप्तश्चास्तं गिरिं प्रति ..
विहारसमये प्राप्त आहिताग्निर्निवेशने .. 29 ..
5.133.m: In the meantime, the sun reached the setting mountain; / and Hārīta, who maintained the sacred fires, returned home at the time of daily recreation.

5.133.s:
hārīto'pi ciraṃ vīkṣya tanmārgaṃ cākṛtāśanaḥ ..
tataḥ sa ciṃtayāmāsa kasmātsā cātra nāgatā .. 30 ..
5.133.d:
हारीतोऽपि चिरं वीक्ष्य तन्मार्गं चाकृताशनः ..
ततः स चिंतयामास कस्मात्सा चात्र नागता .. 30 ..
5.133.m: Watching the path for her for a long time without taking his meal, / he then reflected: "Why has she not come here,

5.133.s:
snātvā tīrthavare tasmindṛṣṭvā tāṃ candrakūpikām..
kāmeśvaraṃ ca deveśaṃ kāmadaṃ sukhadaṃ nṛṇām .. 31 ..
5.133.d:
स्नात्वा तीर्थवरे तस्मिन्दृष्ट्वा तां चन्द्रकूपिकाम्..
कामेश्वरं च देवेशं कामदं सुखदं नृणाम् .. 31 ..
5.133.m: having bathed at that excellent sacred ford and visited that Candrakūpikā / and Kāmeśvara, the lord of gods, who grants desires and happiness to men?"

5.133.s:
tataḥ śiṣyasamāyukto vīkṣamāṇa itastataḥ ..
taṃ deśaṃ samanuprāpto yatra tau dvāvapi sthitau .. 32 ..
5.133.d:
ततः शिष्यसमायुक्तो वीक्षमाण इतस्ततः ..
तं देशं समनुप्राप्तो यत्र तौ द्वावपि स्थितौ .. 32 ..
5.133.m: Then, accompanied by his disciples, looking here and there, / he arrived at that place where both of them were standing.

5.133.s:
ālapanbahudhā kāmo hanyamāno nijaiḥ śaraiḥ ..
sāpi caiva viśeṣeṇa vrīḍayā'dhomukhī sthitā .. 33 ..
5.133.d:
आलपन्बहुधा कामो हन्यमानो निजैः शरैः ..
सापि चैव विशेषेण व्रीडयाऽधोमुखी स्थिता .. 33 ..
5.133.m: Kāma was speaking at length, struck by his own arrows, / and she too stood with her face turned down in extreme shame.

5.133.s:
sa gulmāṃtaritaḥ sarvaṃ tacchrutvā kāmajalpitam ..
tasyāśca tadgataṃ bhāvaṃ tataḥ kopāduvāca saḥ .. 34 ..
5.133.d:
स गुल्मांतरितः सर्वं तच्छ्रुत्वा कामजल्पितम् ..
तस्याश्च तद्गतं भावं ततः कोपादुवाच सः .. 34 ..
5.133.m: Concealed behind a bush, hearing all of Kāma's prattle / and [seeing] her disposition directed toward him, he then spoke in anger:

5.133.s:
yasmātpāpa tvayā patnī mamaivaṃ śarapīḍitā ..
anabhijñā tathā sādhvī patidharmaparāyaṇā ..
kuṣṭhavyādhisamāyuktastasmādvipriyadarśanaḥ .. 35 ..
5.133.d:
यस्मात्पाप त्वया पत्नी ममैवं शरपीडिता ..
अनभिज्ञा तथा साध्वी पतिधर्मपरायणा ..
कुष्ठव्याधिसमायुक्तस्तस्माद्विप्रियदर्शनः .. 35 ..
5.133.m: "Since my wife, innocent, virtuous, and devoted to her wifely duties, / has been thus tormented with arrows by you, wicked one, / therefore, afflicted with leprosy, unpleasant to behold,

5.133.s:
tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi pāpātmanmukto dāraiḥ svakairapi ..
sā'pi caiva viśeṣeṇa vrīḍayā'dhomukhī sthitā .. 36 ..
5.133.d:
त्वं भविष्यसि पापात्मन्मुक्तो दारैः स्वकैरपि ..
साऽपि चैव विशेषेण व्रीडयाऽधोमुखी स्थिता .. 36 ..
5.133.m: you shall become, sinful soul, abandoned even by your own wives!" / And she too stood with her face turned down in extreme shame.

5.133.s:
eṣāpi ca śilāprāyā bhaviṣyati vicetanā ..
tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā yā sarāgā'bhūnnijadharmabahiṣkṛtā .. 37 ..
5.133.d:
एषापि च शिलाप्राया भविष्यति विचेतना ..
त्वां दृष्ट्वा या सरागाऽभून्निजधर्मबहिष्कृता .. 37 ..
5.133.m: "And this woman, having seen you and felt passion, forsaking her own duty, / shall become like a stone, insensate!"

5.133.s:
tataḥ prasādayāmāsa taṃ kāmaḥ praṇipatya ca ..
na jñāteyaṃ mayā vipra tava bhāryeti sundarī .. 38 ..
5.133.d:
ततः प्रसादयामास तं कामः प्रणिपत्य च ..
न ज्ञातेयं मया विप्र तव भार्येति सुन्दरी .. 38 ..
5.133.m: Then Kāma, bowing down, propitiated him: / "Brahmin, it was not known by me that this beautiful woman was your wife.

5.133.s:
tena proktā viruddhāni vākyāni vividhāni ca ..
etasyā nāsti doṣo'tra madbāṇaiḥ pīḍitā bhṛśam .. 39
5.133.d:
तेन प्रोक्ता विरुद्धानि वाक्यानि विविधानि च ..
एतस्या नास्ति दोषोऽत्र मद्बाणैः पीडिता भृशम् .. 39
5.133.m: By that [ignorance] improper words of various kinds were spoken [by me]. / There is no fault of hers here; she was severely tormented by my arrows.

5.133.s:
sānurāgā paraṃ jātā noktaṃ kiṃcidvaco mune ..
tasmānnārhasi śāpaṃ tvaṃ dātumasyāḥ kathaṃcana .. 40 ..
5.133.d:
सानुरागा परं जाता नोक्तं किंचिद्वचो मुने ..
तस्मान्नार्हसि शापं त्वं दातुमस्याः कथंचन .. 40 ..
5.133.m: She only became impassioned, sage; no word was spoken [by her]. / Therefore, you ought not to pronounce a curse upon her in any way.

5.133.s:
mamāstyeṣo 'parādho'tra tasmānme nigrahaṃ kuru ..
bhūyo'pi brāhmaṇaśreṣṭha asyāḥ śāpasamudbhavam .. 41 ..
5.133.d:
ममास्त्येषो ऽपराधोऽत्र तस्मान्मे निग्रहं कुरु ..
भूयोऽपि ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठ अस्याः शापसमुद्भवम् .. 41 ..
5.133.m: This offence is mine alone; therefore, inflict punishment on me! / Furthermore, best of brahmins, concerning the origin of her curse:

5.133.s:
api rudrādayo devā madbāṇebhyo dvijottama ..
soḍhuṃ śaktā na te yasmāttatkathaṃ syādiyaṃ śilā .. 42 ..
5.133.d:
अपि रुद्रादयो देवा मद्बाणेभ्यो द्विजोत्तम ..
सोढुं शक्ता न ते यस्मात्तत्कथं स्यादियं शिला .. 42 ..
5.133.m: Since even gods such as Rudra, supreme twice-born, / are unable to withstand my arrows, how could she become a stone?

5.133.s:
tathātra trividhaṃ pāpaṃ pravadaṃti manīṣiṇaḥ ..
mānasaṃ vācikaṃ caiva karmajaṃ ca tṛtīyakam..
tadasmākaṃ dvidhā jātamekaṃ cāsyā munīśvara . 43 ..
5.133.d:
तथात्र त्रिविधं पापं प्रवदंति मनीषिणः ..
मानसं वाचिकं चैव कर्मजं च तृतीयकम्..
तदस्माकं द्विधा जातमेकं चास्या मुनीश्वर . 43 ..
5.133.m: Moreover, the wise declare sin in this world to be threefold: / mental, verbal, and the third born of bodily action. / That [sin] occurred twofold in us, and only single in her, lord of sages,

5.133.s:
bhāryāyāste surūpāyāstasmātsaṃpūrṇanigraham ..
kariṣyasi na te bhītiḥ kācidasti paratrajā .. .. 44 ..
5.133.d:
भार्यायास्ते सुरूपायास्तस्मात्संपूर्णनिग्रहम् ..
करिष्यसि न ते भीतिः काचिदस्ति परत्रजा .. .. 44 ..
5.133.m: your beautiful wife. Therefore, if you inflict full punishment [upon her], / have you no fear whatsoever born of the next world?

5.133.s:
manastāpādvrajetpāpaṃ mānasaṃ vācikaṃ ca yat ..
tasya prasādanenaiva yasyopari vijalpitam .. 45 ..
5.133.d:
मनस्तापाद्व्रजेत्पापं मानसं वाचिकं च यत् ..
तस्य प्रसादनेनैव यस्योपरि विजल्पितम् .. 45 ..
5.133.m: Mental sin is dispelled through remorse; and that which is verbal / is dispelled only through the appeasement of the person against whom it was spoken;

5.133.s:
prāyaścittairyathoktaiśca karmajaṃ pātakaṃ vrajet .
dharmaśāstraiḥ pariproktaṃ yataḥ sarvairmahāmune .. 46 ..
5.133.d:
प्रायश्चित्तैर्यथोक्तैश्च कर्मजं पातकं व्रजेत् .
धर्मशास्त्रैः परिप्रोक्तं यतः सर्वैर्महामुने .. 46 ..
5.133.m: and sin born of action is dispelled through expiations as prescribed, / because this has been declared by all the treatises on dharma, great sage."

5.133.s:
.. hārīta uvāca .. ..
anyatra viṣaye tasyāḥ pātakaṃ kāmadevate ..
etasya tava dharmasya prādhānyaṃ manasaḥ smṛtam .. 47 ..
5.133.d:
.. हारीत उवाच .. ..
अन्यत्र विषये तस्याः पातकं कामदेवते ..
एतस्य तव धर्मस्य प्राधान्यं मनसः स्मृतम् .. 47 ..
5.133.m: Hārīta said: / "In another matter her sin might be [minor], god of love; / but in this domain of yours, the mind is traditionally held to be primary.

5.133.s:
tasmādevaṃvidhā ceyaṃ sadā sthāsyati cādhama ..
kiṃ punaḥ kuru yatkṛtyaṃ nāhaṃ vakṣyāmi kiṃcana .. 48 ..
5.133.d:
तस्मादेवंविधा चेयं सदा स्थास्यति चाधम ..
किं पुनः कुरु यत्कृत्यं नाहं वक्ष्यामि किंचन .. 48 ..
5.133.m: Therefore, vile one, she shall remain in such a condition forever. / What more? Do what you will; I shall not say anything further.

5.133.s:
prathamaṃ manasā sarvaṃ ciṃtyate tadanaṃtaram ..
tataḥ prajalpate vācā kriyate karmaṇā tataḥ .. 49 ..
5.133.d:
प्रथमं मनसा सर्वं चिंत्यते तदनंतरम् ..
ततः प्रजल्पते वाचा क्रियते कर्मणा ततः .. 49 ..
5.133.m: First everything is conceived by the mind; thereafter / it is uttered in speech, and then performed in bodily action.

5.133.s:
pramāṇaṃ hi manastasmātsarvakṛtyeṣu sarvadā ..
etasmātkāraṇātpūrṇo mayā'syā nigrahaḥ kṛtaḥ .. 50 ..
5.133.d:
प्रमाणं हि मनस्तस्मात्सर्वकृत्येषु सर्वदा ..
एतस्मात्कारणात्पूर्णो मयाऽस्या निग्रहः कृतः .. 50 ..
5.133.m: For the mind is the authority in all actions at all times; / for this reason, full punishment has been inflicted on her by me."

5.133.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evamuktvā muniśreṣṭho hārītaḥ svāśramaṃ yayau ..
sāpi pūrṇakalā jātā śilārūpā ca tatkṣaṇāt .. 51 ..
5.133.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवमुक्त्वा मुनिश्रेष्ठो हारीतः स्वाश्रमं ययौ ..
सापि पूर्णकला जाता शिलारूपा च तत्क्षणात् .. 51 ..
5.133.m:
Sūta said:
Having spoken thus, Hārīta, the best of sages, went to his own hermitage.
And she, Pūrṇakalā, instantly turned into stone. (51)

5.133.s:
kāmadevo'pi kuṣṭhena grasto raudreṇa ca dvijāḥ ..
śīrṇanāsāṃghripāṇiśca netrāṇāmapriyo'bhavat.. 52 ..
5.133.d:
कामदेवोऽपि कुष्ठेन ग्रस्तो रौद्रेण च द्विजाः ..
शीर्णनासांघ्रिपाणिश्च नेत्राणामप्रियोऽभवत्.. 52 ..
5.133.m:
Kāmadeva also, seized by dreadful leprosy, O twice-born ones,
having his nose, feet, and hands decayed, became offensive to the eyes. (52)

5.133.s:
atha kāme nirutsāhe saṃjāte dvijasattamāḥ ..
vyādhigraste jagatyasminsṛṣṭirodho vyajāyata ..53..
5.133.d:
अथ कामे निरुत्साहे संजाते द्विजसत्तमाः ..
व्याधिग्रस्ते जगत्यस्मिन्सृष्टिरोधो व्यजायत ..53..
5.133.m:
Then, when Kāma became dispirited and seized by disease,
O best of the twice-born, the obstruction of procreation arose in this world. (53)

5.133.s:
kevalaṃ kṣīyate loko naiva vṛddhiṃ pragacchati ..
svedajā ye'pi jīvāḥ syustepi yātāḥ parikṣayam .. 54 ..
5.133.d:
केवलं क्षीयते लोको नैव वृद्धिं प्रगच्छति ..
स्वेदजा येऽपि जीवाः स्युस्तेपि याताः परिक्षयम् .. 54 ..
5.133.m:
The world was only decreasing; it did not advance in growth at all.
Even whatever living beings were sweat-born went to ruin. (54)

5.133.s:
etasminnaṃtare devāḥ sarve ciṃtāsamākulāḥ ..
kimidaṃ kṣīyate loko jalasthaiḥ sthalajaiḥ saha ..55..
5.133.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे देवाः सर्वे चिंतासमाकुलाः ..
किमिदं क्षीयते लोको जलस्थैः स्थलजैः सह ..55..
5.133.m:
Meanwhile, all the gods were bewildered with anxiety:
“Why is this world dwindling away, along with the creatures living in water and on land? (55)

5.133.s:
na dṛśyate kvacidbālaḥ ko'pi kaścitkathaṃcana ..
na ca garbhavatī nārī kaccitkṣemaṃ smarasya ca .. ..56..
5.133.d:
न दृश्यते क्वचिद्बालः कोऽपि कश्चित्कथंचन ..
न च गर्भवती नारी कच्चित्क्षेमं स्मरस्य च .. ..56..
5.133.m:
Nowhere is any child seen in any way,
nor is any woman pregnant. Is Smara well?” (56)

5.133.s:
tatastaṃ vyādhinā grastaṃ jñātvātra kṣetrasaṃśrayam ..
ājagmustvaritāḥ sarve vyākulenāṃtarātmanā..57..
5.133.d:
ततस्तं व्याधिना ग्रस्तं ज्ञात्वात्र क्षेत्रसंश्रयम् ..
आजग्मुस्त्वरिताः सर्वे व्याकुलेनांतरात्मना..57..
5.133.m:
Then, having learned that he was seized by disease, taking refuge here in the sacred field,
they all arrived swiftly with agitated minds. (57)

5.133.s:
kāmeśvarapurasthaṃ ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā kusumāyudham..
atyaṃtavikṛtākāraṃ ciṃtayānaṃ maheśvaram .. 58 ..
5.133.d:
कामेश्वरपुरस्थं च तं दृष्ट्वा कुसुमायुधम्..
अत्यंतविकृताकारं चिंतयानं महेश्वरम् .. 58 ..
5.133.m:
And seeing him, the flower-arrowed [god], staying in the city of Kāmeśvara,
extremely deformed in shape, meditating upon Maheśvara, (58)

5.133.s:
tataḥ procuḥ suduḥkhārtāḥ kimidaṃ kusumāyudha ..
nirutsāhaḥ samutpannaḥ kuṣṭhavyādhisamākulaḥ ..59..
5.133.d:
ततः प्रोचुः सुदुःखार्ताः किमिदं कुसुमायुध ..
निरुत्साहः समुत्पन्नः कुष्ठव्याधिसमाकुलः ..59..
5.133.m:
they, afflicted with great distress, then said: “What is this, O flower-arrowed one?
You have become dispirited, afflicted with the disease of leprosy!” (59)

5.133.s:
tataścādhomukho jāto lajjayā parayā vṛtaḥ ..
provāca śāpajaṃ sarvaṃ hārītasya viceṣṭitam .. 6.134.60 ..
tataste vibudhāḥ procuḥ pātakaṃ yadgirā kṛtam ..3
5.133.d:
ततश्चाधोमुखो जातो लज्जया परया वृतः ..
प्रोवाच शापजं सर्वं हारीतस्य विचेष्टितम् .. 6.134.60 ..
ततस्ते विबुधाः प्रोचुः पातकं यद्गिरा कृतम् ..3
5.133.m:
Then he bowed his head down, filled with supreme shame,
and related the whole deed born of Hārīta's curse. (60)
Then those gods said: “The sin that was committed by speech, (61ab)

5.133.s: tattasyārādhanātsarvaṃ saṃkṣayaṃ yātyasaṃśayam .. 61 ..
5.133.d: तत्तस्याराधनात्सर्वं संक्षयं यात्यसंशयम् .. 61 ..
5.133.m: all that goes to destruction through worship of her, without doubt. (61cd)

5.133.s:
tasmādetāṃ śilārūpāṃ tvamārādhaya cittaja ..
yena kuṣṭhaḥ kṣayaṃ yāti tatastejo'bhivardhate .. 62 ..
5.133.d:
तस्मादेतां शिलारूपां त्वमाराधय चित्तज ..
येन कुष्ठः क्षयं याति ततस्तेजोऽभिवर्धते .. 62 ..
5.133.m:
Therefore, worship this one who has the form of stone, O mind-born one,
by which your leprosy will perish, and then your luster will increase. (62)

5.133.s:
jagati syānmahāsṛṣṭirdevakṛtyaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavet ..
na te'sti kāyajaṃ pāpaṃ yato muktvā pravācikam .. 63 ..
5.133.d:
जगति स्यान्महासृष्टिर्देवकृत्यं कृतं भवेत् ..
न तेऽस्ति कायजं पापं यतो मुक्त्वा प्रवाचिकम् .. 63 ..
5.133.m:
Great procreation will take place in the world, and the duty of the gods will be accomplished.
For you have no bodily sin, having been freed [from it], except for that of speech. (63)

5.133.s:
atra kuṇḍe tvadīye'nyo yaḥ snātvā śraddhayānvitaḥ ..
enāṃ pāpavinirmuktāṃ śilāṃ vai mānavaḥ spṛśet .. 64 ..
5.133.d:
अत्र कुण्डे त्वदीयेऽन्यो यः स्नात्वा श्रद्धयान्वितः ..
एनां पापविनिर्मुक्तां शिलां वै मानवः स्पृशेत् .. 64 ..
5.133.m:
Any other human being who, having bathed with faith in this pool of yours,
touches this stone that is freed from sin, (64)

5.133.s:
kuṣṭhavyādhisamopetaḥ kāyotthenāpi karmaṇā ..
so'pi vyādhivinirmukto bhaviṣyati gatajvaraḥ .. 65 ..
5.133.d:
कुष्ठव्याधिसमोपेतः कायोत्थेनापि कर्मणा ..
सोऽपि व्याधिविनिर्मुक्तो भविष्यति गतज्वरः .. 65 ..
5.133.m:
even if afflicted with the disease of leprosy by action arising from the body,
he too will be freed from the disease, rid of fever. (65)

5.133.s:
etatsaubhāgyakūpaṃ ca loke khyātaṃ jalāśayam ..
bhaviṣyati na saṃdehaḥ sarvarogakṣayāvaham .. 66 ..
5.133.d:
एतत्सौभाग्यकूपं च लोके ख्यातं जलाशयम् ..
भविष्यति न संदेहः सर्वरोगक्षयावहम् .. 66 ..
5.133.m:
And this reservoir will be known in the world as the Saubhāgyakūpa,
bringing the destruction of all diseases, of this there is no doubt. (66)

5.133.s:
dadrūṇi durvibhūtāni tathānyāśca vicarcikāḥ ..
atra snātasya yāsyaṃti dṛṣṭvaitāṃ sadya eva hi .. 67 ..
5.133.d:
दद्रूणि दुर्विभूतानि तथान्याश्च विचर्चिकाः ..
अत्र स्नातस्य यास्यंति दृष्ट्वैतां सद्य एव हि .. 67 ..
5.133.m:
Severe ringworms and other eczemas
of one who has bathed here will instantly vanish upon merely seeing this [stone].” (67)

5.133.s:
evamuktvātha te devāḥ prajagmustridaśālayam ..
kāmadevo'pi tatrasthastasyāḥ pūjāmatha vyadhāt .. 68 ..
5.133.d:
एवमुक्त्वाथ ते देवाः प्रजग्मुस्त्रिदशालयम् ..
कामदेवोऽपि तत्रस्थस्तस्याः पूजामथ व्यधात् .. 68 ..
5.133.m:
Having spoken thus, those gods then went to the abode of the thirty [gods].
Kāmadeva also, remaining there, performed her worship. (68)

5.133.s:
tataśca samatikrāṃte māsamātre dvijottamāḥ ..
tādṛgrūpaḥ sa saṃjāto yādṛgāsītpurā smaraḥ .. 69 ..
5.133.d:
ततश्च समतिक्रांते मासमात्रे द्विजोत्तमाः ..
तादृग्रूपः स संजातो यादृगासीत्पुरा स्मरः .. 69 ..
5.133.m:
And then, when just a month had passed, O best of the twice-born,
he became endowed with such a form as Smara had possessed formerly. (69)

5.133.s:
tataścāyatanaṃ tasyāḥ kṛtvā śraddhāsamanvitaḥ ..
jagāma vāṃchitaṃ deśaṃ sṛṣṭyarthaṃ yatnamāsthitaḥ .. 6.134.70 ..
5.133.d:
ततश्चायतनं तस्याः कृत्वा श्रद्धासमन्वितः ..
जगाम वांछितं देशं सृष्ट्यर्थं यत्नमास्थितः .. 6.134.70 ..
5.133.m:
Then, having built a shrine for her with faith,
he went to the desired region, undertaking effort for procreation. (70)

5.133.s:
sāpi namramukhī tādṛktena śaptā tathaiva ca ..
saṃjātā khaṇḍakākārā tena khaṇḍaśilā smṛtā .. 71 ..
5.133.d:
सापि नम्रमुखी तादृक्तेन शप्ता तथैव च ..
संजाता खण्डकाकारा तेन खण्डशिला स्मृता .. 71 ..
5.133.m:
She too, having a lowered face, cursed by him in that very manner,
became fractured in appearance; therefore she is remembered as Khaṇḍaśilā. (71)

5.133.s:
yastāṃ pūjayate bhaktyā trayodaśyāṃ tathaiva ca ..
nāpavādo bhavettasya paradārasamudbhavaḥ .. 72 ..
5.133.d:
यस्तां पूजयते भक्त्या त्रयोदश्यां तथैव च ..
नापवादो भवेत्तस्य परदारसमुद्भवः .. 72 ..
5.133.m:
Whoever worships her with devotion, and likewise on the thirteenth [lunar day],
to him no slander arising from another's wife will occur. (72)

5.133.s:
kāminyāśca viśeṣeṇa prāhaitacchaṃkarātmajaḥ ..
kārtikeyo dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ satyametanmayoditam .. 73 ..
5.133.d:
कामिन्याश्च विशेषेण प्राहैतच्छंकरात्मजः ..
कार्तिकेयो द्विजश्रेष्ठाः सत्यमेतन्मयोदितम् .. 73 ..
5.133.m:
Especially in the case of a desirable woman—so spoke the son of Śaṃkara,
Kārtikeya, O best of the twice-born; this spoken by me is true. (73)

5.133.s:
tathā kāmeśvaraṃ devaṃ kāmadevapratiṣṭhitam ..
trayodaśyāṃ samārādhya sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt .. 74 ..
5.133.d:
तथा कामेश्वरं देवं कामदेवप्रतिष्ठितम् ..
त्रयोदश्यां समाराध्य सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् .. 74 ..
5.133.m:
Likewise, having worshipped the god Kāmeśvara, installed by Kāmadeva,
on the thirteenth [lunar day], one obtains all desires. (74)

5.133.s:
ratiprītisamāyuktaḥ sthitastatra smarastathā ..
mūrto brāhmaṇaśārdūlāḥ śreṣṭhaṃ prāsādamāśritaḥ . 75 .
5.133.d:
रतिप्रीतिसमायुक्तः स्थितस्तत्र स्मरस्तथा ..
मूर्तो ब्राह्मणशार्दूलाः श्रेष्ठं प्रासादमाश्रितः . 75 .
5.133.m:
Smara, endowed with Rati and Prīti, remains there,
embodied, O tigers among brahmins, dwelling in an excellent temple. (75)

5.133.s:
virūpo durbhago yo vā trayodaśyāṃ samāhitaḥ ..
yastaṃ kuṃkumajaiḥ puṣpaiḥ saṃpūjayati mānavaḥ .. 76 ..
5.133.d:
विरूपो दुर्भगो यो वा त्रयोदश्यां समाहितः ..
यस्तं कुंकुमजैः पुष्पैः संपूजयति मानवः .. 76 ..
5.133.m:
Whatever person is ugly or unfortunate, who with concentrated mind on the thirteenth [lunar day]
worships him with saffron-born flowers, (76)

5.133.s:
sa saubhāgyasamāyukto rūpavāṃśca prajāyate ..
yā nārī patinā tyaktā sapatnījanasaṃvṛtā .. 77 ..
5.133.d:
स सौभाग्यसमायुक्तो रूपवांश्च प्रजायते ..
या नारी पतिना त्यक्ता सपत्नीजनसंवृता .. 77 ..
5.133.m:
he becomes handsome and endowed with good fortune.
Any woman abandoned by her husband, surrounded by co-wives, (77)

5.133.s:
taṃ devaṃ sukalatrāḍhyaṃ tathaiva paripūjayet ..
trayodaśyāṃ dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ kesaraiḥ kuṃkumodbhavaiḥ .. 78 ..
5.133.d:
तं देवं सुकलत्राढ्यं तथैव परिपूजयेत् ..
त्रयोदश्यां द्विजश्रेष्ठाः केसरैः कुंकुमोद्भवैः .. 78 ..
5.133.m:
should likewise thoroughly worship that god endowed with good wives,
on the thirteenth [lunar day], O best of the twice-born, with filaments produced from saffron. (78)

5.133.s:
sā saubhāgyavatī viprā jāyate ca prajāvatī ..
dhanadhānyasamṛddhā ca duḥkhaśokavivarjitā ..
doṣaiḥ sarvairvinirmuktā śaṃsitā dharaṇītale .. 79 ..
5.133.d:
सा सौभाग्यवती विप्रा जायते च प्रजावती ..
धनधान्यसमृद्धा च दुःखशोकविवर्जिता ..
दोषैः सर्वैर्विनिर्मुक्ता शंसिता धरणीतले .. 79 ..
5.133.m:
She becomes fortunate, O brahmins, and blessed with offspring,
rich in wealth and grain, free from misery and grief,
freed from all faults, and praised on the surface of the earth. (79)

5.133.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe śrīhāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye khaṃḍaśilāsaubhāgyakūpikotpattimāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma catustriṃśaduttaraśatatamodhyāyaḥ .. 134 ..
5.133.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे श्रीहाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये खंडशिलासौभाग्यकूपिकोत्पत्तिमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम चतुस्त्रिंशदुत्तरशततमोध्यायः .. 134 ..
5.133.m: Thus ends the one hundred thirty-fourth chapter, entitled “Description of the Māhātmya of the Origin of Khaṇḍaśilā and the Saubhāgyakūpikā,” in the glorious Skanda Purāṇa, in the compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses], in the sixth Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the glorification of the sacred field of Śrī Hāṭakeśvara. (134)

5.134.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tathānyāpi ca tatrāsti dīrghikākhyā suśobhanā ..
sarasī lokavikhyātā sarvapātakanāśanī .. 1 ..
5.134.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तथान्यापि च तत्रास्ति दीर्घिकाख्या सुशोभना ..
सरसी लोकविख्याता सर्वपातकनाशनी .. 1 ..
5.134.m:
Sūta said:
Likewise, there is also another very beautiful reservoir there named Dīrghikā,
renowned in the world, the destroyer of all sins, (1)

5.134.s:
yasyāṃ snāto naraḥ samyagbhāskarasyodayaṃ prati ..
jyeṣṭhaśuklacaturdaśyāṃ mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ ..2..
5.134.d:
यस्यां स्नातो नरः सम्यग्भास्करस्योदयं प्रति ..
ज्येष्ठशुक्लचतुर्दश्यां मुच्यते सर्वपातकैः ..2..
5.134.m:
in which a person who bathes properly towards the rising of the sun
on the fourteenth of the bright half of Jyeṣṭha is freed from all sins. (2)

5.134.s:
āsītpūrvaṃ dvijo vīraśarmanāmātiviśrutaḥ ..
vedavidyāvratasnāto vardhamāne purottame .. 3 ..
5.134.d:
आसीत्पूर्वं द्विजो वीरशर्मनामातिविश्रुतः ..
वेदविद्याव्रतस्नातो वर्धमाने पुरोत्तमे .. 3 ..
5.134.m:
Formerly there was a very famous twice-born named Vīraśarman,
who had completed his vows and Vedic study, in the excellent city of Vardhamāna. (3)

5.134.s:
tasya kanyā samutpannā kadācillakṣaṇāccyutā ..
atidīrghā pramāṇena janahāsyavivarddhinī .. 4 ..
5.134.d:
तस्य कन्या समुत्पन्ना कदाचिल्लक्षणाच्च्युता ..
अतिदीर्घा प्रमाणेन जनहास्यविवर्द्धिनी .. 4 ..
5.134.m:
A daughter was born to him, who at some time was devoid of auspicious marks,
extremely tall in measure, increasing the laughter of people. (4)

5.134.s:
tataḥ sā yauvanaṃ prāptā tadrūpāpi kumārikā ..
na kaścidvarayāmāsa śāstravākyamanusmaran .. 5 ..
5.134.d:
ततः सा यौवनं प्राप्ता तद्रूपापि कुमारिका ..
न कश्चिद्वरयामास शास्त्रवाक्यमनुस्मरन् .. 5 ..
5.134.m:
Then, though that maiden attained youth with such a form,
no one chose her as a bride, remembering the injunction of scripture: (5)

5.134.s:
atisaṃkṣiptakeśā yā atidīrghātivāmanā ..
udvāhayati yaḥ kanyāṃ puruṣaḥ kāmamohitaḥ .. 6 ..
5.134.d:
अतिसंक्षिप्तकेशा या अतिदीर्घातिवामना ..
उद्वाहयति यः कन्यां पुरुषः काममोहितः .. 6 ..
5.134.m:
“A man who, infatuated with desire, marries a maiden
who has very short hair, who is excessively tall, or who is excessively dwarfish, (6)

5.134.s:
ṣaṇmāsābhyaṃtare mṛtyuṃ sa prāpnoti naro dhruvam ..
etasmātkāraṇātsarve tāṃ tyajaṃti kumārikām .. 7 ..
5.134.d:
षण्मासाभ्यंतरे मृत्युं स प्राप्नोति नरो ध्रुवम् ..
एतस्मात्कारणात्सर्वे तां त्यजंति कुमारिकाम् .. 7 ..
5.134.m:
that man certainly meets death within six months.”
For this reason, all men shunned that maiden, (7)

5.134.s:
puruṣā atidīrghatvayuktāṃ vīkṣya samaṃtataḥ ..
tato vairāgyamāpannā tapastepe'tidāruṇam.. 8 ..
5.134.d:
पुरुषा अतिदीर्घत्वयुक्तां वीक्ष्य समंततः ..
ततो वैराग्यमापन्ना तपस्तेपेऽतिदारुणम्.. 8 ..
5.134.m:
seeing her endowed with extreme tallness on every side.
Then, having attained dispassion, she performed very fierce austerity. (8)

5.134.s:
cāṃdrāyaṇāni kṛcchrāṇi tayā cīrṇānyanekaśaḥ ..
pārākāṇi yathoktāni tathā sāṃtapanāni ca .. 9 ..
5.134.d:
चांद्रायणानि कृच्छ्राणि तया चीर्णान्यनेकशः ..
पाराकाणि यथोक्तानि तथा सांतपनानि च .. 9 ..
5.134.m:
The cāndrāyaṇa penances and kṛcchra penances were performed by her many times,
as well as the pārāka penances and sāṃtapana penances as prescribed. (9)

5.134.s:
vrataṃ yadvidyate kiṃcinniyamaḥ saṃyamastathā ..
anyaccāpi śubhaṃ kṛtyaṃ tatsarvaṃ ca tayā kṛtam .. 6.135.10 ..
5.134.d:
व्रतं यद्विद्यते किंचिन्नियमः संयमस्तथा ..
अन्यच्चापि शुभं कृत्यं तत्सर्वं च तया कृतम् .. 6.135.10 ..
5.134.m:
Whatever vow, observance, and restraint existed,
and whatever other auspicious rite, all that was performed by her. (10)

5.134.s:
evaṃ tasyā vratasthāyā jarā samyagupasthitā ..
tathāpi tejaso vṛddhirvavṛdhe tapasā kṛtā .. 11 ..
5.134.d:
एवं तस्या व्रतस्थाया जरा सम्यगुपस्थिता ..
तथापि तेजसो वृद्धिर्ववृधे तपसा कृता .. 11 ..
5.134.m:
Thus, while she was steadfast in vows, old age fully approached her;
yet the increase of luster produced by her austerity grew. (11)

5.134.s:
sā ca nityaṃ mahendrasya sabhāṃ yātyatikautukāt ..
devarṣīṇāṃ mataṃ śrotuṃ devatānāṃ viśeṣataḥ .. 12 ..
5.134.d:
सा च नित्यं महेन्द्रस्य सभां यात्यतिकौतुकात् ..
देवर्षीणां मतं श्रोतुं देवतानां विशेषतः .. 12 ..
5.134.m:
And out of great curiosity she constantly went to the assembly of Mahendra
to hear the views of the celestial seers, and especially of the deities. (12)

5.134.s:
yadā sā svāsanaṃ tyaktvā prayāti svagṛhonmukhī ..
tadaivābhyukṣaṇaṃ cakrustatra śakrasya kiṃkarāḥ .. 13 ..
5.134.d:
यदा सा स्वासनं त्यक्त्वा प्रयाति स्वगृहोन्मुखी ..
तदैवाभ्युक्षणं चक्रुस्तत्र शक्रस्य किंकराः .. 13 ..
5.134.m:
Whenever she left her seat and set out facing towards her own home,
just then the attendants of Śakra performed sprinkling with water there. (13)

5.134.s:
tathānyadivase dṛṣṭaṃ kriyamāṇaṃ tayā hi tat ..
abhyukṣaṇaṃ svakīye ca āsane dvijasattamāḥ .. .. 14 ..
5.134.d:
तथान्यदिवसे दृष्टं क्रियमाणं तया हि तत् ..
अभ्युक्षणं स्वकीये च आसने द्विजसत्तमाः .. .. 14 ..
5.134.m: Then, on another day, O best of brahmins, that sprinkling upon her own seat was indeed seen being performed by her.

5.134.s:
tataḥ kopaparītāṃgī dīrghikā sā kumārikā ..
triśākhāṃ bhṛkuṭīṃ kṛtvā tataḥ prāha puraṃdaram .. 15 ..
5.134.d:
ततः कोपपरीतांगी दीर्घिका सा कुमारिका ..
त्रिशाखां भृकुटीं कृत्वा ततः प्राह पुरंदरम् .. 15 ..
5.134.m: Then, her limbs overcome with rage, knitting her eyebrows into three furrows, that maiden Dīrghikā spoke to Puraṃdara:

5.134.s:
kiṃ doṣaṃ vīkṣya me śakra prokṣitaṃ cāsanaṃ tvayā ..
paradvā rakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ kiṃ mayaitatkṛtaṃ kvacit .. 16 ..
5.134.d:
किं दोषं वीक्ष्य मे शक्र प्रोक्षितं चासनं त्वया ..
परद्वा रकृतं दोषं किं मयैतत्कृतं क्वचित् .. 16 ..
5.134.m: “O Śakra, seeing what fault of mine has the seat been sprinkled by you? Was a fault committed through an alien path, or was this done by me anywhere?

5.134.s:
tasmānme pātakaṃ brūhi no cecchāpaṃ sudāruṇam ..
tvayi dāsyāmyasaṃdigdhaṃ satye nātmānamālabhe .. 17 ..
5.134.d:
तस्मान्मे पातकं ब्रूहि नो चेच्छापं सुदारुणम् ..
त्वयि दास्याम्यसंदिग्धं सत्ये नात्मानमालभे .. 17 ..
5.134.m: Therefore tell me my sin; otherwise I shall bestow a terrible curse upon you without doubt. I swear by truth!”

5.134.s:
.. indra uvāca .. ..
na te dīrghe'stidoṣotra kaścidekaṃ vinā śubhe ..
tenātha kriyate caitadāsanasyābhiṣecanam .. .. 18 ..
5.134.d:
.. इन्द्र उवाच .. ..
न ते दीर्घेऽस्तिदोषोत्र कश्चिदेकं विना शुभे ..
तेनाथ क्रियते चैतदासनस्याभिषेचनम् .. .. 18 ..
5.134.m: Indra said: / “O Dīrghā, O auspicious one, there is no fault in you here, except for one; by reason of that, this sprinkling of the seat is performed.

5.134.s:
tvaṃ kumāryapi saṃprāptā ṛtukālaṃ vigarhitā ..
tena doṣaṃ tvamāpannā nānyadastīha kāraṇam .. 19 ..
5.134.d:
त्वं कुमार्यपि संप्राप्ता ऋतुकालं विगर्हिता ..
तेन दोषं त्वमापन्ना नान्यदस्तीह कारणम् .. 19 ..
5.134.m: Though a maiden, you have reached your fertile season, condemned [unmarried]. Therefore you have incurred fault; there is no other reason here.

5.134.s:
tasmādadyāpi tvāṃ kaścidudvāhayati tāpasaḥ ..
tvaṃ taṃ varaya bharttāraṃ yena gacchasi medhyatām .. 6.135.20 ..
5.134.d:
तस्मादद्यापि त्वां कश्चिदुद्वाहयति तापसः ..
त्वं तं वरय भर्त्तारं येन गच्छसि मेध्यताम् .. 6.135.20 ..
5.134.m: Therefore, even today, if an ascetic marries you, choose him as your husband, through which you will attain purity.”

5.134.s:
tataśca lajjayā yuktā sā tadā dīrghakanyakā ..
gatvā bhūmitale tūrṇaṃ vardhamāne purottame .. 21 ..
5.134.d:
ततश्च लज्जया युक्ता सा तदा दीर्घकन्यका ..
गत्वा भूमितले तूर्णं वर्धमाने पुरोत्तमे .. 21 ..
5.134.m: Filled with shame then, that tall maiden quickly went to the earth's surface, to the excellent city of Vardhamāna.

5.134.s:
tataḥ phūtkartumārabdhā catvareṣu trikeṣu ca ..
ucchritya dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ bhramamāṇā itastataḥ .. 22 ..
5.134.d:
ततः फूत्कर्तुमारब्धा चत्वरेषु त्रिकेषु च ..
उच्छ्रित्य दक्षिणं पाणिं भ्रममाणा इतस्ततः .. 22 ..
5.134.m: Then, raising her right hand and wandering here and there in public squares and crossroads, she began to call out aloud:

5.134.s:
yadi kaściddvijo jātyā karoti mama sāṃpratam ..
pāṇigrāhaṃ tapo'rddhasya śreyo yacchāmi tasya ca ..23..
5.134.d:
यदि कश्चिद्द्विजो जात्या करोति मम सांप्रतम् ..
पाणिग्राहं तपोऽर्द्धस्य श्रेयो यच्छामि तस्य च ..23..
5.134.m: “If any brahmin by birth takes my hand in marriage right now, I will grant him the merit of half my austerity!”

5.134.s:
evaṃ tāṃ pravijalpantīṃ śrutvā lokā divāniśam ..
unmattāmiti manvānā hāsyaṃ cakruḥ parasparam .. 24 ..
5.134.d:
एवं तां प्रविजल्पन्तीं श्रुत्वा लोका दिवानिशम् ..
उन्मत्तामिति मन्वाना हास्यं चक्रुः परस्परम् .. 24 ..
5.134.m: Hearing her speaking thus day and night, the people, thinking she was mad, laughed at one another.

5.134.s:
tataḥ katipayāhasya prakurvaṃtī ca dīrghikā ..
kuṣṭhavyādhigṛhītena brāhmaṇena pariśrutā .. 25 ..
5.134.d:
ततः कतिपयाहस्य प्रकुर्वंती च दीर्घिका ..
कुष्ठव्याधिगृहीतेन ब्राह्मणेन परिश्रुता .. 25 ..
5.134.m: Then, after some days, Dīrghikā, crying out thus, was heard by a brahmin afflicted with leprosy.

5.134.s: tataḥ provāca mandaṃ sa samāhūya suduḥkhitām .. 26 ..
5.134.d: ततः प्रोवाच मन्दं स समाहूय सुदुःखिताम् .. 26 ..
5.134.m: Then, summoning the deeply grieved woman, he spoke softly:

5.134.s:
ahaṃ tvāmudvahāmyadya kṛtvā pāṇigrahaṃ tava ..
yadi madvacanaṃ sarvaṃ sarvadaivānutiṣṭhasi .. 27 .. ..
5.134.d:
अहं त्वामुद्वहाम्यद्य कृत्वा पाणिग्रहं तव ..
यदि मद्वचनं सर्वं सर्वदैवानुतिष्ठसि .. 27 .. ..
5.134.m: “I will wed you today, taking your hand in marriage, if you always follow all my instructions.”

5.134.s:
.. kumārikovāca .. ..
kariṣyāmi na saṃdehastava vākyaṃ dvijādhipa ..
kuru pāṇigrahaṃ me'dya vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā .. 28 ..
5.134.d:
.. कुमारिकोवाच .. ..
करिष्यामि न संदेहस्तव वाक्यं द्विजाधिप ..
कुरु पाणिग्रहं मेऽद्य विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा .. 28 ..
5.134.m: The maiden said: / “Without doubt I will carry out your word, O lord of brahmins. Take my hand in marriage today according to the rites seen in the ordinances.”

5.134.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tatastasyāḥ kumāryāḥ sa pāṇiṃ jagrāha dakṣiṇam ..
gṛhyoktena vidhānena devāgnigurusaṃnidhau .. 29 ..
5.134.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
ततस्तस्याः कुमार्याः स पाणिं जग्राह दक्षिणम् ..
गृह्योक्तेन विधानेन देवाग्निगुरुसंनिधौ .. 29 ..
5.134.m: Sūta said: / Then he took the right hand of that maiden according to the rite prescribed in the householder manuals, in the presence of the gods, fire, and the preceptor.

5.134.s:
atha sā prāha bhūyo'pi vivāhakṛtamaṃgalā ..
ādeśaṃ dehi me nātha yaṃ karomi tavādhunā .. 6.135.30 ..
5.134.d:
अथ सा प्राह भूयोऽपि विवाहकृतमंगला ..
आदेशं देहि मे नाथ यं करोमि तवाधुना .. 6.135.30 ..
5.134.m: Then, having completed the auspicious marriage ceremonies, she spoke again: “Give me a command, O my lord, which I may now fulfill for you.”

5.134.s:
.. patiruvāca .. ..
aṣṭaṣaṣṭiṣu tīrtheṣu snātumicchāmi sundari ..
sāhāyyena tvadīyena yadi śaknoṣi tatkuru .. 31 ..
5.134.d:
.. पतिरुवाच .. ..
अष्टषष्टिषु तीर्थेषु स्नातुमिच्छामि सुन्दरि ..
साहाय्येन त्वदीयेन यदि शक्नोषि तत्कुरु .. 31 ..
5.134.m: The husband said: / “O beautiful one, I wish to bathe in the sixty-eight sacred fords with your assistance. If you are able, do that.”

5.134.s:
bāḍhamityeva sā procya tatastūrṇaṃ pativratā ..
tatpramāṇaṃ dṛḍhaṃ kṛtvā ramyaṃ vaṃśakuṭīrakam .. 32 ..
5.134.d:
बाढमित्येव सा प्रोच्य ततस्तूर्णं पतिव्रता ..
तत्प्रमाणं दृढं कृत्वा रम्यं वंशकुटीरकम् .. 32 ..
5.134.m: Saying “So be it,” that devoted wife quickly made a charming, sturdy bamboo basket of suitable measure,

5.134.s:
mṛdu tūlasamāyuktaṃ tataḥ prāha nijaṃ patim ..
kṛtāṃjalipuṭā bhūtvā prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā .. 33 ..
5.134.d:
मृदु तूलसमायुक्तं ततः प्राह निजं पतिम् ..
कृतांजलिपुटा भूत्वा प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना .. 33 ..
5.134.m: furnished with soft cotton; and then, folding her hands in reverence, with a gladdened inner heart, she spoke to her husband:

5.134.s:
etattava kṛte ramyaṃ kṛtaṃ vaṃśakuṭīrakam ..
mama nāthāruhāśu tvaṃ yena kṛtvātha mūrdhani ..
nayāmi sarvatīrtheṣu kṣetreṣu suśubheṣu ca .. 34 ..
5.134.d:
एतत्तव कृते रम्यं कृतं वंशकुटीरकम् ..
मम नाथारुहाशु त्वं येन कृत्वाथ मूर्धनि ..
नयामि सर्वतीर्थेषु क्षेत्रेषु सुशुभेषु च .. 34 ..
5.134.m: “For your sake this charming bamboo basket has been made. O my lord, climb in quickly so that, placing it upon my head, I may carry you to all the sacred fords and very auspicious sacred fields.”

5.134.s:
tataḥ kuṣṭhī prahṛṣṭātmā śanairutthāya bhūtalāt ..
tayā coddhṛtadehaḥ sansupto vaṃśakuṭīrake .. 35 ..
5.134.d:
ततः कुष्ठी प्रहृष्टात्मा शनैरुत्थाय भूतलात् ..
तया चोद्धृतदेहः सन्सुप्तो वंशकुटीरके .. 35 ..
5.134.m: Then the leper, glad at heart, gently rose from the ground and, his body lifted by her, slept in the bamboo basket.

5.134.s:
tatastaṃ mastake kṛtvā sarvatīrthe yathāsukham ..
sarvakṣetreṣu babhrāma snāpayantī nijaṃ patim .. 36 ..
5.134.d:
ततस्तं मस्तके कृत्वा सर्वतीर्थे यथासुखम् ..
सर्वक्षेत्रेषु बभ्राम स्नापयन्ती निजं पतिम् .. 36 ..
5.134.m: Then, placing him upon her head, she wandered at ease to all the sacred fords and through all the sacred fields, bathing her husband.

5.134.s:
yathā yathā sa cakre'tha snānaṃ tīrtheṣu kuṣṭhabhāk ..
tathātathāsya gātreṣu tejo vṛddhiṃ pragacchati ..37..
5.134.d:
यथा यथा स चक्रेऽथ स्नानं तीर्थेषु कुष्ठभाक् ..
तथातथास्य गात्रेषु तेजो वृद्धिं प्रगच्छति ..37..
5.134.m: As the leper bathed in the sacred fords, so did the brilliance in his limbs increase.

5.134.s:
tataḥ krameṇa sā sādhvī bhramamāṇā mahītale ..
hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre saṃprāptā rajanī mukhe .. 38 ..
5.134.d:
ततः क्रमेण सा साध्वी भ्रममाणा महीतले ..
हाटकेश्वरजे क्षेत्रे संप्राप्ता रजनी मुखे .. 38 ..
5.134.m: Then gradually, wandering over the surface of the earth, that virtuous woman arrived at nightfall in the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara.

5.134.s:
klāntā vaiklavyamāpannā bhārākrāntā pativratā ..
nidrāndhā niśvasantī ca praskhalantī padepade .. 39 ..
5.134.d:
क्लान्ता वैक्लव्यमापन्ना भाराक्रान्ता पतिव्रता ..
निद्रान्धा निश्वसन्ती च प्रस्खलन्ती पदेपदे .. 39 ..
5.134.m: Exhausted, overcome with weakness, weighed down by the burden, that devoted wife was blinded by sleep, sighing, and stumbling at every step.

5.134.s:
atha tatra pradeśe tu māṇḍavyo munipuṃgavaḥ ..
śūlāropitagātrastu saṃtiṣṭhati suduḥkhitaḥ .. 6.135.40 ..
5.134.d:
अथ तत्र प्रदेशे तु माण्डव्यो मुनिपुंगवः ..
शूलारोपितगात्रस्तु संतिष्ठति सुदुःखितः .. 6.135.40 ..
5.134.m: Now in that region, Māṇḍavya, the foremost among sages, was remaining in extreme agony, his body impaled on a stake.

5.134.s:
atha sā taṃ samāsādya śūlaṃ rātrau pativratā ..
nijagātreṇa bhārārttā gacchamānā mahāsatī .. 41 ..
5.134.d:
अथ सा तं समासाद्य शूलं रात्रौ पतिव्रता ..
निजगात्रेण भारार्त्ता गच्छमाना महासती .. 41 ..
5.134.m: Then that great virtuous wife, going at night afflicted by the burden, approached the stake with her body.

5.134.s:
tayā saṃcālitaḥ so'tha māṃḍavyo munipuṃgavaḥ ..
parāṃ pīḍāṃ samāsādya tataḥ prāha suduḥkhitaḥ ..42..
5.134.d:
तया संचालितः सोऽथ मांडव्यो मुनिपुंगवः ..
परां पीडां समासाद्य ततः प्राह सुदुःखितः ..42..
5.134.m: Jolted then by her, that foremost of sages, Māṇḍavya, experiencing intense torment, spoke in deep agony:

5.134.s:
kenedaṃ pāpmanā śalyaṃ mamāṃtaḥ paricālitam ..
