yenāhaṃ duḥkhayukto'pi bhūyo duḥkhāspadīkṛtaḥ .. 43 ..
5.134.d:
केनेदं पाप्मना शल्यं ममांतः परिचालितम् ..
येनाहं दुःखयुक्तोऽपि भूयो दुःखास्पदीकृतः .. 43 ..
5.134.m: “By what sinful person has this stake been shaken inside me, whereby, though already full of misery, I have been made the seat of misery once more?”

5.134.s:
.. dīrghikovāca .. ..
na mayā tvaṃ mahābhāga nidropahatayā dṛśā ..
dṛṣṭastena parispṛṣṭo hyaspṛśyaḥ pāpakṛttamaḥ .. 44 ..
5.134.d:
.. दीर्घिकोवाच .. ..
न मया त्वं महाभाग निद्रोपहतया दृशा ..
दृष्टस्तेन परिस्पृष्टो ह्यस्पृश्यः पापकृत्तमः .. 44 ..
5.134.m: Dīrghikā said: / “O illustrious one, because my sight was impaired by sleep, you were not seen by me; hence you were touched, O untouchable one, O greatest committer of sins!

5.134.s:
na tvayā sadṛśaścānyaḥ pāpātmāsti dharātale ..
śirasyudbhūtaśūlo'pi yo mṛtyuṃ nādhigacchati .. .. 45 ..
5.134.d:
न त्वया सदृशश्चान्यः पापात्मास्ति धरातले ..
शिरस्युद्भूतशूलोऽपि यो मृत्युं नाधिगच्छति .. .. 45 ..
5.134.m: There is no other sinful soul equal to you on the surface of the earth, who, even with a stake piercing out through your head, does not meet death!

5.134.s:
ahaṃ pativratā mūḍha vahāmi śirasā dhṛtam ..
tīrthayātrākṛte kāṃtaṃ vikalāṃgaṃ suvallabham .. 46 ..
5.134.d:
अहं पतिव्रता मूढ वहामि शिरसा धृतम् ..
तीर्थयात्राकृते कांतं विकलांगं सुवल्लभम् .. 46 ..
5.134.m: O fool, I am a devoted wife carrying upon my head my beloved husband, who is deformed of limb, for the sake of a pilgrimage to sacred fords.

5.134.s:
kasmāttasyāstiraskāraṃ mama yacchasi niṣṭhuram..
ajñātāṃ mūḍhabuddhiḥ sanviśeṣānmānuṣodbhavām .. 47 ..
5.134.d:
कस्मात्तस्यास्तिरस्कारं मम यच्छसि निष्ठुरम्..
अज्ञातां मूढबुद्धिः सन्विशेषान्मानुषोद्भवाम् .. 47 ..
5.134.m: Why do you cast harsh insults at me, an unknown woman, you fool, and especially one born human?”

5.134.s:
.. māṇḍavya uvāca .. ..
ahaṃ yādṛktvayā proktastādṛgeva na saṃśayaḥ ..
pāpātmā mūḍhabuddhiśca aspṛśyaḥ sarvadehinām .. 48 ..
5.134.d:
.. माण्डव्य उवाच .. ..
अहं यादृक्त्वया प्रोक्तस्तादृगेव न संशयः ..
पापात्मा मूढबुद्धिश्च अस्पृश्यः सर्वदेहिनाम् .. 48 ..
5.134.m: Māṇḍavya said: / “Just as I was described by you, exactly so am I, without doubt: a sinful soul, foolish-minded, and untouchable to all living beings.

5.134.s:
yadi prātastavāyaṃ ca bharttā jīvati niṣṭhure ..
yena me janitā pīḍā prāṇāṃtakaraṇī dṛḍhā .. 49 ..
5.134.d:
यदि प्रातस्तवायं च भर्त्ता जीवति निष्ठुरे ..
येन मे जनिता पीडा प्राणांतकरणी दृढा .. 49 ..
5.134.m: Yet, O cruel woman, if this husband of yours—by whom intense pain, bringing an end to life, has been inflicted on me—lives in the morning,

5.134.s:
tasmādeṣa tavābhīṣṭaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ sūryasya raśmibhiḥ ..
mayā śaptaḥ parityāgaṃ jīvitasya kariṣyati .. 6.135.50 ..
5.134.d:
तस्मादेष तवाभीष्टः स्पृष्टः सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिः ..
मया शप्तः परित्यागं जीवितस्य करिष्यति .. 6.135.50 ..
5.134.m: then, cursed by me, this beloved of yours, touched by the rays of the sun, shall abandon life!”

5.134.s:
.. dīrghikovāca .. ..
yadyevaṃ maraṇaṃ patyuḥ prabhāte saṃbhaviṣyati ..
madīyasya tataḥ prātarnodgamiṣyati bhāskaraḥ .. 51 ..
5.134.d:
.. दीर्घिकोवाच .. ..
यद्येवं मरणं पत्युः प्रभाते संभविष्यति ..
मदीयस्य ततः प्रातर्नोद्गमिष्यति भास्करः .. 51 ..
5.134.m: Dīrghikā said: / “If such death will come to my husband at dawn, then at dawn the sun shall not rise!”

5.134.s:
evamuktvā tataḥ sātha niṣasāda dharātale ..
bhūmau tadbhartṛsaṃyuktaṃ muktvā vaṃśakuṭīrakam .. 52 ..
5.134.d:
एवमुक्त्वा ततः साथ निषसाद धरातले ..
भूमौ तद्भर्तृसंयुक्तं मुक्त्वा वंशकुटीरकम् .. 52 ..
5.134.m: Having spoken thus, she set down upon the earth that bamboo basket with her husband and sat upon the ground.

5.134.s:
atha tāṃ prāha kuṣṭhī sa pipāsā saṃpravartate ..
tasmāttoyaṃ samānehi pānārthamatiśītalam .. 53 ..
5.134.d:
अथ तां प्राह कुष्ठी स पिपासा संप्रवर्तते ..
तस्मात्तोयं समानेहि पानार्थमतिशीतलम् .. 53 ..
5.134.m: Then that leper said to her: “Thirst has arisen; therefore bring very cool water for drinking.”

5.134.s:
tathaiva sā samākarṇya bharturādeśamutsukā ..
itastataśca babhrāma jalārthaṃ na prapaśyati ..
na ca niryāti dūraṃ sā tyaktvāraṇye tathāvidham .. 54 ..
5.134.d:
तथैव सा समाकर्ण्य भर्तुरादेशमुत्सुका ..
इतस्ततश्च बभ्राम जलार्थं न प्रपश्यति ..
न च निर्याति दूरं सा त्यक्त्वारण्ये तथाविधम् .. 54 ..
5.134.m: Hearing her husband’s command, eager [to serve], she wandered here and there, but saw no water; nor did she go far, abandoning him in such a state in the wilderness.

5.134.s:
bhartāraṃ śvāpadotthaṃ ca bhayaṃ hṛdi vitanvatī ..
upaviśya tato bhūmau spṛṣṭvā pādau patestadā ..
provāca dīrghikā vākyaṃ tāravākyena duḥkhitā .. 55 ..
5.134.d:
भर्तारं श्वापदोत्थं च भयं हृदि वितन्वती ..
उपविश्य ततो भूमौ स्पृष्ट्वा पादौ पतेस्तदा ..
प्रोवाच दीर्घिका वाक्यं तारवाक्येन दुःखिता .. 55 ..
5.134.m: Feeling fear in her heart for her husband, arising on account of wild beasts, / she then sat down on the ground, touched her husband's feet, / and the tall woman, stricken with sorrow, spoke these words in a loud voice:

5.134.s:
pativratā tvamācīrṇaṃ yadi samyaṅmayā sphuṭam ..
tena satyena bhūpṛṣṭhānnirgacchatu jalaṃ śubham .. 56 ..
5.134.d:
पतिव्रता त्वमाचीर्णं यदि सम्यङ्मया स्फुटम् ..
तेन सत्येन भूपृष्ठान्निर्गच्छतु जलं शुभम् .. 56 ..
5.134.m: "If the vow of devotion to my husband has been truly and properly observed by me, / by that truth let auspicious water burst forth from the earth's surface!"

5.134.s:
evamuktvā jaghānātha pādāghātena medinīm ..
kāntabhaktiṃ puraskṛtya tasya jīvitavāṃchayā .. 57 ..
5.134.d:
एवमुक्त्वा जघानाथ पादाघातेन मेदिनीम् ..
कान्तभक्तिं पुरस्कृत्य तस्य जीवितवांछया .. 57 ..
5.134.m: Having spoken thus, she then struck the earth with a kick of her foot, / prioritizing devotion to her beloved husband, out of a desire for his life.

5.134.s:
etasminnantare toyaṃ pādāghātādanantataram ..
niṣkrāṃtaṃ nirmalaṃ svādu māṇḍavyasya ca paśyataḥ .. 58 ..
5.134.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तोयं पादाघातादनन्ततरम् ..
निष्क्रांतं निर्मलं स्वादु माण्डव्यस्य च पश्यतः .. 58 ..
5.134.m: At that moment, from that kick of her foot, an endless flow of water / came forth, clear and sweet, right before Māṇḍavya's eyes.

5.134.s:
tatastaṃ snāpayāmāsa tasmiṃstoye śramāturam ..
apāyayattataḥ paścātsvayaṃ snātvā papau jalam .. 59 ..
5.134.d:
ततस्तं स्नापयामास तस्मिंस्तोये श्रमातुरम् ..
अपाययत्ततः पश्चात्स्वयं स्नात्वा पपौ जलम् .. 59 ..
5.134.m: Then she bathed him, afflicted with exhaustion, in that water; / after that she gave him water to drink, and having bathed herself, she drank the water.

5.134.s:
etasminnaṃtare sūryaḥ pativratakṛtādbhayāt ..
nābhyudeti samutpannastataḥ kālātyayo mahān .. 6.135.60 ..
5.134.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे सूर्यः पतिव्रतकृताद्भयात् ..
नाभ्युदेति समुत्पन्नस्ततः कालात्ययो महान् .. 6.135.60 ..
5.134.m: Meanwhile, the sun, out of fear caused by the devoted wife, / did not rise, and a great lapse of time ensued.

5.134.s:
atha rātriṃ samālokya dīrghāṃ ye kāmukā janāḥ ..
te sarve tuṣṭimāpannāstathā ca kula striyaḥ .. 61 ..
5.134.d:
अथ रात्रिं समालोक्य दीर्घां ये कामुका जनाः ..
ते सर्वे तुष्टिमापन्नास्तथा च कुल स्त्रियः .. 61 ..
5.134.m: Then, observing the long night, lustful people— / all of them were filled with delight, and so were unfaithful women.

5.134.s:
kauśikā rākṣasāścāpi corā jārāśca ye narāḥ ..
te sarve procuḥ saṃhṛṣṭāḥ samāliṃgya parasparam .. 62..
5.134.d:
कौशिका राक्षसाश्चापि चोरा जाराश्च ये नराः ..
ते सर्वे प्रोचुः संहृष्टाः समालिंग्य परस्परम् .. 62..
5.134.m: Owls, rākṣasas, and men who were thieves and paramours— / all of them, overjoyed, embraced one another and said:

5.134.s:
adyāsmākaṃ vidhistuṣṭo bhagavānmanmathastathā ..
yena dīrghā kṛtā rātrirnāśaṃ nītaśca bhāskaraḥ .. 63 ..
5.134.d:
अद्यास्माकं विधिस्तुष्टो भगवान्मन्मथस्तथा ..
येन दीर्घा कृता रात्रिर्नाशं नीतश्च भास्करः .. 63 ..
5.134.m: "Today fate is pleased with us, as is Lord Kāmadeva, / by whom the night has been lengthened and the sun brought to destruction!"

5.134.s:
ye punarbrāhmaṇāḥ śāṃtā yajñakarmasamudyatāḥ ..
te sarve duḥkhamāpannāḥ sūryodayavinākṛtāḥ .. 64 ..
5.134.d:
ये पुनर्ब्राह्मणाः शांता यज्ञकर्मसमुद्यताः ..
ते सर्वे दुःखमापन्नाः सूर्योदयविनाकृताः .. 64 ..
5.134.m: Those peaceful brahmins, however, who were intent on sacrificial rites, / all fell into sorrow, deprived of the rising of the sun.

5.134.s:
na kaścidyajanaṃ cakre yājanaṃ na ca saddvijaḥ ..
na śrāddhaṃ na ca saṃkalpaṃ na svādhyāyaṃ kathaṃcana .. .. 65 ..
5.134.d:
न कश्चिद्यजनं चक्रे याजनं न च सद्द्विजः ..
न श्राद्धं न च संकल्पं न स्वाध्यायं कथंचन .. .. 65 ..
5.134.m: No one performed sacrifices, nor did any good twice-born officiate at sacrifices; / neither ancestral rites nor ritual resolves nor sacred recitation occurred at all,

5.134.s:
na snānaṃ na ca dānaṃ ca lokayātrāṃ viśeṣataḥ ..
vyavahāraṃ na kṛtyaṃ ca kiṃciddharmasamudbhavam .. 66 ..
5.134.d:
न स्नानं न च दानं च लोकयात्रां विशेषतः ..
व्यवहारं न कृत्यं च किंचिद्धर्मसमुद्भवम् .. 66 ..
5.134.m: nor ritual ablution nor gifting, especially ordinary worldly affairs, / commerce, or any duty arising from dharma.

5.134.s:
etasminnantare devāḥ sarve śakrapurogamāḥ .
paraṃ dauḥsthyaṃ samāpannā yajñabhāgavivarjitāḥ .. 67 ..
5.134.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे देवाः सर्वे शक्रपुरोगमाः .
परं दौःस्थ्यं समापन्ना यज्ञभागविवर्जिताः .. 67 ..
5.134.m: Meanwhile, all the gods led by Śakra / fell into extreme distress, deprived of their portions of sacrificial offerings.

5.134.s:
tato bhāskaramāsādya ūcurduḥkhasamanvitāḥ ..
kasmānnodgamanaṃ deva prakaroṣi divākara .. .. 68 ..
5.134.d:
ततो भास्करमासाद्य ऊचुर्दुःखसमन्विताः ..
कस्मान्नोद्गमनं देव प्रकरोषि दिवाकर .. .. 68 ..
5.134.m: Then, approaching the sun, filled with grief, they said: / "O god, O maker of daylight, why do you not make your rising?

5.134.s: etattvayā vinā sarvaṃ jagadvyākulatāṃ gatam .. 69 ..
5.134.d: एतत्त्वया विना सर्वं जगद्व्याकुलतां गतम् .. 69 ..
5.134.m: Without you, this entire world has fallen into confusion!

5.134.s:
tasmāllokahitārthāya tvamudgaccha yathāpurā ..
agniṣṭomādikā yajñā vartaṃte yena bhūtale .. 6.135.70 ..
5.134.d:
तस्माल्लोकहितार्थाय त्वमुद्गच्छ यथापुरा ..
अग्निष्टोमादिका यज्ञा वर्तंते येन भूतले .. 6.135.70 ..
5.134.m: Therefore, for the welfare of the world, rise as before, / so that sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma may take place on the face of the earth."

5.134.s:
.. sūrya uvāca . ..
pativratāsamādeśāttyaktaścābhyudayo mayā ..
tasmādgatvā surāḥ sarve tāṃ vadaṃtu kṛte mama .. 71 ..
5.134.d:
.. सूर्य उवाच . ..
पतिव्रतासमादेशात्त्यक्तश्चाभ्युदयो मया ..
तस्माद्गत्वा सुराः सर्वे तां वदंतु कृते मम .. 71 ..
5.134.m: The sun said: / "By the command of the devoted wife, my rising was abandoned by me. / Therefore, O gods, go all of you and speak to her on my behalf,

5.134.s:
yena tadvākyamāsādya pravarttāmi yathāsukham ..
anyathā māṃ śapetkruddhā nūnaṃ sā hi pativratā .. 72 ..
5.134.d:
येन तद्वाक्यमासाद्य प्रवर्त्तामि यथासुखम् ..
अन्यथा मां शपेत्क्रुद्धा नूनं सा हि पतिव्रता .. 72 ..
5.134.m: so that, obtaining her permission, I may proceed as I please; / otherwise, enraged, that devoted wife would surely curse me!

5.134.s:
evaṃ sā tapasā yuktā protkṛṣṭaṃ hi surottamāḥ ..
pativratātvamādhatte tathānyadaparaṃ mahat .. 73 ..
5.134.d:
एवं सा तपसा युक्ता प्रोत्कृष्टं हि सुरोत्तमाः ..
पतिव्रतात्वमाधत्ते तथान्यदपरं महत् .. 73 ..
5.134.m: Endowed with such austerity, O best of gods, / she possesses exalted devotion to her husband, as well as another great [power].

5.134.s:
kastasyā vacanaṃ śaktaḥ kartumevamato'nyathā ..
etasmātkāraṇādbhīto nodgacchāmi kathaṃcana.. 74 ..
5.134.d:
कस्तस्या वचनं शक्तः कर्तुमेवमतोऽन्यथा ..
एतस्मात्कारणाद्भीतो नोद्गच्छामि कथंचन.. 74 ..
5.134.m: Who is able to act contrary to her word? / Afraid for this reason, I do not rise by any means.

5.134.s:
na tatkratusahasreṇa yajaṃtaḥ prāpnuyuḥ phalam ..
pativratātvamāpannā yatstrī viṃdati kevalam .. 79 ..
tataste vibudhāḥ sarve gatvā tatkṣetramuttamam ..
procustāṃ dīrghikāṃ vākyairmṛdubhiḥ purataḥ sthitāḥ .. 76 ..
tvayā pativrate sūryo yanniṣiddho na tatkṛtam ..
śubhaṃ yato hatāḥ sarvā bhūtale śobhanāḥ kriyāḥ ..77..
tasmādudgacchatu prājñe tvadvākyāttīkṣṇadīdhitiḥ ..
yajñakriyā viśeṣeṇa yena vartaṃti bhūtale .. 78 ..
.. pativratovāca ..
ayaṃ ca me patiḥ sadyaḥ prāṇebhyo'pi ca yaḥ priyaḥ ..
so'bhyeti nidhanaṃ devāḥ prodgate ravimaṃḍale .. 79 ..
5.134.d:
न तत्क्रतुसहस्रेण यजंतः प्राप्नुयुः फलम् ..
पतिव्रतात्वमापन्ना यत्स्त्री विंदति केवलम् .. 79 ..
ततस्ते विबुधाः सर्वे गत्वा तत्क्षेत्रमुत्तमम् ..
प्रोचुस्तां दीर्घिकां वाक्यैर्मृदुभिः पुरतः स्थिताः .. 76 ..
त्वया पतिव्रते सूर्यो यन्निषिद्धो न तत्कृतम् ..
शुभं यतो हताः सर्वा भूतले शोभनाः क्रियाः ..77..
तस्मादुद्गच्छतु प्राज्ञे त्वद्वाक्यात्तीक्ष्णदीधितिः ..
यज्ञक्रिया विशेषेण येन वर्तंति भूतले .. 78 ..
.. पतिव्रतोवाच ..
अयं च मे पतिः सद्यः प्राणेभ्योऽपि च यः प्रियः ..
सोऽभ्येति निधनं देवाः प्रोद्गते रविमंडले .. 79 ..
5.134.m:
Those who sacrifice with a thousand rituals cannot attain that fruit / which a woman who has attained devotion to her husband obtains alone."
Then all those gods, having gone to that excellent sacred field, / stood before that tall woman and spoke to her with gentle words:
"O devoted wife, that the sun was forbidden by you was not well done, / since all auspicious rites on the earth's surface have been destroyed.
Therefore, O wise woman, let the hot-rayed [sun] rise at your word, / so that sacrificial rites in particular may proceed on the earth's surface."
The devoted wife said: / "And this husband of mine, who is dearer to me even than life— / he will meet his death, O gods, as soon as the solar orb has risen!

5.134.s:
śaptaścānena duṣṭena māṃḍavyena supāpmanā ..
kāryaṃ vināpi nirdiṣṭastadbrūyāṃ bhāskaraṃ katham .. 6.135.80 ..
5.134.d:
शप्तश्चानेन दुष्टेन मांडव्येन सुपाप्मना ..
कार्यं विनापि निर्दिष्टस्तद्ब्रूयां भास्करं कथम् .. 6.135.80 ..
5.134.m: He was cursed by that wicked, exceedingly sinful Māṇḍavya, / ordained [to die] without even any fault. How, then, could I tell the sun [to rise]?

5.134.s:
udayārthaṃ na me yajñaiḥ kāryaṃ kiṃcinna cāparaiḥ ..
śrāddhadānādikaiḥ kṛtyaiḥ saṃjātairdaryitaṃ vinā .. 81 ..
5.134.d:
उदयार्थं न मे यज्ञैः कार्यं किंचिन्न चापरैः ..
श्राद्धदानादिकैः कृत्यैः संजातैर्दर्यितं विना .. 81 ..
5.134.m: I have no need of sacrifices for the sake of the sunrise, nor of anything else— / of duties such as ancestral rites and gifts performed without my beloved."

5.134.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tataste vibudhāḥ sarve samālokya parasparam ..
cirakālaṃ suduḥkhārtāstāmūcurvinayānvitāḥ .. 82 ..
5.134.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
ततस्ते विबुधाः सर्वे समालोक्य परस्परम् ..
चिरकालं सुदुःखार्तास्तामूचुर्विनयान्विताः .. 82 ..
5.134.m: Sūta said: / Then all those gods, looking at one another, / afflicted with great sorrow for a long time, spoke to her with humility:

5.134.s:
udgacchatu ravirbhadre tavāyaṃ dayitaḥ patiḥ ..
prayātu nidhanaṃ sadyo bhūyādeṣa munīśvaraḥ .. 83 ..
5.134.d:
उद्गच्छतु रविर्भद्रे तवायं दयितः पतिः ..
प्रयातु निधनं सद्यो भूयादेष मुनीश्वरः .. 83 ..
5.134.m: "O auspicious one, let the sun rise; [though] this dear husband of yours / may meet death immediately, let this lord of sages [nevertheless continue].

5.134.s:
punarjīvāpayiṣyāmo vayamenamapi drutam ..
mṛtyumārgamanuprāptaṃ tvatkṛte pativatsale .. 84 ..
5.134.d:
पुनर्जीवापयिष्यामो वयमेनमपि द्रुतम् ..
मृत्युमार्गमनुप्राप्तं त्वत्कृते पतिवत्सले .. 84 ..
5.134.m: We shall bring him back to life again quickly, / even though he has reached the path of death, for your sake, O lover of your husband!

5.134.s:
pañcaviṃśativarṣīyaṃ kāmadevamivāparam ..
tvaṃ drakṣyasi sudīptāṃgaṃ sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitam .. 85 ..
5.134.d:
पञ्चविंशतिवर्षीयं कामदेवमिवापरम् ..
त्वं द्रक्ष्यसि सुदीप्तांगं सर्वलक्षणलक्षितम् .. 85 ..
5.134.m: You shall see him twenty-five years of age, like another Kāmadeva, / his limbs blazing with radiance, endowed with all auspicious marks.

5.134.s:
bhūtvā paṃcadaśābdīyā padmapatrāyatekṣaṇā ..
martyaloke sukhaṃ samyaktvecchayā sādhayiṣyasi .. 86 ..
5.134.d:
भूत्वा पंचदशाब्दीया पद्मपत्रायतेक्षणा ..
मर्त्यलोके सुखं सम्यक्त्वेच्छया साधयिष्यसि .. 86 ..
5.134.m: Becoming fifteen years of age, your eyes long like lotus petals, / you shall fully attain happiness in the mortal world according to your desire.

5.134.s:
eṣo'pi muniśārdūlo vipāpmā sāṃprataṃ śubhe ..
śūlavedhena nirmuktaḥ sukhabhāgī bhavatklama.. .. 87 ..
5.134.d:
एषोऽपि मुनिशार्दूलो विपाप्मा सांप्रतं शुभे ..
शूलवेधेन निर्मुक्तः सुखभागी भवत्क्लम.. .. 87 ..
5.134.m: This tiger among sages too, freed from sin now, O auspicious one, / released from impalement upon the stake, shall share in happiness without distress."

5.134.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
bāḍhamityeva ca prokte tayā sa dvijasattamāḥ ..
udgato bhagavānsūryastatkṣaṇādeva vegataḥ .. 88 ..
5.134.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
बाढमित्येव च प्रोक्ते तया स द्विजसत्तमाः ..
उद्गतो भगवान्सूर्यस्तत्क्षणादेव वेगतः .. 88 ..
5.134.m: Sūta said: / When she had said 'So be it,' O best of the twice-born, / the blessed sun rose with speed at that very moment.

5.134.s:
tataḥ sūryāṃśusaṃspṛṣṭaḥ sa mṛtaśca sukuṣṭhabhāk ..
vibudhānāṃ karaiḥ spṛṣṭaḥ punareva samutthitaḥ .. 89 ..
5.134.d:
ततः सूर्यांशुसंस्पृष्टः स मृतश्च सुकुष्ठभाक् ..
विबुधानां करैः स्पृष्टः पुनरेव समुत्थितः .. 89 ..
5.134.m: Then, touched by the sun's rays, the leper died; / but touched by the hands of the gods, he rose up once again,

5.134.s:
paṃcaviṃśativarṣīyaḥ kāmadeva ivāparaḥ ..
saṃsmaranpūrvikāṃ jātiṃ sarvā harṣa samanvitaḥ .. 6.135.90 ..
5.134.d:
पंचविंशतिवर्षीयः कामदेव इवापरः ..
संस्मरन्पूर्विकां जातिं सर्वा हर्ष समन्वितः .. 6.135.90 ..
5.134.m: twenty-five years of age, like another Kāmadeva, / remembering all of his previous birth, filled with joy.

5.134.s:
dīrghikāpi parispṛṣṭā svayaṃ devena śaṃbhunā .
saṃjātā yauvanopetā divyalakṣaṇalakṣitā .. 91 ..
5.134.d:
दीर्घिकापि परिस्पृष्टा स्वयं देवेन शंभुना .
संजाता यौवनोपेता दिव्यलक्षणलक्षिता .. 91 ..
5.134.m: The tall woman too, touched personally by the god Śambhu, / became endowed with youth, marked with divine characteristics,

5.134.s:
padmapatrekṣaṇā ramyā candrabimbasamānanā ..
madhye kṣāmā sugaurāṃgī pīnonnatapayodharā .. 92 ..
5.134.d:
पद्मपत्रेक्षणा रम्या चन्द्रबिम्बसमानना ..
मध्ये क्षामा सुगौरांगी पीनोन्नतपयोधरा .. 92 ..
5.134.m: having eyes like lotus petals, beautiful, with a face like the orb of the moon, / slender at the waist, very fair of limb, with full, elevated breasts.

5.134.s:
tatastaṃ muniśārdūlaṃ śūlāgrādavatārya ca ..
procuśca vibudhaśreṣṭhāḥ sādaraṃ harṣasaṃyutāḥ ..93..
5.134.d:
ततस्तं मुनिशार्दूलं शूलाग्रादवतार्य च ..
प्रोचुश्च विबुधश्रेष्ठाः सादरं हर्षसंयुताः ..93..
5.134.m: Then, bringing that tiger among sages down from the tip of the stake, / the best of the gods spoke to him respectfully, filled with joy:

5.134.s:
etatsatyaṃ kṛtaṃ vākyaṃ mune tava yathoditam..
mṛto'pi brāhmaṇaḥ kuṣṭhī saṃspṛṣṭo raviraśmibhiḥ..94..
5.134.d:
एतत्सत्यं कृतं वाक्यं मुने तव यथोदितम्..
मृतोऽपि ब्राह्मणः कुष्ठी संस्पृष्टो रविरश्मिभिः..94..
5.134.m: "This word of yours, O sage, has been made true as it was spoken: / the leprous brahmin died as soon as he was touched by the rays of the sun;

5.134.s:
punarutthāpito'smābhiḥ kṛtaśca taruṇaḥ punaḥ..
anayā bhāryayā sārdhaṃ tasmāttvaṃ svāśramaṃ vraja ..95..
5.134.d:
पुनरुत्थापितोऽस्माभिः कृतश्च तरुणः पुनः..
अनया भार्यया सार्धं तस्मात्त्वं स्वाश्रमं व्रज ..95..
5.134.m: he has been raised up again by us and made youthful once more. / Therefore, go to your own hermitage together with this wife [of his].

5.134.s:
nāsmākaṃ darśanaṃ vyarthaṃ kathaṃcidapi jāyate ..
tasmātprārthaya yaccitte tava nityaṃ samāśritam ..96..
5.134.d:
नास्माकं दर्शनं व्यर्थं कथंचिदपि जायते ..
तस्मात्प्रार्थय यच्चित्ते तव नित्यं समाश्रितम् ..96..
5.134.m: Our darśana is never in vain under any circumstance; / therefore, ask for whatever is constantly lodged in your heart."

5.134.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye pativratāvaralābhonāma pañcatriṃśaduttaraśatata mo'dhyāyaḥ .. 135 .. .. cha .. ..
5.134.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये पतिव्रतावरलाभोनाम पञ्चत्रिंशदुत्तरशतत मोऽध्यायः .. 135 .. .. छ .. ..
5.134.m: Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-fifth chapter, named 'The Attainment of the Boon by the Devoted Wife,' in the māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara sacred field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the eighty-one-thousand-verse collection of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa.
